US.name: United States of America
US.key_meta: Yellow triangular signs with the text "No Passing Zone" are unique to the United States.

metas.title: No passing zone sign
metas.description: Yellow triangular signs with the text "No Passing Zone" are unique to the United States.

metas.title: Speed limit signs
metas.description: U.S. speed limit signs feature the text "Speed Limit," while Canadian signs use the text "Maximum."

metas.title: Alaskan highway shield
metas.description: The Alaskan highway shield has an image of the Big Dipper constellation on the bottom left.

metas.title: Corn fields
metas.description: Corn fields can most commonly be found in these regions. For a detailed overview, see this map.

metas.title: Stilt Houses
metas.description: Stilt houses can sometimes be seen on the coast. These are especially common toward the south, and on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.

metas.title: Eastern white pine
metas.description: The Eastern white pine (Pinus strobus) is a large pine native to eastern North America. It can be found in the Great Lakes region and in the Appalachian Mountains.
metas.comparison: Image source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/nrs/atlas/tree/v3/129

metas.title: Sagebrush
metas.description: Great Basin Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata) is a short, shrubby blue-green bush that is common in the interior western United States.It is most common in arid areas.

metas.title: H-Reflector
metas.description: Snowplowable raised pavement markers can only be found on highways in the eastern states shown in the image. They are built into the road and somewhat resemble the letter H.

metas.title: Dormant Grass
metas.description: Grass that is used in lawns in the southern US (colloquially known as Bermuda and St. Augustine grasses) go dormant in the winter months. This causes the lawns to turn beige or light brown in winter; whereas grasses used in more northern areas of the US stay much greener in winter.

metas.title: Short Stilts
metas.description: Similar in style to aforementioned stilt houses, houses with much shorter stilts are common in the western and central Gulf Coast. These houses typically feature short stilts made of concrete or wood (1-3 feet off the ground) and are primarily found in areas near the coast and any adjacent rivers.

metas.title: Southern Pines
metas.description: The loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), and longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), commonly referred to as southern pines in the community, are found throughout the southeastern US. They are a great way to recognize this region, as they are abundant, recognizable and mostly limited to this part of the country. They tend to be tall, with fluffy-looking clusters of pine needles.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Pittsburgh Reflectors
metas.description: These circular reflectors are found in Pittsburgh.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Nashville Bins
metas.description: Nashville has trash bins with the recognizable logo.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - New Hampshire
metas.description: Number in a white rectangle with a thick colorful border.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - New Hampshire (old)
metas.description: They look like colorful post-its with a black number on it.

metas.title: Car Meta - Santa Catalina Car
metas.description: This island to the south of Los Angeles has a unique Google car.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Texas
metas.description: MMYY (for example 1022) in a white rectangle with a colorful border.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Orange T Circle
metas.description: This windshield sticker with an orange T is found exclusively in Dallas.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - New York
metas.description: One number on the left, one on the right with a long white gap in between.

metas.title: Infrastructure - North Carolina / Blue Parking Sign
metas.description: Charlotte uses green parking signs, whereas Raleigh uses blue parking signs.

metas.title: Car Meta - Golden Gate Car
metas.description: This car can be found to the north of the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - DC
metas.description: Cars registered in DC are legally required to have this sticker in their windshield.

metas.title: Architecture - North-Eastern House
metas.description: Houses in North-Eastern USA often have walls made up of horizontal, overlapping boards

metas.title: Infrastructure - New Hampshire Interstate Sign
metas.description: These signs should only be found in NH (notice the dividing line between the two numbers).

metas.title: Infrastructure - Roadname on Sidewalk
metas.description: In San Francisco, CA, almost every intersection has the road name written on the sidewalk.
metas.comparison: This is due to the many earthquakes in this city, making sure every road is still labeled in case the streetsigns fall off.

metas.title: Architecture - Art Deco Architecture
metas.description: Art Deco is a very distinctive architectural style that is found predominantly in Miami, FL.
metas.comparison: There are many features that make it distinct (picture), and a good way to remember them is that they're inspired by ships, for example the Strong central vertical element, which gives the building an appearance like looking straight at a ship. Or round port hole windows, resembling ship windows. Another distinctive feature is the so-called eyebrows above the windows which have a practical use, which is blocking the strong Miami sunlight from shining into the building and heating it up.

metas.title: Infrastructure - County Road - Clark County
metas.description: Clark County is the county Las Vegas is situated in and it uses a unique county route shield.

metas.title: Landscape - Mid-Atlantic Agricultural
metas.description: Some locations in the Mid-Atlantic region can look deceivingly Midwestern but with more trees.

metas.title: Car Meta - Daniel Boone Car
metas.description: This section of road in Daniel Boone National Forest near Beattyville, KY has a unique Google car.
metas.comparison: Note by MB: This coverage is overwritten afaik.

metas.title: Infrastructure - North Carolina - Circular Pay to Park
metas.description: Raleigh, NC uses circular pay to park signs to indicate parking meter locations. (unlike Charlotte, NC)

metas.title: Infrastructure - License Plate - Florida
metas.description: Each state in the United States has one or more unique license plate designs. See picture for reference.

metas.title: Architecture - New Orleans Architecture
metas.description: Neighbourhoods all around the city of New Orleans feature many colourful, historic, shotgun-style houses.
metas.comparison: Buildings in central areas of New Orleans often feature colourful facades with second story wrap-around balconies.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Red Streetsign
metas.description: Mesa, a city next to Phoenix, sometimes uses these red street name signs in the western part of the city.

metas.title: Infrastructure - State Flag - Arizona
metas.description: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - Massachusetts
metas.description: Three white rectangles. Central one is horizontal, and has a number on it. Left and right one are vertical.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Nevada Mile Marker
metas.description: Top part has the highway name. The middle part is an abbreviation of the county name. The lower part has the mile number.

metas.title: Vegetation - California Fan Palm
metas.description: Washingtonia filifera is the only palm native to the Western United States and one of the country's largest native palms.

metas.title: Trekker - Dry Tortugas
metas.description: The main island of Dry Tortugas National Park, west of Key West, can be identified by the hexagonal brick structure and the surrounding moat.
metas.comparison: The Loggerhead Lighthouse, situated on the Loggerhead Key, has a brown top-half and a white bottom. The path on which the trekker walks on is also made of bright concrete, and many palm trees can be seen around the lighthouse.

metas.title: Architecture - Miami Modern Architecture
metas.description: Miami Modern Architecture is characterized by "fun", unconventional designs, decorative elements, smooth corners, flat roofs and lots of glass.
metas.comparison: It is find in certain districts of Miami and Miami Beach.

metas.title: Landscape - Southern California - Urban
metas.description: In general Los Angeles and San Diego feel more tropical and the houses are more spread out as opposed to the more compact and dense feel of San Francisco.

metas.title: Landscape - Badlands
metas.description: Badlands National Park features these distinct, sand-brown, eroded rock formations. The formations may sometimes appear more rounded, and lighter in colour.

metas.title: Architecture - Brick
metas.description: Brick buildings are more common in the Mid-Atlantic states than in other parts of the country. The area around Philadelphia especially has many brick buildings.

metas.title: Landscape - Northern California
metas.description: One thing that sets NoCal apart from SoCal is the amount of palm trees. You generally see palms everywhere in the LA area but hardly any in the San Francisco Bay Area.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Windshield Sticker - New Jersey
metas.description: Three rectangles. Each contains a number. The outer ones make a year (like 2023), and are filled in a given color. The central one has a white background and a single digit.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Trolley - Miami Beach
metas.description:
The Greater Miami area has a so-called trolley system which is a free public transport system.
Different towns have different colors in their trolleys. The Miami Beach Trolley is blue.

metas.title: Architecture - Wooden House
metas.description: Houses and commercial buildings in the interior Western US are often made of lots of dark wooden boards and timbers. Buildings at high elevations also commonly have metal roofs, to avoid snow build-up.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Zoox
metas.description: Zoox is a robotaxi service that as of Dec 18th, 2025, operates in San Francisco and Las Vegas. The cars have a very distinct shape and have no driver. You can find the current coverage area of Zoox here

metas.title: Infrastructure - Adopt-A-Highway Signs
metas.description: Most states have unique, distinct and learnable Adopt-a-Highway signs, which can be seen on the side of roads. A map of those can be seen here. Keep in mind, some states have slight variations in design.

metas.title: Landscape - Death Valley
metas.description: Death Valley National Park can be easily recognized by the dry, sandy, treeless mountains that can be seen from the roads that go through the park. In Generation 3 coverage, the sky can look particularly dusty.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Many smaller roads in Death Valley only have Generation 1 coverage.

metas.title: Trekker - Disney World Trekker
metas.description: GeoGuessr’s official maps have a bias for trekkers. Thus, if you’re playing the official US map or official state streaks, you should be aware of there being a lot of trekker coverage in Disney World in Orlando.

metas.title: Architecture - Victorian Architecture
metas.description: Row Houses and other buildings in San Francisco are often in the style of Victorian architecture, with many bay windows, turrets, and ornate exterior details. These homes are built close together and can be very colourful.

metas.title: Architecture - Short Stilt House
metas.description: Houses with short stilts are common in the western and central Gulf Coast. These houses typically feature short stilts made of concrete or wood (30cm-90cm off the ground) and are primarily found in areas near the coast and any adjacent rivers.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Highway Signs
metas.description: Maximum speed limits vary by state and territory. The maximum speed limits shown here will generally be seen on interstate highways. Some interstates and highways in their respective states or territories will have lower maximum speed limits than what is shown.

metas.title: Infrastructure - National Parks
metas.description: Guardrails, signs, and signposts are commonly painted a medium brown colour in US National Parks, which are often located in the west. Guardrails that are painted brown can be made out of both wood and metal. Rock walls can also sometimes be seen in place of guardrails.
metas.comparison: NOTE: There are occasional exceptions to this rule, so consider other clues before guessing in a National Park.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Waymo
metas.description: Waymo is an autonomous driving company which offers taxi services in several cities. Its cars are very distinct, have a lidar on top and notably have no person sitting behind the wheel. As of Dec 18th, 2025, it operates in San Francisco (CA), Los Angeles (CA), Phoenix (AZ), Austin (TX) and Atlanta (GA). You can find the current operation here

general_rules.text: State highways are grouped by their first digit, with 1 and 2 found on Hawaiʻi, 3 on Maui, 4 on Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi, 5 on Kauaʻi and 6 to 9 on Oʻahu. Moreover, all four of the so-called interstate highways are located on Oʻahu.

The Island of Oʻahu lies southeast of Kauaʻi. It is known for being home to the Honolulu urban area. It also is home to steep, lush hills, which can be commonly seen from all around the island, especially in Honolulu’s suburbs.

The US, as well as most of the Americas, uses short licence plates, in contrast to longer European ones. Each US state has their own unique licence plate design. Some of these are recognizable through the blur, and are thus worth learning. Around half of the states also do not require front plates, which can also be useful in determining the state. You can click on the image to enlarge it. Here you can also find a map showing the locations of each plate.
US telephone numbers start with a three-digit area code. While these area codes are not clustered by initial digits, they are useful to learn. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Vermont features small rectangular green signs on stop sign posts with three rows of horizontal numbers. The top row of numbers correlates to the highway or road number that the road with the stop sign intersects with. For example, this image is taken from Vermont State Road 116, looking towards the intersecting road. The State of New York uses similar style signs. However, these signs can be attached to different types of sign posts (town entry signs, highway signs, etc.)

California.text: Utility poles with 3 yellow stripes are most commonly found in California.
A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.
Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.

Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road.

NOTE: This can rarely be seen in other states, notably Kentucky

Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here.

In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.

Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana.

Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.

This bollard is extremely common in Oregon and is almost exclusive to this state. It can rarely be seen in California (but usually when it is the case, it is not exactly this bollard, the white rectangle will be bigger or it won’t be all the way on top for example).

Spanish Colonial Revival Architecture can be categorised as buildings with lightly-coloured stucco walls and red clay-tile roofs. They can be found in the desert southwest states of California, Nevada, Arizona, and Texas. You can also find similar types of buildings in Florida and coastal Georgia.
Wooden Signposts are mainly found in the Northwestern 5 States, and in California
Southern California outside the major cities of Los Angeles and San Diego is a barren desert.
Instead of Mile Markers, California uses postal markers that are white instead of green and have a county abbreviation.
‘In-N-Out Burger’ is a regional fast food chain located primarily in the Southwest US. California has the most locations.

Aldi is found in the eastern half, starting at ~Mid Texas. It is however not found in Maine.
In the West, it's only found in California and around Phoenix, Arizona.
California posts these bridge markers (with a lot of numbers) on bridges. The county abbreviations used on the bridge markers are different from those on the postal markers.

This bollard has a white rectangular plate, with 6 bolts: 2 at the top, 2 in the middle and 2 at the bottom.
There are different variants, with circular reflectors, rectangular reflectors, or no reflectors at all.

They're all found in California

Palm trees are common in coastal areas of the Southeastern states, as well as the Desert Southwest region. Shown here is the Mexican Fan Palm, which is most common in California and along the Gulf Coast, but other palm tree types have a similar range.

Shown here is a topographic map of the US. Most significant elevation is in the west: here you will find large mountain ranges, but also more flat, high plateaus. Some parts have lower elevation: good examples are the Central Valley and Imperial Valley in California. Elevation in the east is generally much lower. The most significant amount of elevation is found in the Appalachians, low mountain ranges running through the eastern and northeastern US. Good examples of hills in otherwise fairly flat regions are the Driftless Area in the Midwest, and The Ozarks in Missouri and Arkansas. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

The Great Basin, centred around Nevada, can be recognized by the tall, sometimes snow-capped mountains in the background. There are dry, but grassy, and slightly shrubby plains leading up to the mountains. The tallest mountains are in Nevada, Utah and California. More gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon, and greener mountains can be seen in Idaho and central Utah. Keep in mind that there are exceptions, so make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana. Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.

Palm trees are common in coastal areas of the Southeastern states, as well as the Desert Southwest region. Shown here is the Mexican Fan Palm, which is most common in California and along the Gulf Coast, but other palm tree types have a similar range.

Central Valley, California can be recognized by its Mediterranean climate. This is reflected in its agriculture, seen in the vineyards and olive trees that can commonly be found here. In addition, rolling hills can be seen toward the edges of the valley.
A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.
Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.
Some small roads in California lack a middle yellow line; instead only feature solid white lines on each side of the road. NOTE: This can rarely be seen in other states.

Alaska.text: There are three variants of Alaska license plates.
Trees in Alaska are generally thinner and have less broad leaves than those seen in the other 49 states.
Generation 4 coverage in Alaska is concentrated around the city of Anchorage.
Most of interior and northern Alaska lies in subarctic or tundra climate zones. These areas feature relatively low amounts of forest undergrowth and shorter trees.
The only two major urban areas in Alaska are Anchorage and Fairbanks.

Most of the suburban areas in Alaska are in and around Anchorage.These areas feature wide roads, commercial districts, and sometimes heavy traffic. Mountains can commonly be seen in the distance. NOTE: Fairbanks has some similar areas, but mountains are less prevalent.
Aspen trees (Populus tremuloides) can be found in lower elevation areas of interior and south-central regions of Alaska. These trees have white bark and rounded leaves.
Due to Alaska’s very cold climate; agricultural fields are mainly found in the south of the state, mostly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.
The Alaskan pipeline which is usually visible from main roads, can be seen at these points. This is an easy way to identify Alaska as there are no similar pipelines in the rest of the US.

Wisconsin.text: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.
These simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.
A rectangular white metal plate, with an orange rectangle and diamond, can be seen on most poles in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula.

A horizontal blue, red, or green sign can commonly be seen at the ends of driveways in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula. The house number is present, in addition to either the town name and or the road name (usually.)

NOTE: Nearby states often use similar markers, but typically lack any town or street name information and only feature numbers.

Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word ‘county’ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.
‘Hy-Vee’ is a supermarket that is common primarily in the Upper Midwest states of Iowa, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Illinois.
‘Kwik Trip’ is a chain of gas stations and convenience stores that are located in the Upper Midwest states of Wisconsin and Minnesota.
‘Stop-N-Go’ is a chain of gas stations and convenience stores that are located in the Upper Midwest states of Iowa, Wisconsin and Minnesota.
The driftless area in Southwestern Wisconsin is quite unique. It has features of Midwestern States (for example agriculture), but is very hilly.

Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word ‘county’ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.
These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.
A rectangular white metal plate, with an orange rectangle and diamond, can be seen on most poles in Wisconsin and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan.
These simple white bollards with black reflectors are unique to Wisconsin.

A horizontal blue, red, or green sign can commonly be seen at the ends of driveways in Wisconsin and the Michigan peninsula. The house number is present, in addition to either the town name and or the road name (usually.) NOTE: Nearby states often use similar markers, but typically lack any town or street name information and only feature numbers.

Nebraska.text:
Corn fields can most commonly be found in these regions:-Iowa

-North of Iowa -Nebraska without NW
The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

You may have noticed some difference between farmland in different states on satellite view… It can be difficult to tell the farmland apart unless you’re at a corner up close, but as it turns out, the circles are actually created by a giant machine you can see from a distance

This is called centre point irrigation and can be found in many regions in the country!! The most common states are Idaho, Nebraska and Kansas
The Nebraska Sandhills are a recognizable region of rolling hills covered with prairie grass in the central-north part of the state.

Hawaii.text:
Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas.

NOTE: Similar reflectors can sometimes be seen in other states, such as Hawaii.

A stubby antenna can be seen in most Generation 3 coverage on Hawaii.

NOTE: The antenna is not always visible, so make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
(This antenna can also be seen in Cambodia, New Zealand, and US National Parks)
Hawaii license plates has black text on a white background. It also has a rainbow in the background that is somtimes more or less visible. Front plates are required.

Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used. Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.

Hawaiian is a vowel-oriented language that only uses eight consonants: H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and (ʻ), called an ʻOkina. Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U. Each vowel can also have a macron over it: Ā, Ē, Ī, Ō, and Ū. These vowels are often combined to make Diphthongs. I.e. UI, AI, AE, etc...

Topography on Hawaii is characterised by many sloping volcanoes, rugged cliffs, hills, valleys and craters. Such distinct topography combined with tropical vegetation is a good way to identify Hawaii.

Hawaii also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front, with parts of the black car being visible. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.
On the three largest islands, namely Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu, smallcam coverage was taken with a black Google car.
Smallcam imagery on the islands of Kauaʻi, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi was captured by a white car. Just like with the black car, you will often be able to see the unblurred hood and mirrors.
Generation 2 and non-smallcam Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the islands of Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu. The other islands only have Generation 3 or smallcam coverage.

The Island of Kauaʻi is the furthest west island in Hawaii with official Google coverage. This island has deep red soil and has large rugged hills with lush, jungle-like vegetation. NOTE: Other islands such as Maui and Molokaʻi have similar soil colours, but the hillsides on them will typically have less dense vegetation.
Honolulu, located on southern Oʻahu, is by far the largest city and urban area in Hawaii. If you are in a dense urban area and can see tall buildings, you will always be in or near Honolulu.

The Island of Molokaʻi is just southeast of Oʻahu. It features deep red soil and a prominent volcano on the eastern end of the island. Especially in the older Generation 3 coverage, the vegetation appears very dry. Molokaʻi is also very sparsely populated.

The Island of Lānaʻi is a small, yet distinct island that lies just south of Moloka’i. A volcano is found just east of the centre of the island, adjacent to the town of Lānaʻi. In this area, tall Cook pines are abundant. In addition, some main roads near the centre of the island are lined with younger Cook pines.
Towards the coasts of the island of Lānaʻi, hills dotted with dry grass and shrubby vegetation are commonly seen. These areas are very rural with few buildings.
The Island of Maui sits southeast of Molokaʻi. In the centre of the island, you will find dry and somewhat flat grasslands with one or both of the mountain ranges on the island visible.
Coastal areas of Maui are noticeably more lush and green. Banana plants, palm trees, and views of the mountains are all common.

The Island of Hawai’i (also referred to as The Big Island) is both the largest and farthest southeast island with Street View coverage in the state. The interior areas feature rolling, grassy plains and volcanic rocks. You can typically see one or more of the island’s volcanoes from the road.

The coastal areas of the island of Hawai’i are where most of the towns and built-up areas on the island are located. These areas are typically more lush and have more trees and fern plants than the interior.

Rural roads going through forests within a flat landscape are commonly found south of the city of Hilo, on the island of Hawaiʻi. NOTE: Mountainous forests are dotted around Hawaii, but if you are in one, and you see red soil with Generation 3, consider guessing in Kauaʻi, the westernmost covered island.
Within Hawaii, a distinct green blur can only be seen on the island of Oʻahu.
Yellow or red bands can commonly be seen around signposts in Texas. NOTE: Similar reflectors can sometimes be seen in other states, such as Hawaii.

New Mexico.text:
Texan roads often have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface.

NOTE: Similar pavement can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.
New Mexico license plates has red text on yellow background or yellow text on green background, it shows up as a mostly yellow or green blur, and is easy to spot. Front plates are NOT required.

Pueblo Revival style houses are commonly seen in New Mexico. They are typically constructed of adobe or brick and concrete. They have rounded edges and flat roofs, and are usually sand-brown in colour.

NOTE: Pueblo style houses can also be seen in Arizona and Colorado to a lesser extent.

The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.
In adjacent areas of New Mexico and Texas, smaller foothills of the Guadaloupe Mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.
Spruce and pine forests are a common sight in the western United States in New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, and to the west of those states.
Horizontal Traffic Lights are common in Nebraska, New Mexico, Texas and Louisiana. They also appear occasionally in Oklahoma, Louisiana and Georgia.
Navajo is spoken in the Navajo Nation in Arizona and New Mexico. It’s the largest Native American language by the number of speakers. Navajo can be recognized from the double vowels and diacritics.

Spanish is the most commonly spoken non-English language in the United States. It’s the most prevalent near Mexico in Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, and California and in Florida where it’s the most spoken language in Miami-Dade County.

Along the New Mexico and or Texas border there is a ridge of tall, dry peaks known as the Guadalupe Mountains. In adjacent areas of both states, smaller foothills of these mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.

Shiprock is a rock formation and a municipality in northwestern New Mexico. This striking, isolated mountain is visible from distances of up to 40 km (roughly the red square) and is therefore a good clue for identifying the region within the Navajo Nation. Similar rock formations can be seen around Shiprock, but they do not have a long, low stone wall next to them.
Texan roads often have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface. NOTE: Similar pavement can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.

Washington.text:
Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington.

NOTE: Flat areas of northern and eastern Oregon can have a similar appearance.

Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns.

NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.
The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

These short and fine lines can often be seen in between Oregon roadlines which are usually wide, you can see similar lines elsewhere but it is useful to distinguish Oregon from surrounding states especially Washington who also often uses wide roadlines.

The Alaskan towns in the Alexander Archipelago, on the British Columbia border have a unique look. Tall mountains with lush green forests can be seen in the background, with the majority of buildings made of wood. In addition, Generation 2 coverage is often overcast and misty. NOTE: Coastal areas of Oregon and Washington can have a similar appearance in terms of landscape and foliage.

Temperate rainforests are found in coastal areas of Washington, Oregon, and Northern California. These rainforests feature many broadleaf trees, large conifers, and ferns. NOTE: These rainforests stretch north into coastal British Columbia and Southeast Alaska as well.
Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington. NOTE: Flat areas of northern and eastern Oregon can have a similar appearance.
The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.

Oregon.text: Within the Great Basin, more gradual, rocky hills can be seen in Oregon.
Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word ‘Speed’ instead of the standard ‘Speed Limit’.
Oregon license plates has blue text on white background with a green tree in the middle, it shows up as a green dot in the white/blue blur on the sides. Front plates are required.
Speed signs in Oregon often simply have the word ‘Speed’ instead of the standard ‘Speed Limit’.

North Carolina.text: White signs attached to signposts can commonly be seen in North Carolina.

North Carolina commonly uses a style of street signs showing street numbers and arrows in addition to the street name.

NOTE: Other states occasionally feature street signs with similar designs, so use other clues before guessing.
This tree can only be found in the South. However, southern magnolias don’t grow in southern Florida. The range stretches from Orlando and Tampa to North Carolina and Texas.

Cars without Front Plates are mostly found south of the linie north of Arizona to North Carolina (except for Texas), Ohio and it's neighboring states + Delaware and Oklahoma.

In the picture, the yellow states do not require front license plates, the purple and blue states generally do. Keep in mind that cars travel, and not all people follow the law, so use with caution.
The Cherokee language is concentrated in the Cherokee Nation of Oklahoma and a few areas of North Carolina. It has a distinctive writing system called the Cherokee syllabary.
Sabal palmetto is native to the subtropical coastal regions of the American states of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, southeastern North Carolina, and extreme southern Texas.

Buildings with red metal rooftops are most commonly found in the Mid-South and Southern Appalachia states of Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, and North Carolina.

NOTE: These types of rooftops can be found in other areas, so use other clues before guessing.

As part of a promotional campaign, the TransAmerica Trail from Oregon to North Carolina was covered by a Ford Bronco. The car can recognised by its unblurred black roof and red hood, and is mostly found on unpaved rural roads.

Looking backwards, you will see two other Ford SUVs escorting the camera car.

You’ll find red soil everywhere in the South. The area where red soil can be found stretches all the way from some parts of Louisiana and Arkansas all the way to southern Virginia through Mississippi, southern Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina, and North Carolina.

The Oklahoma City region in Oklahoma is also notable for its red soil.

You may already know Ohio’s nickname, the Buckeye State, but despite the name, buckeyes grow in other states too. They’re most commonly seen in the east from Ohio down through West Virginia, Virginia, and Kentucky to Tennessee and North Carolina. Some can be found in Missouri too.

California is the only state in the west where you can see buckeyes.

North Carolina commonly uses a style of street signs showing street numbers and arrows in addition to the street name. NOTE: Other states occasionally feature street signs with similar designs, so use other clues before guessing.
White signs attached to signposts can commonly be seen in North Carolina.

Streets in Utah and Idaho, particularly in urban areas, are often named by using a combination of a number and cardinal direction (i.e. ‘600 South.’)

NOTE: This style of street naming can be found rarely in other Western states.

Aspen trees are thin trees with white barks that often grow in groups. In the contiguous states, you can find it in North-East USA, all states that border the great lakes (+NE-Iowa), in Northern Idaho and in random areas in the West.

Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.

Texas’s nickname is the Lone Star State. You can see the Texas star on the state’s flag. Many Texans use the star as a decoration on gates, for example.

Florida.text: Florida license plates has green text on a white background, and it has oranges in the middle, which makes the plate unique. Front plates are NOT required.
South Florida is marshy and tropical. You’ll see an abundance of palm trees here.
Small circular shallow lakes are especially common in Central Florida around Lakeland and Orlando.
The soil gets a little more sandy in Central Florida. There are also more pine trees than palms (they’re occasionally seen too).
North Florida has sandier soil and rarely has any palm trees. Most forests are pine forests and the vibes feel more like Florida’s neighbors to the north than Florida itself.

This tree can commonly be found in Florida and along the southern coast as shown by the range map. A southern live oak will often have Spanish moss hanging from the branches, giving the tree a pendulous appearance.

The Gumbo Limbo tree can be recognized by its red bark and by its irregular, sometimes twisting trunks. Its leaves are green and oval shaved. You will only find it in Coastal Florida, south of Orlando and south of Tampa.

The area between the cities of Orlando and Lakeland in Florida sometimes feature low, rolling hills. Lakes and agricultural fields are also common in this area. This is the only main hilly area in central or southern Florida.

The Florida Keys are an archipelago of tropical islands west of Miami. The highway connecting the islands can be recognized by green, tropical vegetation on the sides of the usually single lane road. The soil is also sandy white.

Urban locations are also similar, but with many more planted palm trees and mowed grass being a common sight.

Vermont.text: Vermont license plates has white text on green background, it shows up as a green blur with white on the sides, and is easy to spot. Front plates are required.

North Dakota.text: Along the Canadian border in North Dakota, and rarely Montana, fields filled with short yellow canola flowers (Brassica napus) can commonly be seen from the road.

Signs warning about ice (like this) are commonplace in Louisiana.

This sticker can be seen on windshields in Louisiana. The sticker has four smaller squares in it, hence the name.

Louisiana doesn’t call its counties counties but uses the word parish instead. This is a relic of the French colonial past of the state. You might occasionally spot the word on an intersection sign, for example. The location is guaranteed to be in Louisiana because no other state uses the word parish in that way.

These county routes are given unique three-digit numbers that begin with a 5. There is only one route per number. The same number cannot be duplicated in multiple counties. There is therefore only one County Route 525 in the entire state of New Jersey. What’s also interesting about the 500 Series routes is that they follow the same cardinal direction rule as Interstates: even-numbered routes run east-to-west and odd-numbered ones north-to-south. In common with the U.S. Routes, the numbers increase southward.

You can find same cactus in Mexico over the border in Sonora or similar one in north of Argentina.

New York.text:
Square guardrails are the most dominant (but not the only) type of guardrail in the states of New York and Wyoming. They have a long bar across the top, with several square legs supporting them.

NOTE: These guardrails can be found, to a lesser extent, in some adjacent states.

Vermont features small rectangular green signs on stop sign posts with three rows of horizontal numbers. The top row of numbers correlates to the highway or road number that the road with the stop sign intersects with. For example, this image is taken from Vermont State Road 116, looking towards the intersecting road.

The State of New York uses similar style signs. However, these signs can be attached to different types of sign posts (town entry signs, highway signs, etc.)

You can find those square guardrails mostly in state of New York and Wyoming.

You can rarely see them in states close to New York state.

The ending -kill is common in New York place names. Examples include Catskill and Cobleskill. The word is derived from the Middle Dutch word kille (modern Dutch kil). As New York used to be under Dutch rule in the 17th century, that’s where you’ll find them the most.

Wyoming.text: Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming.

In far Northeastern Wyoming lies Devil’s Tower, which is a very tall, standalone butte protruding from the surrounding land. This can sometimes be seen from many miles away because of the lack of nearby mountains.
Roadside bollards in Wyoming often feature a dark metal pole with a white circular reflector at the top. The top of the metal pole is sometimes painted white or grey, which is unique to Wyoming.

Northeast.text: Brownstone buildings are typically row houses or government buildings made out of various types of brick and sandstone. They are most commonly found in dense urban areas of the Northeast US, as well as Chicago.

The Balsam Fir is a very symmetric tree. It has pretty dark needles and often grows close to the ground.

Within the US, you will find it in the Northeast, starting in Northern New York. You can also see it near the Great Lakes, on Latitudes similar to Vermont/Maine.

Montana.text: These bollards with a rectangle on top are common in Idaho and can only be seen there in western US. The rectangle can be white or yellow. Montana has a similar yellow version, but the reflector is much larger.

The area spanning from the Montana Border with Saskatchewan to the Western Great Lakes features many ‘prairie potholes.’ These are areas of low-lying wetlands that feature marshy grasses and small, shallow ponds.

Along the Canadian border in Montana lies Glacier National Park. It is easily recognizable by its extremely tall and steep mountain peaks. Most coverage is also hazy and taken during summer.

NOTE: Other National Parks within the Rocky Mountain range of the US can have a similar appearance, so consider other clues before guessing.

Theodore Roosevelt National Park features similar, sand-brown, eroded rock formations to Badlands National Park. The rock formations in this park tend to have more trees on them. Additionally, almost all coverage has fall colours visible.

NOTE: Similar formations can be seen in far eastern Montana as well.

Southwest.text: In the Appalachian area stretching from southern New York to southern Virginia, there are a lot of forest-covered rolling hills, with flat valleys dividing them. A majority of the ridges are oriented Southwest to Northeast.

Big Bend National Park is located along the Mexico border in Southwest Texas. It can be identified by its dry, rocky peaks and shrubby foliage. This park is adjacent to the Chihauhan desert, so plants such as yucca and prickly pear cactus are common.

‘Carl’s Jr.’ and ‘Hardee’s’ are fast food restaurants that are operated by the same company and have a similar logo and colour scheme. However, Carl’s Jr. locations are all located on the West Coast and Southwest US, while Hardee’s are found in the central and Eastern areas of the country. Two states, Wyoming and Oklahoma, have both kinds of restaurants present.

The Southwest, centred around the Four Corners region of Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, and Colorado, feature many mesas and tablelands. Often, these rock formations will be red in colour. Additionally, red soil is common in these areas.

In the Appalachian area stretching from southern New York to southern Virginia, there are a lot of forest-covered rolling hills, with flat valleys dividing them. A majority of the ridges are oriented Southwest to Northeast.

Kentucky.text: Kentucky commonly uses thin strips on the edge of the road, which is unique to the state. These strips are not to be confused with long thin strips that do not reach the edge of the road, which can also be used in Kentucky but also elsewhere.
Some roads and highways in the state of Kentucky use uniquely-shaped rumble strips that are thin, relatively long recessed lines on the very outside edges of the road.

Great Plains.text: The Great Plains are in the middle of the United States and stretch from the Canadian border in the North, to central Texas in the South. This area is primarily flat with few trees. Some areas feature agriculture fields, while others feature dry and barren grassy fields.

The Great Plains are in the middle of the United States and stretch from the Canadian border in the North, to central Texas in the South. This area is primarily flat with few trees. Some areas feature agriculture fields, while others feature dry and barren grassy fields.

Rocky Mountains.text: The area stretching from the Canadian border to Northern New Mexico is home to the Rocky Mountains. These jagged, rocky formations often feature many pine trees and visible snow all-year round at the highest peaks. Some areas of the Rocky Mountain Range are noticeably dry, with few trees.

The Black Hills, located in far Western South Dakota and far Eastern Wyoming, are a series of moderately tall mountains with large amounts of conifer trees and rocky outcroppings. The surrounding areas are typically much flatter with lesser tree cover.

NOTE: This area has a similar appearance to many areas within the Rocky Mountains, which lie further to the West.

Central Colorado is home to a large North-to-South oriented mountain ridge. This divides the Rocky Mountains to the west and the Great Plains to the east.These mountains are adjacent to the major metropolitan areas of Boulder, Denver, and Colorado Springs.

Indiana.text: This kind of blue square on a post is exclusive to Indiana.

Georgia.text: Georgia likes to decorate its freeway offramps with no parking signs.
Saw Palmetto grows in clumps or dense thickets in sandy coastal areas, and as undergrowth in pine woods or hardwood hammocks. You can find it in coastal areas of Florida and Georgia.

‘Tim Hortons’ is known for being the most popular restaurant chain in Canada. However, there are also many locations in the United States. They are primarily located in states adjacent to the Canadian Provinces of Ontario and Quebec, with a few locations also in Texas and Georgia.

Tennessee.text: Tennessee and Kentucky look like a mix of Appalachian and Southern Landscape.
The city of Chattanooga in Tennessee has its own unique font that is used on some signs in the city.
Tennessee state routes have these unique mile markers. The larger number is the mile (resets at county borders) and the smaller bottom one is the state route number.
This three-star symbol is found in many places in Tennessee, including but not limited to these historical place signs. It’s the same symbol as on the state flag but it can also be black and white.

New Hampshire.text: These are also specific to New Hampshire. Notice the dividing line on the sign.
In New Hampshire there will often be a white metal sign with the characters ‘E-2’ on it adjacent to the road, typically at either end of bridges.
In New Hampshire there will often be a white metal sign with the characters ‘E-2’ on it adjacent to the road, typically at either end of bridges.

Maryland.text: This green U.S. Route shield with the word business at the top is unique to Maryland.
Some Interstate bridges in Maryland (but not the neighboring states or DC) seem to have this code painted on them. (Discovered by bagaboiebailey in the USA GeoGuessr Community server).

Iowa.text: ‘Kwik Star' is a chain of gas stations and convenience stores that are located in Iowa

Southeast.text: The supermarket chain ‘Piggly Wiggly’ is found mostly in the Southeast, as well as the state of Wisconsin.

Small, rectangular manufactured homes, also known as mobile or ‘trailer’ homes, are popular in rural areas of the US. In general, mobile homes are more common in the Southeast but they can be seen anywhere in the country.

The restaurant chain ‘Waffle House’ is a regional chain that is primarily found in the Southern and Southeast US. Some midwest and mid-atlantic states have some locations. Georgia, by far, is the state with the most Waffle House locations.

‘Zaxby’s,’ a fast-food chicken chain, is another restaurant that is most common in the Southeast US. There are several pockets outside the Southeast that have locations, such as Utah and Montana. Like Waffle House, Georgia has the highest number of locations.

Maine.text: The Maine inspection stickers come in various colors but they all have one thing in common - all have one edge or a chunk from one side missing.

Maine often uses a dashed single yellow line or a combination of dashed and solid instead of a solid double one in the middle of a road.
I feel like Maine does it a bit more often than other states in the region.

Missouri.text: ‘Casey’s’ is a popular gas station and convenience store chain that is found in the Midwest, Plains, and parts of the Mid-South. Illinois, Iowa, and Missouri have the highest number of locations.
Shown here is the population density of the United States. In General, areas east of the Missouri river are more densely populated than areas to the west. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Illinois.text: Some rural roads in the Upper Midwest use a similar road pavement to Texas. They will have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface, but will vary in colour. These roads are most common in the state of Illinois.

Some rural roads in the Upper Midwest use a similar road pavement to Texas. They will have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface, but will vary in colour. These roads are most common in the state of Illinois.

spotlight.text: Juneau, Alaska’s Capital city, is the largest settlement in the Alaskan panhandle. Therefore, it is much more ‘built up’ than other towns in this area. The city is surrounded by heavily forested mountains and hills.

The Denali highway, stretching from Cantwell to Paxson in central Alaska, is a mostly gravel highway in the ‘Alaska’ mountain range. This road runs generally east to west, is covered in the generation 2 camera, and was taken in late summer, so wildflowers and green shrubby plants are common.

The infamous “Hawaiian lattice” can be recognized by the volcanic soil and rocks that are abundant in the region. Volcanic vegetation can also be seen lining the roads. Note that the angle of the roads is a big clue for the area, and that this lattice was built on the slope of Mauna Loa.
On the eastern side of the island of Molokaʻi lies the Kamakou volcano, leading to a significantly hillier and slightly more vegetated landscape than the western parts of the island.

Kahoʻolawe is a small island that lies just to the southwest of Maui. It only has trekker coverage on small gravel roads and dirt trails, and is characterised by dry, shrubby vegetation, rolling hills, and dark red soil. On the western end of this coverage, several buildings can be seen. To report inaccuracies, suggest new clues or give general feedback about our content, please use this form: https://www.plonkit.net/feedback

As part of a promotional campaign, the TransAmerica Trail from Oregon to North Carolina was covered by a Ford Bronco. The car can recognised by its unblurred black roof and red hood, and is mostly found on unpaved rural roads. Looking backwards, you will see two other Ford SUVs escorting the camera car.

Interstate 19 in Arizona from Tucson to the Mexico border uses kilometres on the exit and distance signs. This is the only part of the country that uses kilometres instead of miles for highway signs. NOTE: Speed limit signs in this area still use MPH instead of KPH.

Many bridges are used to connect the various neighbourhoods of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. These expansive, steel bridges are commonly painted bright yellow. Additionally, Pittsburgh is easy to identify because of it being flanked by 3 rivers and steep bluffs on all sides.

The Florida Keys are an archipelago of tropical islands west of Miami. The highway connecting the islands can be recognized by green, tropical vegetation on the sides of the usually single lane road. The soil is also sandy white. Urban locations are also similar, but with many more planted palm trees and mowed grass being a common sight.

Deep South Florida, between the metropolitan areas of Ft. Myers and Miami, features dense, jungle-like forests that have few inhabitants. Roads through these areas are commonly very straight and long.

The area between the cities of Orlando and Lakeland in Florida sometimes feature low, rolling hills. Lakes and agricultural fields are also common in this area. This is the only main hilly area in central or southern Florida.
Southwestern Oklahoma features a small area of rocky, shrubby peaks. Some of the mountains are also covered in trees, and the rocks can have a pinkish red tint to them.

Central Colorado is home to a large North-to-South oriented mountain ridge. This divides the Rocky Mountains to the west and the Great Plains to the east.These mountains are adjacent to the major metropolitan areas of Boulder, Denver, and Colorado Springs.

Big Bend National Park is located along the Mexico border in Southwest Texas. It can be identified by its dry, rocky peaks and shrubby foliage. This park is adjacent to the Chihauhan desert, so plants such as yucca and prickly pear cactus are common.

Along the New Mexico and or Texas border there is a ridge of tall, dry peaks known as the Guadalupe Mountains. In adjacent areas of both states, smaller foothills of these mountains can be seen with relatively flat tops and shrubby foliage.

Along the Canadian border in Montana lies Glacier National Park. It is easily recognizable by its extremely tall and steep mountain peaks. Most coverage is also hazy and taken during summer. NOTE: Other National Parks within the Rocky Mountain range of the US can have a similar appearance, so consider other clues before guessing.

Theodore Roosevelt National Park features similar, sand-brown, eroded rock formations to Badlands National Park. The rock formations in this park tend to have more trees on them. Additionally, almost all coverage has fall colours visible. NOTE: Similar formations can be seen in far eastern Montana as well.

In far Northeastern Wyoming lies Devil’s Tower, which is a very tall, standalone butte protruding from the surrounding land. This can sometimes be seen from many miles away because of the lack of nearby mountains.

The Black Hills, located in far Western South Dakota and far Eastern Wyoming, are a series of moderately tall mountains with large amounts of conifer trees and rocky outcroppings. The surrounding areas are typically much flatter with lesser tree cover. NOTE: This area has a similar appearance to many areas within the Rocky Mountains, which lie further to the West.

AL.name: Albania
AL.key_meta: If you look up and see a "rift" in the sky, this glitch is most commonly found in Albania or Montenegro within Europe.

metas.title: Rifts
metas.description: If you look up and see a "rift" in the sky, this glitch is most commonly found in Albania or Montenegro within Europe. Most of the time, you will see it, but if you don’t, don’t rule out these countries.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: Albanian bollards are triangular in shape, and white with a black top. They have a red front and a white rear reflector.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Italy uses the same bollards.

Coverage.text: Coverage in Albania is limited. Generally only the larger towns have extensive side-road coverage. Note that while the coverage is limited, a lot of it still appears to be very rural. It is not just on big main roads or urban areas. You can click on the image to enlarge it, or use this site to study the official coverage in detail.

Rift.text: There are two types of car and camera meta in Albania: Coverage where the Google car has a long antenna and you can see rifts in the sky. Coverage where the Google car has a long antenna and you can see rifts in the sky. Coverage where the Google car has a short antenna and there are no rifts visible. Coverage where the Google car has a short antenna and there are no rifts visible. You can click on the image to enlarge it. You can also use this Maps layer to look at the coverage in more detail (credits to icraig1205).

spotlight.text: The road leading into Theth National Park can typically be recognised by the tall, jagged mountains, often with bare mountainsides.
The road by the eastern part of the Montenegrin border goes in a valley with tall, fully exposed cliff sides along the road.
Maja e Papingut is a massive mountain in the south of Albania, with an almost completely vertical cliffside near the top. It can be seen from several nearby roads.
A wide, almost dried out river valley going southeast to northwest, can be seen along the SH71 between Pishaj and Kokel.

The large Bay of Vlorë can be seen on many parts of the SH4 between Vlorë and Orikum. It can be recognized by the large Karaburun peninsula jutting out into the ocean from the south, and the small Sazan island just to its north.
A couple of small roads northwest of Vlorë can be recognised by the very coastal-looking Aleppo pine forest.
On the SH4 between Levan and Tepelenë and right by the Greek border, you may see double outer road lines with a wide gap between them.

On this section of the E86 near the Greek border, you will sometimes see these unique bollards. They have a round shape and a simple red reflector. They look superficially similar to the flatter Turkish bollard.

AS.name: American Samoa
AS.key_meta: If you see a Street View car with a slightly rusted black truck bed, you know you're in American Samoa.

metas.title: Unique car
metas.description: If you see a Street View car with a slightly rusted black truck bed, you know you're in American Samoa.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner

metas.title: Infrastructure - Coconut / Powerline / Guardrail
metas.description: Tau has a long East-West road that is difficult to line up.
metas.comparison: If you're generally heading East-West, have Concrete Pavement and you see a lot of Coconut Palms, you're in the central part of the road, east of the river. The short stretch immediately east of the river only shows the Coconuts in the distance towards East. There's both a Powerline and a Guardrail.

metas.title: Landscape - Camel Rock
metas.description: Behold: The Camel Rock. Two little peaks reaching into the ocean.
metas.comparison: It is marked as a POI on Google Maps.

metas.title: Car Meta - Tutuila Car
metas.description: A slightly rusted black truck bed can be seen on the main island of Tutuila.
metas.comparison: This is the most common car that will be seen as it has the most coverage.

metas.title: Trekker - Aunu Ferry
metas.description: The only ferry Trekker of American Samoa. If you're on a boat between two islands in AS, you're here.

metas.title: Trekker - Ofu Beach
metas.description: Ofu Beach is easy to recognize, with the coast to the Southeast and three distinct peaks in the Northeast.

metas.title: Landscape - Manu'a - Ofu
metas.description: The town Ofu on Manu'a has a West Coast. This road can be distinguished from the West Coast of Olosega, because:

metas.title: Car Meta - Manu'a Car
metas.description: The front of a silver-grey truck with side mirrors can be seen on Manu’a and Olosega, which are connected by a bridge.

metas.title: Car Meta - Tau Car
metas.description: The front of a similar truck can be seen on the easternmost covered island of Tau. However, the truck will be glossy black, with side mirrors visible.

metas.title: Landscape - Tutuila East Coast
metas.description: This is the only part of Tutuila where you can see Coast on the east, without other parts of Tutuila visible. You will often see Aunu'u in the Southeast.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Tutuila Concrete Road
metas.description: If you are on Tutuila and have a Concrete Road with no coast visible, you're on the far Eastern Part of the island, between Onenoa and Matatula Elementary school.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Manu'a/Olosega Sand Road
metas.description: From slightly North of the town entry of Olosega until the southernmost house WEST of the road, you will have a plain sand road, with no grass verge in the middle.
metas.comparison: This is the only road of this kind on the two islands with this Google Car.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Super Straight Road
metas.description: This section of the Rte 014 is by far the straightest covered road on Tutuila. Use the road angle to confirm. The appearance is quite varied, but it's also very flat

metas.title: Landscape - Fagasa Bay
metas.description: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northwest. Note that Afono is opened towards North proper, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

metas.title: Landscape - Tau - Faleasao
metas.description: Faleasao is a little town on Tau (and thus has the Tau car). It has a coast in the North and is otherwise surrounded by mountains. Together with the Tau car, it is unique.

metas.title: Landscape - Vatia Bay
metas.description: Vatia Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards Northeast. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Afono Bay is opened towards North proper.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Ofu Airport
metas.description: Ofu Airport is small with a concrete runway. The Google Car covering it has two orange straps on the roof. Many palm trees can also be seen on the other side of the runway.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Bridge
metas.description: The single-lane bridge, connecting the islands of Manu’a and Olosega, can be easily recognized by the thin wire guardrail, with the two islands on either side of the bridge.

metas.title: Landscape - Afono Bay
metas.description: Afono Bay is the only Bay with coverage that is opened towards straight North. Note that Fagasa Bay is opened towards Northwest, while Vatia Bay is opened towards Northeast.

metas.title: Landscape - Pago Pago Harbour
metas.description: The roads alonog the Pago Pago Harbour are recognizable because they're generally very urban (for American Samoa), and you can often see the harbour when it isn't blocked by buildings.

metas.title: Landscape - East of Summit 001 - Overcast
metas.description: This road crosses the district border on the 001. It is characterized through the unique angle and the mountains in the north. Often you can see a unique summit in the west. The driving direction is eastwards.
metas.comparison: There is a stretch of the 001 with a similar angle near Malaeimi, but it has a clearly visible valley in the North which is not found on this road. The road can further be divided as it is overcast in the Western District and sunny in the Eastern District.

metas.title: Landscape - Western South Coast Road
metas.description: This road is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car drives eastward (unlike the Eastern Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your left.
metas.comparison: On the eastern south coast road, there is a tiny part that also drives eastward for some reason, which can be baity.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Tutuila Airport
metas.description: On the roads along the airport on Tutuila, you will always see these fences surrounding the airport. This is obviously common for airports, but since Tutuila only has one airstrip, this road is a free 5k together with the Tutuila car.

metas.title: Landscape - Tutuila - Rte 018
metas.description: The Rte 018 in Tafuna is urban and uniquely shows this mountain in the North. The alignment is generally North-South. The road has double yellow lines (not that common in AS) and a power line in the East. The driving direction is to the North.
metas.comparison: Make sure that parts of the Rte 001 can look similar with a similar road angle. To confirm it's the Rte 018, you can pan exactly North. If you look at the mountain, it's the Rte 018, otherwise it's not.

metas.title: Landscape - Manu'a - North Coast road (paved)
metas.description: On Manu'a/Olosega (which have a unique car), there are two covered roads with North coast: The roads east and west of the famous bridge. They can easily be differentiated, because the Olosega (east) road is unpaved, while the Manu'a (west) road has concrete pavement.

metas.title: Landscape - Eastern South Coast Road
metas.description: This long stretch of road (which is probably further regionguessable) is easily recognizable because it has a South Coast and the Car Drives westward (unlike the Western Coastal Road). That means that when you pan onto the back of the truck, the water will be to your right.
metas.comparison: There is one annoying exception, around the POI 'Amouli Beach Fales' east of the town Amouli.

Main.text: A slightly rusted black truck bed can be seen on the main island of Tutuila. This is the most common car that will be seen as it has the most coverage.

Other.text: The front of a silver-grey truck with side mirrors can be seen on Manu’a and Olosega, which are connected by a bridge. See below for more information.
The front of a similar truck can be seen on the easternmost covered island of Tau. However, the truck will be glossy black, with side mirrors visible.

spotlight.text: The single-lane bridge, connecting the islands of Manu’a and Olosega, can be easily recognized by the thin wire guardrail, with the two islands on either side of the bridge.

Ofu Airport is small with a concrete runway. The Google Car covering it has two orange straps on the roof. Many palm trees can also be seen on the other side of the runway. AD.name: Andorra
AD.key_meta: Andorra has a lot of these distinct stone buildings, visible almost everywhere in the country.

metas.title: Stone buildings
metas.description: Andorra has a lot of these distinct stone buildings, visible almost everywhere in the country.
metas.comparison: These buildings can also be found near Andorra, in the French and Spanish Pyrenees.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: The Andorran bollard has an orange reflector and can be occasionally found on the main highways.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This bollard can also be found in Spain.

metas.title: Gen 3 Autumn
metas.description: All the Generation 3 coverage was taken in October, meaning that many deciduous trees have autumn colours.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

Vella.text: Andorra la Vella is a capital city surrounded by high mountains, making it recognisable. NOTE: It is the highest European capital with an altitude of 1023 metres.

Caldea.text: In the capital Andorra la Vella you can often see the Caldea tower and the sky wheel.

Pas.text: Pas de la Casa, a touristy city in eastern Andorra, can be easily recognized by the plethora of shops and hotels. As it is located at an altitude of 2080 metres, there are no trees visible on the mountains surrounding it.

AQ.name: Antarctica
AQ.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (17 regions covered).

Halfmoonisland.text: Half Moon Island was covered by a tripod. It can also be recognized by the numerous other people in red jackets.

Deceptionisland.text: The Deception Island Bay can be recognized by the blue and white ship in the bay, and the abandoned equipment on the beach.

Deceptionislandconga.text: The trekker can be seen walking in a line on Deception Island.

Deceptionislanddarkbeach.text: A beach with black sand and many penguins can be seen on Deception Island.

Cuvervilleisland.text: Cuverville Island can be recognised by the overcast weather combined with the coastline to the northwest. You’ll also see a decent number of penguins, particularly toward the east.

Dancoisland.text: Danco Island can be recognised by the beautiful sunset coverage over a snowy fjord.

Petermannisland.text: Petermann Island can be recognized by the layer of snow with patches of exposed rocks, and the overexposed camera.

Rossisland.text: The coverage at the western tip of Ross Island can typically be recognised by the extremely dark, and mostly barren, rocky soil.

Rossislandcabin.text: A tripod featuring the exterior and interior of a small wooden cabin with a grey metal roof can be found south of the eastern tip of Ross Island.

Mcmurdo.text: McMurdo Station is the largest research station on Antarctica, and can be recognized by the dark brown soil, many buildings, American infrastructure and sunset coverage. NOTE: A lot of the coverage around McMurdo Station has the sun setting in the south, which shouldn’t lead you to guess in the northern hemisphere.

Mcmurdotripods.text: You can also find tripod coverage inside several buildings at McMurdo Station.

Mcmurdohut.text: On the eastern side of McMurdo Station you can find a small wooden cabin, having a tripod going inside.

Icetrekker.text: Southeast of McMurdo station, the trekker can be seen walking on a layer of ice around various machinery.

Mainlandvalleys.text: The trekker can be seen walking through a fantastical landscape consisting of many desolate valleys on mainland Antarctica, west of Ross Island.

Blackisland.text: A vast, snowy landscape with spread out hills can be seen south of McMurdo station.

Southpole.text: The tripod at the south pole can be recognized by numerous countries’ flags around the tripod, and a sign with ‘Geographic South Pole’ written on it. This location is often on community-made world maps for a better scoring range.

Southpoleobservatory.text: The South Pole Observatory has tripod coverage going around and inside of it. To report inaccuracies, suggest new clues or give general feedback about our content, please use this form: https://www.plonkit.net/feedback

metas.title: Landscape + black car
metas.description: If you find yourself in a flat, desolate, treeless, sparsely populated area with a visible black back of the Google car, you're likely in Argentina.
metas.comparison: (Jordan might resemble this landscape for new players, and it also has a black back on the car, so be aware of that.) (Only other countries in South America with car like that are: Peru and Uruguay)

A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner

metas.title: Double concrete pole
metas.description: This double-rounded concrete pole connected by a concrete ring is almost exclusive to Argentina. Similar ones can occasionally be found in Bolivia, but the landscape will be vastly different.
