metas.description: All car coverage in Germany is made with a Generation 4 camera.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Camera Meta - Low Cam
metas.description: Lowcam coverage can be found around Singen and near Switzerland.

metas.title: White Sticker Poles
metas.description: Most wooden poles in Germany will feature a rectangular white sticker.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Architecture - Red Brick
metas.description: These brick houses are generally concentrated in northwestern Germany.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This map is very approximate.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Round Concrete Poles
metas.description: These round concrete poles are almost unique to Former Eastern Germany.

metas.title: Car Meta - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.description: You can find a Generation 3 black car in this safari park southeast of Bielefeld.
metas.comparison: You can commonly see 4x4s painted with a zebra pattern in the park. NOTE: This car is unique to this park within all of Europe.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Black Disk Bollard
metas.description: Bollards standing on these black disks are commonly found in all of eastern Germany.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Hanover
metas.description: Hanover uses white signs with a wider than usual gap between the sign and metallic frame.

metas.title: No Stopping Signs
metas.description: “No Stopping” and “No Waiting” signs in Germany will often have white arrows drawn on them.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Infrastructure - White Tree Paint
metas.description: You can spot trees that are painted white close to the bottom of the trunk in the northeast.
metas.comparison: NOTE: You will rarely find them outside the shaded region.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Cologne Lamppost Plate
metas.description: Lampposts in Cologne will often feature these bright yellow numbers on a black piece of plastic.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Similar looking things can be found elsewhere as well.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Darmstadt
metas.description: Streetsigns in Darmstadt are white and often are written in ALL CAPS, which is unique in Germany.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Grey Bollard Plate
metas.description: Baden-Württemberg is the only state where the plates on the bollards can be grey instead of white.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Düsseldorf
metas.description: Düsseldorf has black signs with a white border, similar to Munich. The signs have a metallic frame.

metas.title: Landscape - Alps
metas.description: The German Alps is the most mountainous region in Germany, it is mostly concentrated on the Austrian Border.

metas.title: Central - Black Fish Scale Roofs & Walls
metas.description: Houses with black slate walls, resembling fish scales, are commonly found in a large area of central Germany.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Thicc T Pole
metas.description: These pole tops where the middle of the horizontal bar is thicker can be found in all of former East Germany.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Wuppertal
metas.description: Wuppertal uses white signs with a unique font and a white painted frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.title: Infrastructure - ALDI Nord
metas.description: There are two regional Aldi chains, which have split Germany in two; Aldi Süd in the south, and Aldi Nord in the north.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Munich
metas.description: Munich has blue street signs with a white decorative border that does not touch the corners. Also note the unique font.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Nuremberg
metas.description: Nuremberg has blue signs with a unique font. The signs also have a grey frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dortmund
metas.description: Dortmund uses blue signs with a white border and a grey frame. The signs also have a separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Frankfurt
metas.description: Frankfurt uses blue street signs with a metallic border around the sign, as well as the separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.title: Vegetation - Baltic Pines
metas.description: Baltic Pines or Pinus sylvestris are generally more concentrated in the northeast of Germany. They can be recognized by their orange-tinged trunk.

metas.title: Language - Sorbian
metas.description: Sorbian, a Slavic language, is spoken near the Polish and Czech border. You can find it on a variety of signs in this region between Cottbus and Bautzen.

metas.title: East - Large Apartment Buildings
metas.description: These large, utilitarian apartment buildings constructed during the socialist era, that are also known as “Commie blocks” are common in all of former East Germany.

metas.title: Landscape - Regensburg Plains & Ridge
metas.description: The flat plains southeast of Regensburg can be recognised by the slight ridge often visible to the northeast. The plains themselves are flat, and quite agricultural.

metas.title: Landscape - Sylt
metas.description: The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.

metas.title: Flat-Arm-on-Inside Germany
metas.description: White Belt: Croatia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Pointed Shoes: Germany, Hungary. > Germany Belt: Above hip. Hungary Belt: Bottom of hip. Germany arm: Flat side on left. Hungary arm: Flat side on right.

general_rules.text: German area codes are grouped by their first digit. You can practise them by playing this map.
Postal codes are arranged in a counter-clockwise fashion, starting with 0 around Saxony and ending with 9 in northern Bavaria and parts of Thuringia.
Each German state also has their own coat of arms. They are found on unblurred licence plates and some official buildings.

Saarland.text: These dark-green designs can be found in Saarland only.
I'd avise to learn where this cannot be found, which is Easter Germany, Hesse, Baden-Württemberg and Saarland.
These basic white plates on bollards can be found in all states except for Bavaria, Saarland and the City States.

Berlin.text: Berlin uses segmented bus stops, with a yellow signpost.
Berlin uses bright orange bins that have white text on them.
Berlin uses white signs with a grey border, and a separate section for numbers under the street name. Also note how the letter ß looks.

Hamburg.text: Hamburg uses bright red bins, with white speech bubbles.

You can find this rare white and black Generation 4 car in Hamburg and around Frankfurt.

NOTE: You can also find the same car around London and in Ireland.
Hamburg bus stops have a red signpost, and the route numbers are within hexagons. Note that they can be found outside of Hamburg as well
This rare Generation 3 car coverage with an antenna can be found in central Hamburg (Speicherstadt). Note by MB: This is officially a trekker, so you won't find any copyright.
You can find this rare white and black Generation 4 car in Hamburg and around Frankfurt. NOTE: You can also find the same car around London and in Ireland.

Brandenburg.text: Fully yellow posts are found in the state of Brandenburg.
Fully yellow posts are found in the state of Brandenburg.

Bremen.text: Bremen has green and grey bins, with orange speech bubbles.
Bremen proper uses simple bus stops, which have the bus stop name within a red section. The edges can be rounded.
Bremerhaven, which is still part of Bremen, uses bus stops with a grey section on the opposite side of the signpost. And the bus stop name is red within a yellow section.

Saxony-Anhalt.text:
Yellow posts with a white plate on them are found in Saxony-Anhalt.

NOTE: Sometimes there is only 1 plate, which can make it hard to tell apart from a Brandenburg post.
Folded Signs are most common in Bremen, then Saxony-Anhalt and Saarland.
These trident-like pole tops can be found in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, and Baden-Württemberg.
These white posts with a red cap are found in all of former East Germany, but most commonly in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.
Hop fields are mainly found between Ingolstadt and Landshut - an area called 'Hallertau/Holledau' in Bavaria. There are some minor regions in Thuringia, Saxony-Anhalt and Saxony as well.

There are 13 wine regions in Germany. They are mostly concentrated in the southwest of Germany. However, there are a couple regions further east as well, along the border between Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt, as well as along the Elbe in Saxony.
These white posts with a red cap are found in all of former East Germany, but most commonly in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.
Yellow posts with a white plate on them are found in Saxony-Anhalt. NOTE: Sometimes there is only 1 plate, which can make it hard to tell apart from a Brandenburg post.
These trident-like pole tops can be found in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, and Baden-Württemberg.

Bavaria.text: These round wooden bollards, which have a painted top, are found in Bavaria.
Pole tops which have a curved horizontal bar can be found in Bavaria, though they are rare.
These simple orange posts are most commonly found in Bavaria, and also in the other highlighted states.
These round wooden bollards, which have a painted top, are found in Bavaria.
These simple orange posts are most commonly found in Bavaria, and also in the other highlighted states.
Bavaria uses these white rectangular road markers, which are divided by black lines into three sections. The left section provides the road you are currently on.
Pole tops which have a curved horizontal bar can be found in Bavaria, though they are rare.

Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.text: The suffix -ow can be found in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Berlin and Brandenburg.
Many trees in Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern have these tiny green markers on them. You can very rarely find them in Lower Saxony.
Non-folded signbacks are most common in Schleswig-Holstein, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Hesse, Hamburg, Bremen, then Brandenburg, Saxony, Baden-Württemberg.
The double connector signback is very common in Schleswig-Holstein and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. It is also found in Brandenburg. Rarely, you may see it in Saxony, Rhineland-Palatinate or Hamburg.

Thatched roofs and rock walls are most common on the North Frisian Islands, as well as mainland Schleswig-Holstein.
You can also commonly find them in coastal resort towns in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
Many trees in Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern have these tiny green markers on them. You can very rarely find them in Lower Saxony.

Lower Saxony.text: You can find these simple rectangular markers, with rounded edges in Lower Saxony.
Red bicycle signs can be found in Northrhine-Westphalia, Southern Lower Saxony and Hamburg.

These irregular looking bollards, which do not have a white encasing on the bottom half, are found on K-roads in this region of Lower Saxony, around Lüneburg. K-Roads in this region will not have any other type of bollard.

These irregular looking bollards, which do not have a white encasing on the bottom half, are found on K-roads in this region of Lower Saxony. K-Roads in this region will not have any other type of bollard.
You can find these simple rectangular markers, with rounded edges in Lower Saxony.
These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. NOTE: The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony.

Rhineland-Palatinate.text: The suffix -weiler can mainly be found in Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland and Baden-Württemberg.
Rhineland-Palatinate is the only state where the plates on the bollards are orange instead of white.
Rhineland-Palatinate and Saxony use unpainted, rocky looking posts, with white plates stuck on each side.
I'd avise to learn where this cannot be found, which is Schleswig-Holstein, Rhineland-Palatinate, Bremen and Hamburg.

While most of Germany uses B-Type guardrails, A-type guardrails are common in the northwest, as well as in Rhineland-Palatinate and parts of Bavaria. NOTE: There will always be rare exceptions. For a good overview of European guardrails, see this infographic.
Rhineland-Palatinate is the only state where the plates on the bollards are orange instead of white.

North Rhine-Westphalia.text: Some bollards in North Rhine-Westphalia have a green bit at the top. The top can also be another colour.
North Rhine-Westphalia uses white posts without white plates on the sides. You can also find posts which go all the way to the ground.
Some of the green caps will have the text ‘LVR’, along with a small coat of arms. These specific green caps are unique to southern North Rhine-Westphalia.

Bicycle direction signs typically feature a white background with green lettering. In Hamburg, North Rhine-Westphalia and a neighbouring part of Lower Saxony, you will instead find red lettering. The Saarland has its own distinctive design, with white text on a dark green background.
Some of the green caps will have the text ‘LVR’, along with a small coat of arms. These specific green caps are unique to southern North Rhine-Westphalia.

Saxony.text: This type of half-timbered house with arches at the ground floor is very common in this region of Saxony.

Thuringia.text: The plates on the Thuringia Triangle Posts are unique, as they have sections which are seperated by a black line.
Saarland, Thuringia, and Baden-Württemberg use white posts, with the same white plates attached. Note by MB: PlonkIt says they're smaller in BaWü. From what I saw, this is fake though.

Schleswig-Holstein.text: Schleswig-Holstein sometimes uses slightly different cycling sign designs. For the one with town-names, note the difference in the arrow. For the one without, the shape is different.
These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony.

Nordrhein-Westfalen.text: Bollards with darker reflectors than usual are commonly found in Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Bavaria. They can sometimes be found in Baden-Württemberg and rarely in Hesse.

NRW.text: Some bollards in North Rhine-Westphalia have a green bit at the top. The top can also be another colour.

spotlight.text: Every city state has recognisable rubbish bins all around the city. Berlin uses bright orange bins that have white text on them. Berlin uses bright orange bins that have white text on them. Hamburg uses bright red bins, with white speech bubbles. Hamburg uses bright red bins, with white speech bubbles. Bremen has green and grey bins, with orange speech bubbles. Bremen has green and grey bins, with orange speech bubbles. Bremerhaven uses a more generic green design, with a black logo.
This type of half-timbered house with arches at the ground floor is very common in this region of Saxony.
This rare Generation 3 car coverage with an antenna can be found in central Hamburg.

GH.name: Ghana
GH.key_meta: All regular road coverage in Ghana features a unique Google car with a visible roof rack and a piece of black tape on the right end of the front bar.

metas.title: Unique car
metas.description: All regular road coverage in Ghana features a unique Google car with a visible roof rack and a piece of black tape on the right end of the front bar. The hood is usually visible, displaying a Street View car wrapping with a red rectangle and other distinctive elements.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner
A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Basics

general_rules.text: This map shows the distribution of paved and unpaved roads across the country. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Coverage.text: The coverage in Ghana is limited and easy to memorize, as most of it was taken on its main roads and in major cities. The most dense coverage is located in the south, around the cities of Accra and Kumasi.

The.text: Ghana features 3 distinct types of tape on the google car: In the southwest, you can find the ‘unpeeled tape’, which is essentially a mostly intact tape, which is not peeling off. In the east and north, you can find the ‘peeled tape’, which unlike the ‘unpeeled tape’, is slightly peeled off. North of Kumasi, and west of Tamale, you can find this ‘scotched tape’, which has two distinct white spots on the left side of the tape.

Landscape.text: Northern Ghana features a savannah landscape, which can be identified by its dry soil and less dense vegetation.

Mountain.text: Tall mountain ranges in Ghana are typically seen near Lake Volta in the highlighted area. NOTE: Mountain ranges to the east are more common in the area near Togo.

Forests.text: Dense forests in Ghana are typically found in the southwest and east. You will usually see many naturally occurring palm trees, making the two regions recognizable.

Coastal.text: Tall palm trees are commonly found along the coast. Most of them are located in the west.

spotlight.text: Most unpaved roads in a dry savannah landscape are found north of Wa, as well as near the town itself. NOTE: The other unpaved roads in northern Ghana are the Yendi-Nkwanta road in the east, and part of the Salaga-Tamale road, which has very distinct soil. See the tips below.

The road connecting the town of Sawla with the N10 has very crisp, new road lines. Most of the road runs in a general east-west direction, through a lush savannah landscape. The middle line can be solid or dashed. NOTE: There are a couple of other roads with crisp road lines like these, however these tend to have a different road angle or landscape.

The Salaga-Tamale road up to Kpalbusi is a dirt road with very moody overcast coverage. The soil tends to be very dark, with a purple or brown tinge to it. The road also has a unique tropical savannah feel. The soil is most dark near the town of Salaga. NOTE: Unpaved roads with overcast coverage and a savannah landscape can be found in other places. The unique aspect of this road is the dark purplish brown soil and the especially dark cloud cover.

The road between Nkwanta and Domanko is unpaved, with a powerline close to the road to your east or northeast. The road itself runs in a general SE-NW direction, through a lush savannah landscape that is typical of central Ghana. NOTE: In urban areas, there can be a powerline on both sides of the road. In addition, a section of the Salaga-Tamale road has a powerline to the east as well, but the darker soil and moody cloud cover makes it distinguishable.

On a section of the N2 east of Lake Volta, you can often see a ridgeline to your southeast, somewhat close to the road. The road itself also has a distinct angle, running in a general SW-NE direction. The sky is very overcast and grey.

The coastal area just east of Accra, especially on the N1, has a distinct landscape: it is very flat and wide open, with significantly less vegetation than the rest of southern Ghana. Some parts can look somewhat dry.

The section of the N1 road near the border town of Elubo is very new: it has dark and unblemished asphalt, a very crisp-looking middle line, and no outer lines. The vegetation is dense and occasionally features palm trees. NOTE: This new road surface continues until the town of Azuleti. The middle line can be dashed or solid. Near Azuleti, the road does not have a middle line.

The Keta Lagoon in the southeast of Ghana can be seen on the road that runs along it, with the lake being most visible in the northern section. You can sometimes see grey rocks on the side of the road. The soil is quite sandy in comparison to the rest of the country, and it should have a coastal feel.

metas.title: Greece
metas.description: Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > Detailed guy with no hat: Greece. Note that Greece's icon has hair that may almost look like a hat but it's just hair. Kinda looks like the Dame Tu Cosita guy

general_rules.text: Greek area codes will always begin with a 2, followed by 1-3 digits determining the area. NOTE: If the third digit is 1, you will be in the largest city of the region, and if the third digit is 9, you will be in the area surrounding that city.

Coverage.text: Greece is a country with many small islands, some with coverage and some without. Furthermore, while mainland Greece and Crete have all three camera generations, this will not be true for most islands. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Flatvalleys.text: The largest flat agricultural valleys in Greece are found close to Thessaloniki and Larissa, but smaller flat valleys, where the mountains generally appear closer, can be found in several other areas in the north and centre of the country.

Westernmountains.text: The tallest Greek mountains are found in the western half of the country, and contain most of the country’s high-altitude mountain roads with coverage.

Whitebluehouse.text: One of the most well-known types of Greek architecture; houses with completely white walls, blue doors and shutters, is mainly found on the small central Cyclade islands.

Centralislandslandscape.text: On many of the central islands you can find a very barren landscape, with small bushes and no trees in sight. This tends to be more common on the smaller islands with coverage.

Oliveplantations.text: Olive plantations are found in coastal areas, particularly on Crete and southern Peloponnese.

Citrus.text: Citrus plantations are mainly found in coastal areas, particularly on southern Peloponnese.

Creteantenna.text: On Crete, you may find this unique car antenna, with a slight bulge at the tip.

spotlight.text: Mount Pangaion can be recognised from its shape, being more of a solitary mountain rather than a wide mountain range, combined with the fact that it is located to the south of a flat agricultural valley.
These extraordinary monolithic mountains are called Meteora, and can be found north of Trikala.
Yellow taxis are found in Athens.
Blue taxis with a white roof are found in Thessaloniki.
In Thessaloniki, you will often see a large amount of unusually tall antennas on top of buildings.

GL.name: Greenland
GL.key_meta: Coverage in Greenland was taken with many different vehicles.

metas.title: Vibes
metas.description: Coverage in Greenland was taken with many different vehicles. Architecture and landscape look very similar all over Greenland but it's hard to put it in words but it's pretty recognizable that's why I included it in this map.

metas.title: Colorful Wooden Houses
metas.description:
Greenlandic architecture mainly consists of small, colourful, simple looking wooden houses, which even in cities are typically placed quite sparsely.
The major cities have some larger buildings, which normally look fairly minimalistic.

Trekker.text: Important note: not every single Greenlandic town and trekker is covered by a tip in the subsequent sections. All major towns are included however.

Nuuk.text: While Nuuk is most easily recognized by the grey Street View car, it can also be recognized by being the largest city by far.

Sisimiut.text: The city of Sisimiut can be easily recognized by the black snowmobile with side mirrors pointing straight up. The coverage is generally very overcast and grey.

Ilulissat.text: Most coverage in Ilulissat can be recognized by the green ATV with black bars and the driver wearing a beige hat. Note however that there are some small sections where the driver does not wear it. The coverage is fairly sunny and bright.

Qaqortoq.text: Qaqortoq can be recognized by the red rectangular car. The coverage is extremely sunny and the area is greener and less barren than most of the country.

Aasiaat.text: The most noticeable feature of the coverage in Aasiaat is the windshield with a shiny red, white and black reflection. The large, round side mirrors can also be used to identify the town. The coverage is very sunny and has thick, thawing snow along most of the roads.

Tasiilaq.text: The coverage in Tasiilaq can be recognized by the ATV with large grey handguards on either side. The coverage has a lot of very thin clouds and the area is somewhat green.

Uummannaq.text: Uummannaq has two distinctive features: a sharp mountain to the north and a green snowmobile with large black side mirrors. Neither of the two can be seen on all coverage but at least one can be seen on most.

Narsaq.text: Narsaq can be identified by the thin antenna seen on the right side of the car. The coverage is very sunny and fairly green.

Boatwestcoast1.text: This boat, with a white cabin and a red roof, can be found by a multitude of towns and villages on the west coast. However, most of the coverage is in the general area around the city of Aasiaat.

Boatwestcoast2.text: Similar to the previous boat, this one with a red square cabin can be found at multiple locations on the west coast, most significantly by and around Akunnaaq.

Boatittoqqortoormiit.text: A boat with a black box near the front, and a chequered pattern on the bow can be found fairly north on the east coast. While the western part of the coverage is very foggy and somewhat overcast, the eastern parts of the coverage is slightly less foggy and very sunny. A man wearing a black coat can also be seen captaining the boat.

Boattiilerilaaq.text: This bright red boat can be found on the east coast near the towns of Tiilerillaq and Kuummiit respectively. While the coverage near Tiilerillaq does not have a cloud in sight, the coverage near Kuummiit is somewhat overcast.

spotlight.text: The coverage in Maniitsoq was taken by a tractor, making it very recognizable. The coverage is overcast and fairly snowy.

The coverage in Narsarsuaq can be recognized by the driver wearing a black hoodie. The coverage was taken close to sunset on a very sunny day. There is also a fair amount of small bushes along the road, which is somewhat unusual in Greenland.

On the other side of the fjord from Narsarsuaq, a black ATV with an orange and purple bag in the front can be seen. The coverage has a lot of tall green grass and the dirt is unusually red for Greenland.
Qeqertarsuaq is most easily recognized by the blue ATV with wide side mirrors. The coverage is fairly overcast and with a lot of yellow grass along the roads.

Most coverage in Ittoqqortoormiit can be recognized by the brown wooden box at the front of the ATV and the driver wearing a purple beanie. The ground is mostly grey and stony and the coverage is very sunny.

The coverage in and around Igaliku is most easily recognized by the wide, snow-covered mountain range to the northeast which looks very bright due to the setting sun. The green ATV, while not entirely unique on its own, can also be a useful hint.

Paamiut can typically be recognized by the round, grey car which is often only barely visible. The coverage has a lot of thin clouds, but is still quite bright and the foliage consists of a mixture of yellow and green grass, and reddish moss.

Kangerlussuaq can typically be recognized by the many streaky clouds in the sky, combined with the significant dryness. The roads near Kangerlussuaq can also be recognized by its unconventional look, with many small bushes, sandy soil with an almost arid climate.
The road east of Kangerlussuaq is easily recognized by the large white truck.

The coverage connecting Sisimiut and Kangerlussuaq is easily recognized by the thick layer of snow on and around the road. The sun sets along the road, making the western parts very bright and the eastern parts very dark.

To the north of Saattut you can see a wide mountain range shrouded in clouds, on the other side of a fjord. The paths covered are mostly dark, muddy dirt roads, and the foliage is mainly yellow grass tufts.
The coverage on Kulusuk island has a round, red ATV, with a pyramid shaped mountain often seen to the northeast. The footage was taken right after sunset on a clear day, making it fairly dark.
Kangaatsiaq has a large amount of thawing snow on the side of the roads. The sun is setting and there is a large body of water to the west.
Ikerasak is most easily recognized by the large monolithic mountain to the west.
Ukkusissat is located below a tall cliffside to the east with mountains towering above it.
Kuummiit can be recognized by two distinct mountains, a sharp one to the east and a rounder one to the north. The coverage is slightly dark due to clouds and the sun setting.

Unlike most houses in Greenland, the houses in Tiilerilaaq are commonly grey rather than colourful. The village can also be recognized by the ground, which is almost entirely made up of smooth, light grey rocks.
Large, dark grey rocks towering over Niaqornat can be used to recognize the village.

Siorapaluk can be recognized by the sandy, pyramid-shaped mountains to the north, combined with the wide sand beach below the village. NOTE: Look for the store named “Pilersuisoq” to locate the village, as you have to zoom in very far on Google Maps to see the label of the village.

To the southwest of Qaanaaq, you can see icebergs in a large body of water, and a wide mountain range on the other side, where the snow is bright white as it reflects the sunlight through the thick clouds.
A red and black ATV can be found in and around the village of Kapisillit, northeast of Nuuk. Many mountains in the distance are covered in a layer of snow.
Kangerluk can be recognized by the evenly tall mountains with a particular shape on the other side of the fjord.

On a small bit of coverage east of Nuuk you can see a large number of sharp mountains, powdered in snow. The coverage is somewhat dark due to the thick clouds and the sun being hidden behind the mountains.
About 20 km northeast of Narsarsuaq, you can find a small piece of coverage with large ice blocks in every direction.
In Upernavik, the airport runway is covered on Street View, making it by far the widest paved road found on Street View in Greenland.
A black and white boat, with a blue roof, is found between the towns of Kuummiit and Tasiilaq.
This small white boat, with a brown wooden top and lights and monitoring devices, can be seen between Tiilerilaaq and Tasiilaq.
A small, rounded red bow can be found on a boat going south of Tasiilaq.
This small, red and black boat, with multiple people sitting in it, can be found in a fjord far north on the east coast.
This wooden fishing boat is found outside Ilulissat.

This small, white boat with a silver handrail on the bow can be found west of Narsaq and east of Qaqortoq. While the sun is in the west on the coverage near Narsaq, it is in the east on the coverage near Qaqortoq.
This large, all white boat can be seen in between Narsarsuaq with the opposing shore.
A grey boat is found east of Nuuk.
A mostly white boat, with extremely tall antennas on the rear can be found going into the fjord east of Nuuk.

metas.title: Alto
metas.description: Guatemala, Panama, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Stop Signs

metas.title: Pastel Stone Houses
metas.description:
Guatemalan architecture mainly consists of pastel painted stone houses, commonly with rusted sheet metal roofs.
It is also somewhat common for buildings to be made out of exposed white brick.

general_rules.text: Phone numbers starting with a 2 are unique to Guatemala City.

Similarly, phone numbers starting with a 6 are unique to the Guatemala Department. NOTE: Phone numbers starting with 7 are found anywhere except for Guatemala Department, and phones starting with 3, 4 or 5 can be found anywhere in the country.

Coverage.text: Guatemala has a fairly low amount of coverage, particularly in the north. Here you can see which roads are covered.

Topography.text: This is a topographic map of Guatemala. Generally speaking, the middle of the country is mountainous, while the south and north are fairly flat.

Flatsouth.text: The southern regions of Guatemala mainly consist of completely flat agricultural land. It is generally more built up than flat areas in the north.

Mountainousmiddle.text: The central regions of Guatemala are generally mountainous.

Semiflatnorth.text: The northern regions of Guatemala are typically fairly flat. You will however usually see some hills or a slightly rolling landscape, rather than the complete flatness of the south.

Oilpalm.text: Oil palm plantations are primarily found in two general areas: in the southwest and just north of the central mountain range.

Greenpoles.text: Completely green utility poles are primarily found in the southeast of the country, but also on a road in the further north in the east and on a small stretch of road around Melchor de Mencos, near the end of the coverage in the far northeast. These poles also feature small pole plates, which can further narrow down the road. This will be further explained in the next tip.

Poleplate.text: Most green utility poles contain a white pole plate, for which the top two characters will determine which road you are on. These roads and their corresponding characters are shown in this infographic.

Carbarforward.text: In most of the Guatemala coverage, the top right bar will be facing forward. This means that you can see this line on the side facing forward.

Backwards.text: The opposite is true in southeastern Guatemala, where the line is facing backwards.

Blueropecar.text: In these regions, you can often see a blue rope on the bottom right bar. NOTE: Sometimes it can be hard or almost impossible to see, in which case it might look like a normal backward facing bar.

Carbarbackwardnocap.text: These regions in the south and northeast also have the backwards facing bar. The difference here is that the bottom right bar is missing the thin black cap, which is present in the other regions.

spotlight.text: Lago de Atitlán is by far the largest lake in the mountainous regions of Guatemala. It is surrounded by mountains, and some volcanoes.
A small dirt road in the middle of a dense jungle can be found north of Tikal, in the far north of the country.
These small white bollards with two black stripes can be found on road 1 northeast of Quetzaltenango.
The PET-11, south of Las Pozas can be recognised by the slightly rolling landscape combined with its completely north-to-south road angle.
The CA9, going between Escuintla and the coast, can be recognised by being a divided highway with concrete pavement.

A trekker featuring several Mayan temples can be found just west of the town of Tikal. It is worth mentioning that while there are other Guatemalan trekkers featuring Mayan ruins, this is by far the most prominent and contains the largest and most intact temple structures.
These white rectangular stickers that have the word ‘electricista’ written on them are unique to Guatemala City.

HK.name: Hong Kong
HK.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (10 regions covered).

Apple.text: A double-decker tram line runs along the north of Hong Kong Island. A full map of the route can be seen here. NOTE: Make sure not to mistake this tram for the red MTR railway line, which has some sections above ground.

Very.text: The northwestern part of the New Territories is served by a distinct light rail system. It can be recognised by its green-and-orange platforms, single-level train cars and the fact that the tracks are separated from the street.

Momn.text: Mong Kok and the surrounding districts in Kowloon can be recognized by the crowded, busy, gridded streets, with apartment blocks situated above the shops. NOTE: These buildings are usually older, which means there will be a lack of glass walls (as opposed to parts of Hong Kong Island which feature more glass).

Wateh.text: The north-western area near the Mainland China border is mostly flat and features a patchwork of waterlogged rice paddies. The Shenzhen skyline is visible in the distance, to your north.

What.text: The Central District can be recognized by the large concentration of modern skyscrapers. The district feels quite busy, affluent and well-kept, with lots of luxury brand stores and ads.

File.text: You can use these two skyscrapers to determine whether you are on the Kowloon or Hong Kong Island side. The IFC is on the Hong Kong Island side and the ICC is on the Kowloon side. The ICC has straighter edges and looks more like a cuboid, while the IFC is rounder. The IFC will also have noticeable vertical window frames, while the ICC has none.

Hose.text: Mid-Levels is a residential district that is easily recognized by the non-identical tall modern apartments and hilliness.

Neck.text: The residential district of Sai Wan Ho has a lot of identical white and brown apartment blocks, and tall glass office buildings.

Construkshin.text: Chek Lap Kok Island and the Boundary Crossing Facilities can be recognized by the various large scale construction works going on in the area. From the outside, it can be identified by the many bridges that connect other parts of Hong Kong to the two islands.

Why.text: The residential district of Caribbean Coast and Tung Chung has identical apartment blocks that face the same direction, almost like a “wall” of buildings. There are a lot of planted palm trees in between and on the side of roads.

spotlight.text: The Tsing Ma Bridge can be recognized by being the only major suspension bridge in Hong Kong. The bridge has two ladder-like support towers, and yellow and red guardrails.

Ting Kau Bridge, a cable-stayed bridge connecting Ting Kau and Tsing Yi, can be identified by the generally clean asphalt and newer condition, three cylindrical support towers, hangers coming directly from the towers themselves, and yellow paint seen in the median and on the outsides.

While similar to the Ting Kau Bridge, the cable-stayed Stonecutters Bridge can be identified by the lack of yellow paint, and its box beam guardrail design, as opposed to the cable design seen on the other two bridges.
Lung Wo Road can be recognized by the Hong Kong Island skyline to the south and the Kowloon skyline to the north. The road is also in good condition and the sidewalks are clean.

The Tai Chung Kiu Road is a divided road that runs in a north-east direction, and has views of the Shing Mun River to the west. The median has palm trees. In addition, a bicycle path runs alongside the road. Further north, Route 2 also runs alongside the river, but this road has more lanes.

Fan Kam Road runs in a general north-east direction, and can be recognized by the dense tropical vegetation surrounding the road, and sometimes mountains in the background. The road is also quite narrow and does not have any outer lines. Many small villages branch off of the road, south and north of the country park.

Lam Kam Road is similar to Fan Kam Road, however it runs in a more east-west direction. The road should also feel busier with more cars driving along the road and more houses on the sides of the road. In addition, the road is usually wider and a median containing trees can be seen separating sidewalks near the villages.

The Kai Tak Cruise Terminal can mainly be seen from the Eastern Corridor, north of Tsat Tsz Mui, and from the Kwun Tong bypass south-west of Kwun Tong. The cruise terminal can be recognized by its shiny, cylindrical appearance, with triangular windows along the side.

The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge can be seen from the South Perimeter Road, on Chek Lap Kok Island. Its length stretches into the horizon, spanning across the ocean. The road itself can be recognized by the black and yellow concrete barriers on either side.
The roads going to Disneyland are divided, with palm trees along the side of the road with teal coloured street lamps.

Between Hong Kong Island and Lantau Island, there are three unique islands: Peng Chau, Cheung Chau and Lamma Island, with trekker coverage. These islands can be identified by the lack of cars, narrow streets, and rural architecture. Lamma Island is also the hilliest of the three.
The Lugard Road trekker around Victoria Peak can be recognized by the distinct black guardrail, view of the skyline and tourists walking along the path.

They are similar to those in Poland and Romania, but Polish poles have holes that don't go all the way to the top or bottom, and Romanian poles are usually wider and painted white at the bottom.

metas.title: Bollard

Hungarian chevrons are white on red.
Black-and-white chevrons may also be seen, but are considerably less common.

These green kilometre markers can be seen along most Hungarian roads.

metas.description: White Belt: Croatia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Pointed Shoes: Germany, Hungary. > Germany Belt: Above hip. Hungary Belt: Bottom of hip. Germany arm: Flat side on left. Hungary arm: Flat side on right.

metas.title: Red Tiles Roofs & Light Colors
metas.description:
Hungarian houses are typically made of stone, painted in a light colour and almost always with red tiled roofs.
Suburban houses are typically only one storeyed, while more central houses may be taller.
Houses in town and city centres are often fairly old but well-kept.

general_rules.text: Hungarian phone numbers consist of either 8 or 10 digits. If the number has 8 digits, the first and second digit is the area code. And if the number has 10 digits, the third and fourth digit is the area code. The only exception is Budapest, where only the first or third digit, being a 1, respectively is the area code. NOTE: Area codes whose second digit is 0 or 1 are not region specific.
The first digit of Hungarian numbered roads are ordered in a circle, centred around Budapest. Remembering this system should make it quite easy to find any numbered road.

Budapest.text: If you see a blue or green street sign shaped like an arrow, attached to a utility pole or street light, you are likely to be in the county of Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg. NOTE: Blue arrow-shaped street signs can also be found in Dunakeszi, north of Budapest. However, those are attached to blue sign posts.

metas.title: Landscape - Flat-Topped Mountains
metas.description: The Westfjords region features numerous narrow fjords, surrounded by moderately tall, and mostly flat-topped mountains.

metas.title: Landscape - Fog
metas.description: Very foggy coverage can be found around the town of Bakkagerði, in northeastern Iceland. The fog can also be seen from a distance.

metas.title: Landscape - Glaciers
metas.description: The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive glaciers visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the Vatnajökull ice cap.

metas.title: Car Meta - Red Truck
metas.description: Iceland can be split in half depending on the colour of the pickup truck, with red being found in the southwest, and white being found in the northeast.
metas.comparison: The Red Truck is found between Sudurland and Vesturland

metas.title: Landscape - Large Jagged Mountains
metas.description: The far east of the country is also home to several fjords. What distinguishes them from the Westfjords are the generally larger and more jagged mountains.

metas.title: Landscape - Akureyri Mountains
metas.description: The mountains west of Akureyri contain many valleys, sandwiched between tall, often slightly snowcapped peaks. Most of these valleys generally face north to northeast.

metas.title: Landscape - Eiðar Valley
metas.description: The wide valley around Eiðar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, snowy peaks visible in the distance on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.

metas.title: Landscape - Southwest Farmland
metas.description: The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat farmland landscape scattered with numerous farmsteads, fields, meadows and grasslands.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Although there are other smaller agricultural areas in Iceland, mountains in this area tend to be quite distant, making it unique.

metas.title: Landscape - Selfoss Mountain
metas.description: You can recognise the area near the town of Selfoss from its distinct flat-ridge mountain. Due to the otherwise flat landscape, this mountain can be seen from a wide area.

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description:
Iceland has unique yellow bollards with a white reflector.
These bollards are extremely common and can be found throughout the country on almost every section of rural road.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: Iceland has unique yellow bollards with a white reflector. These bollards are extremely common and can be found throughout the country on almost every section of rural road.

metas.title: Landscape - Heimaey
metas.description: The Island of Heimaey can easily be recognised by seeing these ragged rocky cliffs overlooking the town of Vestmannaeyjabær. Similar cliffs can be seen on the islands off the coast.

metas.title: Landscape - Inland Iceland
metas.description: Barren landscapes consisting mostly of dark volcanic gravel, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.

metas.title: Landscape - Akureyri
metas.description: Akureyri is the second-biggest city in Iceland and is located in a North-South oriented valley, along the western edge of the bay. The city features mountains ranges to the east and west, making it recognisable.

metas.title: Landscape - Hallormsstaður Valley
metas.description: The valley around Hallormsstaður has a distinct northeast/southwest angle with low-lying mountains on either side, a wide river flowing through it, and an unusual amount of trees for Iceland. Some of the sideroads are in the forests.

metas.title: Landscape - Reykjavík
metas.description: Reykjavík is the capital and by far the largest city in Iceland. The city is mostly flat with slight hills, and is located on the south side of a bay. It is most recognizable as it is significantly larger than other Icelandic cities, with a large urban area and “bigger city” feel.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The city of Akureyri can feel urban in some places. You can distinguish it from Reykjavik as it has mountains to the east and west.

metas.title: Landscape
metas.description:
Iceland is a very geologically active country, where plate tectonics and volcanic processes have shaped the landscape.
As a result, many regions are rugged, mountainous and a sight to behold.
In addition, strange and bewildering landscapes can be found all over, such as geothermal lakes, lava fields, rift valleys, and towering rock formations.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

general_rules.text: Iceland has a very sensible road numbering system that allows for quick 5k’s, provided you find the yellow direction signs that list the road numbers of the intersection you are on. The main ring road, which circles the entire island, simply has the number 1. There are no other roads that start with 1. The first digit of the other road numbers is region-specific. These regions have a sequential distribution around the island, starting from 2 in the south and increasing up until 9 in a clockwise direction (see map for approximate distribution).

Coverage.text: Iceland is rather sparsely covered. The southwest region has the densest coverage. Only a few interior roads are covered. You can click on the image to enlarge it. Alternatively, you can look at the coverage in more detail on this site.

Westfjords.text: The Westfjords region features numerous narrow fjords, surrounded by moderately tall, and mostly flat-topped mountains.

Eastfjords.text: The far east of the country is also home to several fjords. What distinguishes them from the Westfjords are the generally larger and more jagged mountains.

Valleys.text: The mountains west of Akureyri contain many valleys, sandwiched between tall, often slightly snowcapped peaks. Most of these valleys generally face north to northeast.

Middl.text: Barren landscapes consisting mostly of dark volcanic gravel, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.

Southwest.text: The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat farmland landscape scattered with numerous farmsteads, fields, meadows and grasslands. NOTE: Although there are other smaller agricultural areas in Iceland, mountains in this area tend to be quite distant, making it unique.

Eibar.text: The wide valley around Eiðar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, snowy peaks visible in the distance on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.

Forested.text: The valley around Hallormsstaður has a distinct northeast/southwest angle with low-lying mountains on either side, a wide river flowing through it, and an unusual amount of trees for Iceland. Some of the sideroads are in the forests.

Selfoss.text: You can recognise the area near the town of Selfoss from its distinct flat-ridge mountain. Due to the otherwise flat landscape, this mountain can be seen from a wide area.

spotlight.text: The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive glaciers visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the Vatnajökull ice cap.

There are only a handful of highways in Iceland which are either divided or have more than two lanes. The divided highways are shown in dark red, while the highways with three or more lanes are shown in bright red. NOTE: There are two exceptions to this: Divided roads can be found inside cities other than Reykjavík. Divided roads can be found inside cities other than Reykjavík. Roads may temporarily be divided close to intersections.
The Island of Heimaey can easily be recognised by seeing these ragged rocky cliffs overlooking the town of Vestmannaeyjabær. Similar cliffs can be seen on the islands off the coast.

Very foggy coverage can be found around the town of Bakkagerði, in northeastern Iceland. The fog can also be seen from a distance. To report inaccuracies, suggest new clues or give general feedback about our content, please use this form: https://www.plonkit.net/feedback

metas.title: Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles & Thatched Roofs

metas.title: Northeast - Square Panels

metas.title: Car Meta - Flower Car

metas.description: Since Imphal is located in a valley, it is fairly simple to recognize it after a few games.
metas.comparison: The landscape around the city consists of agricultural fields surrounded by mountains, so it is pretty easy to know you are in Imphal.

metas.title: Car Meta - NH179B Car
metas.description: This car has an antenna with some kind of a spring. It basically goes from Salem to Chennai.

metas.title: Car Meta - Haryal Car
metas.description: This car is unique to Haryal, PB. It looks similar to the boxy car, but with a rounded front.

metas.title: Landscape - Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary
metas.description: Unique hilly landscape with dead trees. Note that not all coverage in this park looks like this.

metas.title: Landscape - NH3 between Gramphu and Dalang
metas.description:
This section of road  features huge mountains, with a little bit more **green on their slopes.
**

metas.title: Car - Kuno National Park Car
metas.description: This car has a back curving bar, but is mostly blurred. It can be found east of Kuno National Park

metas.title: Landscape - Amygdaloidal Basalt
metas.description: This is a volcanic rock, which is recognizable by it's dark color with white mineral patches on it.
metas.comparison: It is mostly found between Pune and Jalgaon. It's important to note that this rock alone, without the mineral patches is more widely spread.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Pole Band
metas.description: A section of the NH13 west of Roing has poles marked with white numbers on blue, red or black paint.

metas.title: Misc - Lungi
metas.description: People wearing a Lungi, which looks like a towel wrapped around the waist, are more common in South India.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Concrete Blocks
metas.description: Concrete blocks, similar to those you see in Bhutan, are commonly found in (but not limited to) North-East India

metas.title: Landscape - Spiti River Valley
metas.description: The shape of the mountains iin this valley are truly unique : very dry, very high in elevation and sparsely green.
metas.comparison: If you have trouble making the difference between this road and the NH3 to the west because it looks roughly similar, just know that the NH3 is paved whilst the Spiti river valley roads usually are not.

metas.title: Landscape - Rewa Ridge
metas.description: A pretty straight east-west range with a slight north east angle can be found near Rewa. It is fairly easy to recognize.

metas.title: Vegetation - Euphorbia Neriifolia (Hilly Landcape)
metas.description: South of Udaipur, you can find a very distinct landscape with narrow hills and a lot of this type of cactus (Euphorbia).

metas.title: Landscape - Ladakh - Snow Coverage
metas.description: Coverage extends to roads that are very high in altitude, so snow can be visible on the end of the streetview east of Leh.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Hyderabad Mesh Pole
metas.description: Mesh pole with three wires on one or both sides, that are connected to the pole in a "pyramid shaped" extension on the side.
metas.comparison: Note that it has to be a pole, not a cellphone tower (which would be a lot larger). Found around Hyderabad, TG

metas.title: Vegetation - Palmyra Palms
metas.description: Palmyra Palms have a round crown with fan shaped leaves and a trunk with consistent thickness, giving them a lollipop shape.
metas.comparison: They appear mostly in 3 areas: They are also common in

metas.title: Car Meta - Mechuka Car
metas.description: Mechuka features a unique car in Arunachal. It can be found in the valley and on the road leading to it from Along on the NH13.

metas.title: Car Meta - Rewa Car
metas.description: This car has a back curving bar at the front and white bars on the side. It's found mostly around Rewa, but also around Raipura.

metas.title: Vegetation - Doum Palm
metas.description: Doum palms, which appear similar to Palmyra palms but with multiple branches, are almost exclusive to the union territory of Diu.

metas.title: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Red Car
metas.description: The red front blur can be found on Andrott. Sometimes, the same car has a bit different blur, where there's some exposed red visible.
metas.comparison: Note that Andrott can also have the big circular blur where you see no car.

metas.title: Car Meta - Satpura National Park Car
metas.description: This car has a back-curving bar and a singular black bar. It's found mainly east of Satpura National Park, and sometimes around Raipura.

metas.title: Architecture - Red Brick
metas.description: While Red Brick can be found anywhere in India, there is a notable concentration in the Ganges River Valley, especially towards the West.

metas.title: Architecture - Shimla Vibes
metas.description: Shimla is definitely the place in the Himalayas with the biggest amount of bright green and bright red roofs (and architecture in general).
metas.comparison: Note by MB: It also spams Himalayan Cedars.

metas.title: Car Meta - Open Trunk
metas.description:
In the eastern parts of Ajmer, RJ, you can sometimes see an open trunk in Smallcam.
It can be found north of Shrinagar/west of Circular Rd.

metas.title: Central - Rounded Roof Tiles
metas.description:
Rounded roof tiles are common in central India.
They often appear disorganised and are kept in rows/columns that are not completely straight.

metas.title: Architecture - Dumka House
metas.description: Houses between Dumka and Pakur have long tiled roofs and walls are painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom

metas.title: Infrastructure - Seperated Bus Lane
metas.description: On large roads in Ahmedabad and Surat you can find separated middle lanes for buses. Beware that people will still often drive in these lanes.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Andaman Horizontal Bar Poletop
metas.description: Pole tops in Andaman mostly consist of horizontal bars perpendicular to the pole. They are not 100% unique to Andaman, but are very common there.

metas.title: Coverage Meta - Andaman Vibes
metas.description: Andaman Islands are remote Islands that have their own distinct vegetation. It is covered in areca palm forests and the roads are often very thin.
metas.comparison: Andaman has been covered using a camera with maxed out saturation somehow. The result is these very bright/white colors.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Harsil Road
metas.description: On the road south of Harsil (UK), you will find a large amount of poles with red/yellow stripes and black bollards with stripes (see UK/JH bollard)

metas.title: Landscape - Badvel Valley
metas.description: Wind turbines aligned on top of mountain ranges are very common in these mountain ranges valleys I would say. (I know there are some in RJ as well)
metas.comparison: Even without wind turbines, you can click in this valley if you have a good north/south angle. I would even say that it is the only place in India with such big N/S dry ranges to the west AND to the east. Differentiations:

metas.title: Infrastructure - Andaman Black Sticker
metas.description: These black paint can be circular or square, features 2 letters, an arrow beneath, and some numbers beneath that and can be on metal/concrete poles.
metas.comparison: They're found mostly near the capital (Port Blair/Sri Vijaya Puram) (95%) and rarely near Diglipur (5%)

The flag of UPPL is yellow white green with a farmer on a tractor on it.
Found in Bodoland, which consists of the Assamese districts bordering Bhutan.

metas.description: From the city of Sukma to the border with Andra Pradesh, the NH30 has yellow road lines and is made of concrete. (Kinda similar to the famous Ruta 9 in Chile)

metas.title: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Exposed Black
metas.description: This car with an exposed black front is unique to Kiltan. Note that the front is always exposed on Kiltan, if it's blurred (even partly), it's not the Kiltan car.

metas.title: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Adidas Car
metas.description: The "Adidas Car" is characterized by the black stripes on the white car front. Sometimes it has a visible side mirror. It also often has a visible bar at the back.
metas.comparison: It is exclusive to the island of Amini

metas.title: Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Lampe Circles
metas.description: The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as round yellow markings on street lights.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.title: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred Black Front
metas.description: This car with the subtle black blur at the front is found in Kalpeni. The blur can be very subtle sometimes, and is confusable with the blurred white edges on Agatti.
metas.comparison: Sometimes the same car has a slightly different blur, where the edges are exposed. Kalpeni can also have a big circular blur, so don't rule out Kalpeni if you don't see this car.

metas.title: Landscape - Chaukhamba
metas.description: Chaukhamba, located near the town of Ukhimath, is a mountain massif covered in snow which can be recognised by its three distinct peaks, with the centre peak being the tallest.

metas.title: Language - Bengali
metas.description: Bengali is found in northeastern India and has a similar look to Devanagari (Hindi), however it can usually be recognised by the many letters featuring left-facing triangular shapes.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This is also the language found in Bangladesh.

metas.title: Landscape - Himachal Pradesh - North/South Valley
metas.description: The city of Manali is fairly recognizable due to it being one of the two areas with coverage in a recognizable north-south valley. The other is from Kullu to Nagwain 50 km south of it.
metas.comparison: The only way I came up with to tell the 2 apart is the vegetation but this is kinda fake since both cities are located in the same valley. According to me, Manali has poplar trees and pines within the city whereas the other area doesn’t have much of those and mostly consists of random trees.

metas.title: Landscape - Tirupati
metas.description:
The city of Tirupati, AP can easily be recognized by the huge ridge in the North.
Other metas, like black&yellow Tuk-Tuks, two-indent poles or simply Telugu language, can help confirm.

metas.title: Landscape - Elevated Jammu & Kashmir
metas.description: While a lot of the coverage in Jammu is located in flat parts, there are some areas north and northeast of the city of Jammu with elevation, where you will be able to see a lot of pines.

metas.title: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Exposed Front
metas.description: This car with an exposed white front is found of Kadmat. This car can be confused with others: It's not the Kadmat car if it has a visible side mirror. It's also not the Kadmat car if the front is blurred.

metas.title: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Big Blur
