metas.title: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred White Edges
metas.description:
This car is mostly blurred and has subtle white edges at the front. It's found on the island of Agatti.
Sometimes the edges are so subtle that you can overlook them and confuse it with the Kalpeni car (which has a subtle black blur)

metas.title: Landscape - Mechuka Valley
metas.description: The Mechuka valley is the only place in Northeast India where snowy mountains are visible. The valley contains brownish grass and a plethora of Bhutan white pine. North of Mechuka the coverage gradually becomes overcast and somewhat dark.

metas.title: Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Car with Mirror
metas.description: This car is the most likely to encounter if you get Lakshadweep. It has a white front and always a bit of mirror visible on the left. Sometimes a part of the mirror is blurred, but you can always see at least a bit of it exposed. This car is so common because it's on the main island of Lakshadweep, Kavaratti.

metas.title: Vegetation - Macaranga Peltata
metas.description: Parasol leaf tree (Macaranga peltata) is common along the southwestern coast anywhere south of Mumbai and seems to be virtually exclusive to that area, I have yet to find it anywhere else in India. To identify it, look for the teardrop shape of the leaves and the spot where the leaf stem connects to the inner part of the leaf blade.

Madhya Pradesh.text:
It has “U” shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.

It’s very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.
Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A slightly below the top of the pole.
Flat tiles seem to be the worst type of tile by their appearance. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar pradesh.
Upside down triangle poletops placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.
Slate roofs in Madhya Pradesh can be found west of Sagar
Found only in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.
U tiles are more common in the eastern half of Madhya Pradesh.

A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid.

80% Chhattisgarh
10% Maharashtra
3% Karnataka
2% Odisha
1% each: Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present. Northeast India also has some trapezoid poletops that look a bit different.

Found in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chattisgarh, sometimes in Odisha.

Don't confuse with Duraton Cement.

32% Maharashtra
32% Madhya Pradesh
32% Chattisgarh
1% Andhra Pradesh
1% Telangana

It has a “U” shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.

It’s very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.
Within Madhya Pradesh, a reddish or pinkish soil is generally more common towards the East.
W tiles are quite rare in Madhya Pradesh but can still be seen west of Jabalpur and south of Guna

Found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes also in Uttar Pradesh or Madhya Pradesh.

Don't confuse this with Bangur Cement, which has a different distribution.
Within Madhya Pradesh, sugar cane can commonly be found southwest and northeast of the Satpura National Park.
This double smudge can be found in the central-northern parts of the Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh.

The BJP is a popular national party, and thus it's flags can be found everywhere. Their symbol is a lotus flower.

It is most popular in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha, so if you see a lot of BJP flags in one pano, you are likely to be in this belt.

Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A (∀) slightly below the top of the pole.

94% Madhya Pradesh
2% Jharkhand
1% each: Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu
In Madhya Pradesh, rock walls are very common around two national parks : Kuno National Park and Panna National Park
Houses with tiled roofs and blue painted walls are very common in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, a little less in Madhya Pradesh
Flat tiles can be spotted in random places in Madhya Pradesh, but mainly around Guna, Chhatarpur and Sagar in the center of the state.
W-Tiles are mostly found on the western coast and in Tamil Nadu, but it also goes further inland in western Madhya Pradesh and in Telangana.
Jainism is a pretty rare minority religion. Jainist symbols are found mostly in Maharashtra, then Gujarat and Rajasthan, then Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.
There are a few places where you can have elevation in Madhya Pradesh. The main elevation areas are around Yawal and satpura park, as well as south of Indore

Vertical bar at the poletop. It is attached to the pole with two short bars. Note that those bars are not at the end of the vertical bar, which would make it a ring pole (and change the distribution)

50% Chhattisgarh
30% Madhya Pradesh
15% Maharashtra
10% West Bengal

Large visible, square shaped cars can be found in all states northwest of Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, except for Madhya Pradesh. It can also be found in and around Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai.

Very similar to a second vertical bar, but it is attached to the pole on its ends, rather than in the middle, giving it a ring shape. What differentiates it from the big ring pole is that the bar isn't far away from the pole.

35% Maharashtra
35% Madhya Pradesh
20% Chhattisgarh
2% Rajasthan & Mizoram
1% Tripura

Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Gujarat uses a variety of poletops, some of which can be used to identify other states. Beware that holey poles generally take precedence over poletop metas. NOTE: They are rarely found in other states especially Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh.
Upside down triangle poletops placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.
Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A slightly below the top of the pole.

Assam.text: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90° angle can be found in Assam.
Assamese, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably ৰ and ৱ.
Within Assam, sugarcane is mainly found around Lanka
Hilliness in Assam is found mostly South or East of Nagaon.
If you see a back antenna in Assam, you're in the far east of the state.
Within Assam, you can find thatched roofs all the way north east in the state.
Within Assam, you can find corn between Guwahati and Nagaon, south of the river.

Commonly found everywhere, except for North East.
Within North-East, it is sometimes found in Assam.

The Karbi are an ethnic group that inhabit two districts in Assam, Karbi Anglong and West Karbi Anglong.

Their flag is rarely shown, but you can often find Karbi colors (dark red, black and white) in those districts.
Many roads in Assam are paved with these tiles. What makes it stand out is that it is also found on very rural roads.
Within Assam, Tea is mostly planted in the eastern and in the southern regions. There are also some patches in Western Assam.
This flag with this tool on an Indian background is found in Bodoland, which consists of the districts in Assam bordering Bhutan.
Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90° angle can be found in Assam.

Haryana.text: Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab(super common) and Haryana.

Electricity boxes what are mint green with small window-like squares are almost exclusive to Punjab.

You can rarely see them in Haryana

The northern part of Haryana is very green and agricultural.

Note by MB: Ganges River Valley in general looks like this, but I feel like this area is even greener and lusher, and it also has more sugarcane.
Electricity counters in Punjab are usually mint green with small window-like squares. They can rarely be seen in Haryana.

The western Ganges River Valley (Punjab/Haryana/Western UP) usually looks wetter and greener than the general Ganges River Valley. You can often see rice and sugarcane. Note that areas like this can still be found in other parts of the river valley, this is not a 100% meta
Electricity counters in Punjab are usually mint green with small window-like squares. They can rarely be seen in Haryana.
Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab and Haryana.

Bihar.text: Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.

Flag is green-white-green, the symbol is an arrow.

Found only in Bihar.

Within Bihar, you can find regular Wide W Tiles around Katihar.

Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
Within Bihar, tea plantations can be found in the far Northeast.
White painted clay huts are found in northwestern Bihar, northwest of Muzaffapur.
Woven walls, plastered with clay are found on the western half of the Bihar-Nepal border.
Pineapple is very uncommon in India, but if you see it, it's in Bihar in the corridor between Nepal and Bangladesh.
Wooden huts with sticks around can be found in the western half of Bihar, at a latitude between Patna and Muzaffarpur..
These huts that are made entirely out of hay, and have thatched roofs are found in Southwestern Bihar, mainly between Patna and Gaya.

The northern plains, also known as the Ganges River Valley, of India are very fertile with extremely flat and open agricultural fields.

Note by MB: Agriculture can be found in many parts of India. I think what sets apart these Northern Plains is the lack of palm trees (except for the occasional date palms and the Palmyra palm spam in Bihar).
This black-yellow-black pole painting (which is famous for appearing in Antioquia in Colo), can also be found in Eastern Bihar along the Ganges.
Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.

Gujarat.text: Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

Recognizable by the Lion Logo.
Found only in Gujarat.

Recognizable by the wavy triangle logo.
Found only in Gujarat.
Found in Gujarat, mainly at the southern peninsula (could be fake)
Found in Central and East India, in Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes in Gujarat.
Almost all poles in Gujarat are holey poles. Generic poles are only found sometimes in very far west Gujarat, near the border with Pakistan
Gujarati, found in Gujarat, has a script with several similarities to the Hindi script, however it notably lacks the horizontal line at the top of every word.
The NH51 in Gujarat is unique because it is lined with many dark metal poles (unlike most of Gujarat which has concrete holey poles). It is also divided and paved with concrete.

Tamil Nadu.text: Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.
The Tamil script is found in Tamil Nadu and has a distinct combination of curves, straight lines and 90° angles. Some letters also have diacritics shaped like dots.
Flag of a political party active only in Tamil Nadu
Flag of a political party only active in Tamil Nadu.
Within Tamil Nadu, date palms can be found in the North-East.

2 insulators on each side, with the top of the pole sticking out.

Found in Karnataka (94%)
and rarely in Tamil Nadu (4%) or Kerala (1%)
In Tamil Nadu, thatched roofs are more common south east of Thanjavur.
Blue and red flag with a Myanmar-style star, found only in Tamil Nadu.
A flat, bushy landscape with very red soil can be found in southern Tamil Nadu.

White and black stripes on the bottom of a pole are found in both Meghalaya and Tripura.

Note by MB: Don't confuse this with the Tamil Nadu polepainting, which is always white-black-white and further up on the pole.
Found everywhere, except for Himalayan states, North Eastern States, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

Sugar cane can be found in several areas, the two main ones being near Erode and Thiruvanamalai.

It is also findable in smaller areas between those two big areas, but it is still mainly a northern Tamil Nadu thing.
Black and red colored flag. Other objects in this colors are also commonly found in the state of Tamil Nadu.

U tiled roofs are quite rare in Tamil Nadu, but if you come across such roofs, it should be in the northeast.

It is possible to find some further down near Thanjavur, but it will more likely come with the combination of thatched roofs.
Mountains in Tamil Nadu can be found along the western border. Additionally, there's a lot of mountains west of Madurai and some east of Salem.
Tea plantations in India are mostly located in the northeast and in Kerala, but it spills in one particular area in Tamil Nadu northwest of Coimbatore
Near the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, you can find these large monolithic mountains, with huge exposed rocks. Several of these mountains can be seen from afar, especially the Magenthiragiri hills.

BJP is one of the most popular national parties in India. You can find its flags basically everywhere.
However, they are less popular in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, meaning their flags are rare there.

Their symbol is a lotus flower.

Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Odisha to Tamil Nadu tend to be made of dried palm fans.

In Tamil Nadu, you will often come across quite good looking houses, the most recognizable are the ones with W tiled roofs and blueish paint. The combination of the color and the tiles should be 95% Tamil Nadu, the remaining 5% being spill in bordering states.

W tiled roofs are pretty much everywhere but somewhat less common in the northeast and on the eastern coast, where U tiles can be found more commonly.

In poorer parts of the Ganges Valley it is common for villages to construct their own large chimneys to fire clay into bricks. These can be seen from far away and are a good clue for the Ganges Valley specifically, especially UP and Bihar. Note that they are also fairly common in the poorer eastern parts of Tamil Nadu.
Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.

Jharkhand.text: In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.
A car with an orange flag can be found in the Jharkhand north-east panhandle.
These elevated structures are found a lot of them between Hazaribagh and Ranchi in Jharkhand.
Elevated Roads (similar to Bangladesh), with a dry landscape, are common in and around Jharkhand.
U tiles are commonly found on the northwest of the state, on the borders with Jharkhand and Chhattsgarh.
This flag and this symbol stand for Sarnaism. They are very localized, found in Ranchi and in Southern Jharkhand.

In Bihar and Jharkhand you will see many ads with this man with a turban and a beard. He's usually accompanied by a hexagonal company logo and a yellow background.

Note by MB: This sounds ridiculous but he seems to be so popular that there are copycats of him with the same Turban/beard style. So if you see a different company logo, don't trust this.

In Jharkhand, you will very often see the combination of date palms (a lot of them) and palmyra palms. I think it is one of the best clues for getting Jharkhand because it’s pretty unique. I also saw a lot of that combination of palms in Telangana so be careful and look for text before guessing.
In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.

Andhra Pradesh.text: Poles divided in two sections, in a similar fashion to Brazilian poles, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid is most common in Chhattisgarh and somewhat common in Meghalaya, Tripura and Maharashtra, but can rarely be found in many other states.

NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present.

Telugu, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh has script with a lot of smooth curves and circles. It looks similar to Kannada language but you can see a lot of distinct "checkmarks" on top of the letters.

This pole extensions (above the pole) with 3 insulators

45% Andhra Pradesh
45% Telangana
9% Tamil Nadu

Commonly found in Kerala (especially with yellow stickers).

Note that there's also a version with the two indents, which is not found in Kerala, but in Andhra Pradesh.

Thick gray trapezoid, with two indents in the pole material.

97% Andhra Pradesh
Found in South India, especially in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

This black sticker usually just has few characters, often just a number.

35% Tamil Nadu
35% Andhra Pradesh
20% Telangana Note that it's a weak meta for Andhra over Telangana. Do not confuse for Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
Within Andhra Pradesh, thatched roofs can commonly be found in three places.

3 insulators in a horizontal line, or middle insulator slightly above others

88% Tamil Nadu
5% Bihar
3% Haryana
2% Uttar Pradesh
1.5% Andhra Pradesh

Coastal Andhra Pradesh is characterized by a flat, agricultural landscape with coastal bushes

50/50 Tip ! Similar bushes can also be found in Gujarat, but Gujarat will often have distinct holey poles or have a boxy car. Also, Gujarat will primarily have date palms whereas Andhra will have palmyra palms as the main occurrence in palm trees. The harder rounds in Andhra are the coastal, agricultural ones without any Palmyra or any pole. This basically becomes a 50/50 with any other flat & agricultural state.
Oil palm plantations are almost exclusive to Andhra Pradesh and are mostly located around Eluru.
If you see a Coconut, hedge in the south eastern half towards Andhra Pradesh, it has more of them.
This party is exclusive to Andhra Pradesh, and most popular in the South. Their symbol is a ceiling fan.

Two-section poles can sometimes be regionguessed by looking at the bar above the crossbar (which doesn't always exist).

If it's high on the pole (meaning you can barely see the concrete above it), it's 80% Telangana, 20% Andhra Pradesh (especially western) Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope

Yellow tuk tuks with black roofs are common in the southern Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

NOTE: They can also rarely be found elsewhere.
Auto Rickshaws with a Black Body and a Yellow Roof (i.e. reverse to the Andhra Pradesh / Telangana variant) are commonly found in Nagaland.
Houses with very "strong colors", such as dark yellow, pink, purple, are often found in Tamil Nadu, and sometimes in Kerala and Andhra Pradesh

Around Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, you can find a landscape that combines the Andhra Pradesh Panhandle and the agricultural east coast further south.

You will have lots of agriculture (more than in Panhandle) and also many palm trees (more than in the coastal region further south).

Telangana and Andra Pradesh have a lot of “rockiness”. It can be rocks on the side of the road, boulders or even rocky hill slopes but they share that in common.

I found it to be more in Telangana so the meta is here, but note that it can extend to surrounding states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Note by MB: In my experience, in AP, rockiness is very common west of the ridge from Tirupati to Nallamala Forest.
Telugu, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, has a script very similar to Kannada, but you’ll often see diacritics resembling checkmarks at the top of letters.

Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

AP stands for Andhra Pradesh. The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

Bridges in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are often recognizable by the color of their guardrails.
It is often made of vertical red/pink/orange concrete blocks with horizontal white/light yellow blocks.

INC is a popular national party, and found almost everywhere. The notable exceptions are West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, where the INC has regional versions, meaning you won't find any INC imagery there.

Their symbol is a flat hand facing you, on the background of the Indian tricolor.

Andhra Pradesh has a long coast along the bay of Bengal and it is fairly recognizable because of the red soil combined with overall flatness. This is the area in which you fill find red soil in Andhra Pradesh.

Flat landscape with red soil and lots of Palmyra should pretty much always give the eastern India coast.

The panhandle of Andhra Pradesh looks quite different than the rest of the state. It is much greener (and has an arguably "darker greener" tone). There are also A LOT more coconut palms here than anywhere else in AP.

Other parts of Andhra Pradesh do have Palmyra Palms, but Coconut palms are kinda rare outside of the panhandle. The area south of Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh can also look extremely similar, but it has a lot less coverage.

This is not something you will come across very often, but if you have a black car and don’t really know where to go/want to confirm your guess, black car is more common in Telangana/Andhra Pradesh, especially in Northern Telangana and Coastal AP.

In Karnataka (85%), and sometimes in Haryana (6%), Western Andhra Pradesh (6%) and rarely Uttar Pradesh (1%), you can find trident poletops on concrete poles where the central insulator is attached directly to the top of the pole, while the other two are attached to a horizontal crossbar positioned slightly further down. There are different variants of this poletop that increase the likelihood for Karnataka.

Note by MB: Make sure not to confuse it with the trident with a small bar at the top (see images).
Yellow tuk tuks with black roofs are common in the southern Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. NOTE: They can also rarely be found elsewhere.
Poles divided in two sections, in a similar fashion to Brazilian poles, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid is most common in Chhattisgarh and somewhat common in Meghalaya, Tripura and Maharashtra, but can rarely be found in many other states. NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present.
Oil palm plantations are most commonly found in the panhandle of Andhra Pradesh, especially near the eastern border with Telangana.

West Bengal.text:
This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.

It is very common in West Bengal, eastern Jharkhand and eastern Bihar, but doesn’t go further north than Purnia, Bihar.
Found in North-East India, West Bengal and sometimes Bihar.

Tea plantations can be found in the northeast and the far south.

NOTE: If you find tea plantations in a flat area, you are likely in Assam or northeastern West Bengal, near the Assam border.
Found in East India (i.e. Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha)
West Bengal only has E-Rickshaws. They have a unique shape and are often blue.
Within West Bengal, tea plantations are found near the northern border to Bhutan.
In the eastern parts of Jharkhand, you can find some West Bengal wide W tiles spill
The flag is green-white-yellow and can be found in West Bengal near the Sikkim Border.
Found in South India, however less common in Karnataka. Sometimes also found in West Bengal.

The flag of this party often has these flowers on some grass with the Indian flag as background.

It can be found mainly in West Bengal, however less commonly in the Northern Parts.
Sometimes it's also found in Western Meghalaya

Yellow - Grey - Dark Red Flag with a nice landscape in the middle and some Devanagari (!) text at the top.

Found in West Bengal near the Sikkim border.
Large hip roofs made of corrugated sheet metal are found in West Bengal and adjacent areas in Bihar and Odisha.
A variety of poletops attached to the pole with two vertical bars forming a tall and narrow rectangle can be found in West Bengal.
The bridges in West Bengal frequently feature blue and white concrete blocks. It is also rarely found in Bihar around the city of Gaya.

Found mostly in the main, southern part of West Bengal, but more in the west.
Sometimes also found in Bihar at the border to eastern Nepal.

Note by MB: This meta is not sufficiently researched, but it's still good to know
If you see these hip roofs made out of tin - which are usually found in West Bengal - in Bihar, you're in the Northeastern Quarter of Bihar.
In West Bengal, houses with walls painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom, are usually found near the Jharkhand border.
In Assam, these white flowers can often be seen along the road in three areas: - The border to West Bengal - The border to Eastern Bhutan - West of Nagaon.
Flat roof tiles, similar to the ones found in the south, with a small diamond shaped protrusion in the middle, are commonly found in and around West Bengal.
These vans (can be white, red, or orange) with specifically yellow plates, in NE India are found only within West Bengal and Assam. Doesn’t count with a white plate.

In West Bengal you may also find poletops containing two crossbars which are connected to each other with thin vertical supports on either side. The lower bar is connected on either side to the pole with diagonal supports.
A variety of poletops attached to the pole with two vertical bars forming a tall and narrow rectangle can be found in West Bengal.

In West Bengal you may also find poletops containing two crossbars which are connected to each other with thin vertical supports on either side. The lower bar is connected on either side to the pole with diagonal supports.
Tea plantations can be found in the northeast and the far south. NOTE: If you find tea plantations in a flat area, you are likely in Assam or northeastern West Bengal, near the Assam border.

Uttar Pradesh.text: Flat Guna tiles is just a tiled roof full of staple-shaped tiles. It can be found around Prayagraj, south east of Uttar Pradesh state,

3-5 Insulators pointing upwards, attached to the pole.

Common in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Bihar.
Exclusive to Uttar Pradesh, their symbol is a bicycle.
Sugarcane is most commonly found in the north in and around Uttar Pradesh, and in the southwest.

Advertisements for IELTS-exams are relatively often seen between Punjab and Western Uttar Pradesh

Note by MB: Of course, advertisements like this can theoretically be found everywhere.
Eucalyptus trees are a good clue for the Uttarakhand foothills and nearby areas in Uttar Pradesh.
Southern Haryana and Southern Uttar Pradesh are very agricultural, but often still look dry. These areas look like a mix of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

If the generic poletop has a grey crossbar, you're most likely in Uttar Pradesh. It's less commonly found in Odisha, Bihar, and more rarely in Haryan and Jharkhand.

If it's in South India, it's 98% Kerala.
Sugarcane is most commonly found in the north in and around Uttar Pradesh, and in the southwest.

Manipur.text: In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.
The Meitei people inhabit Manipur state, especially Imphal. Their flag is commonly found in and around that city.
Manipuri, also called Meitei, is the official language of Manipur. It is written using the Meitei script, which can be recognised by its many vertical lines and right angles.
In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.

Kerala.text: The Malayalam script can be found in Kerala and mostly consists of somewhat simple-looking curvy letters, often containing upside-down U-shapes.
You can commonly find those small yellow pole markings in Kerala. Other states might have sometimes yellow markings like that but they are just way more rare.

Small yellow pole markings are commonly found in Kerala.

Can also be used to rule out Kerala since 80-90% of all poles have it. Can also be found in Goa (2-3%)

Green flag with half moon and star, pointing at the top left corner.

This party is almost exclusively active in Kerala. Mostly in the districts of Kozhikode and Malappuram.

In 2025, a large part of the NH-66 in Kerala is under construction, making it very recognizable.

If you see a long, straight highway with construction in Smallcam, you're likely to be on the NH-66.
Blue and white bridges can commonly be found all over Kerala. They can sometimes be painted in green.
Goa and Kerala are two of the most developed states in India and often have very wealthy and modern homes.

Nallukettu architecture has distinct roofs, which are often very high and red.
This style is often found around Kerala Backwaters.
Metal holey poles are common in Kerala.
Small yellow pole markings are commonly found in Kerala. NOTE: Similar stickers can rarely be found in other states.

Maharashtra.text: Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script so basically looks like hindi but if you can see the letter ळ that means it's Marathi. Sometimes you won't see that letter so don't rule out Maharashtra.
Sugarcane in Maharashtra is mostly central from what I saw.

Dark soil in India is usually found in and around Maharashtra.

In many cases you can see trident poles together with this dark soil, which will put you in Northern Karnataka, usually near the Maha border (free 4.5k+)
Black Tuk-Tuks are most common in Maharashtra (maybe fake meta)
Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and adjacent regions.
Maharashtra is by far the state with the highest grape production in India.
Found in South India, Goa + Maharashtra, and Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.

Recognizable by the C-Logo
Found in South India, and sometimes in Goa and Maharashtra.
Cotton is commonly found in the western parts of India, particularly in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

Found in North and Central India, plus Jharkhand, Odisha and Gujarat.
Sometimes also in Maharashtra.

Don't confuse with JK Power Cement (which hasn't been researched yet).

Cotton (within) is mostly found around Nanded, more generally in the middle/eastern part of Maharashtra.

Note by MB: Very unreliable in my experience

This hat is called the Gandhi Topi is almost unique to Maharashtra. Note the shape which resembles a boat.

Note by MB: White hats in general are a common attire for Muslims in India, so make sure it's the boat shape.

This poletop has two crossbars, the top one is short with 2 insulators, the bottom one is long with 4 insulators.

It's mostly found in Goa (95%) and rarely in Kerala (2%), Maharashtra (1%) and Karnataka (1%)

This pole is either metal or concrete (but more skinny than a generic pole). It has one or two small bars near the poletop.

It's not exclusive to Maharashtra, but very common there.

Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script, however it sometimes uses the letter ळ  which is not found in Hindi.

Further differences, analyzed by MB:
Shivaji is a person often depicted on statues in Maharashtra. He is always riding a horse, and is often accompanied by an orange flag.
This blue flag with this symbol in the middle is specific for Navayana Buddhism, the branch of Buddhism common in Central-Eastern Maharashtra.
This type of cacti (Euphorbia neriifolia) can commonly be seen as part of fences throughout Gujarat, western Maharashtra and the southern half of Rajasthan.
Teak forests in wet season with boxy car can be found around the Gujarat-Maharashtra border between Surat and Nashik. The trees are quite distinctive, tall and narrow.
The landscape west of the Western Ghatts in Maharashtra is quite unique. It has a lot of forests, and a dark brown soil. It's mostly a vibe thing, but it looks kinda like Kerala but with less palms.

The places with the most wind farms are indeed Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. This is pretty advanced knowledge, but region guessing states can be possible by learning where wind farms are:

Cotton fields in Telangana are logically next to the big area that produces the most of it in Maharashtra, so it is gonna be found mostly north-west of the state. You can click in Nizamabad for a good score.

Note by MB: In my experience, it's more common North of Nizamabad.

Coconut palms are most common in Kerala, the Western Half of Karnataka and Southern Coastal Maharashtra
In general, they appear near Coasts, near the border to Bangladesh, and anywhere South of Central Telangana

The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their distinct ridgelines, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation.

NOTE: During the rainy season the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.

Hindi is the most common language in India and can be found in many central and northern regions. It uses the Devanagari script, which can be recognised by the line going through the top of each word and the straight vertical lines found in the majority of all letters.

Note by MB: Maharashtra has a different language that uses the same script.

Buddhist prayer flags and other Buddhist signals are mostly found in the Himalayas.
Sometimes you can also find them in the Northeast, around Bangladesh, especially in Western Meghalaya, Western Mizoram and Southern Tripura.
Rarely you can find it in central-eastern Maharashtra around Nagpur.

Note by MB: The colors in the map don't exactly match the text. The text is right though (for Geoguessr), not the map.
This type of cacti (Euphorbia neriifolia) can commonly be seen as part of fences throughout Gujarat, western Maharashtra and the southern half of Rajasthan.
Cotton is commonly found in the western parts of India, particularly in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and adjacent regions.

The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their distinct ridgelines, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation. NOTE: During the rainy season the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.

Odisha.text: The Oriya script is found in Odisha and has a curvy look, with many letters having wide semi-circles covering the top. Many letters have a distinct diacritic in the shape of a wide curve above the top of the letter. A useful mnemonic is that the shape of the characters resembles 💀 emoji.
W tiled roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:
A boxy car with 6 indents is found near Malkangiri, Odisha.
A boxy car with an extra step at the front is found in Odisha.

This shell is the symbol of a Odisha specific political party:
Biju Janata Dal

W tiled roofs combined with Thatched Roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:

Note by MB: This is also true if you just see W-Tiles, without Thatched Roofs.
Some bridges in Odisha are made of green and white concrete blocks as guardrails
A pole with no poletop except for this tiny bar, is often found in Odisha (70-80%)

In the northeast you will commonly see fences made of thin wooden sticks in a square pattern.

They can also sometimes be seen in Odisha, which has a very different landscape, making it useful to distinguish Odisha from other eastern states.
The Odisha Hills are very "wonky", i.e. they're undulating and can also very greatly in height.
A boxy car with 5 indents can be found near the river mouth of the Subarnarekha river near the Odisha/WB border.

Thatched roofs can be found pretty much all over the eastern coast of India. In the state of Odisha, they can mostly be seen between Balasore and Puri, but also more inland and in the southwest of the state.

If you see only thatched, the coast is more likely.

The coverage on road NH326 (labelled 326) west of Brahmapur in Odisha has a thin grey antenna. The images are generally very high-quality for shitcam, with an especially high quality near the Harabhangi Reservoir.

Karnataka.text: Kannada is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu. It is very similar to the Telugu script(but that one has usually "checkmarks" on top of letters.
Boxy car in Karnataka is only found in and around Bengaluru.

Areca Palms can be recognised by their very thin trunk and a small crown.

They are most common in Assam, but also in other northeastern areas, stretiching to coastal Odisha. A second common region is Kerala and coastal Karnataka

Tripra Mothi is a Tripura-specific party. Its flag has two vertical stripes, yellow and red.

Don't confuse it with the Karnataka flag, where the stripes are horizontal.
If you come across a W tiled roof in Karnataka, you can basically go in the western/southwestern part

If a trident pole has these insulators with three circles and air between them, it is found 98% in Karnataka.

The other versions of this poletop have lower certainties for Karnataka.

In Karnataka, and sometimes in Haryana, you can find trident poletops on concrete poles where the central insulator is attached directly to the top of the pole, while the other two are attached to a horizontal crossbar positioned slightly further down. There is also a variant having several bars instead of one.

Punjab.text: Punjabi can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters ਨ, ਲ and ਅ.

Trident poletop, V-shaped bars underneath and Punjab Poletop.

Very hyperspecific for some roads in Chandigarh.
Within Punjab, the black boxy car can be found on the Pakistani border between Firozpur and Amritsar.
Within Punjab, this car is is unique to Dasuya Forest. Beware that this car is not unique to Punjab though.
Within Punjab, the red boxy car can be found in Ludhiana, Chandigarh, and a bit north between them. The coverage forms a reverse 'v'.

Jammu looks like a fairly developed state compared to most places in India. The architecture looks richer and overall way nicer. Punjab has a similar architecture.

50/50 Tip ! It can be hard to differentiate Punjab and Jammu in urban rounds due to the similarity of their architecture. If you see rich looking houses, look at the car to know whether you are in Punjab or in Jammu. If you don’t see one of the two Jammu cars (boxy with top right thread or central strap, see image 3&4), click Punjab. Note by MB: This 50/50 tip is not 100% reliable, so look at other clues (like Punjabi language) too.

Gurdwaras, which can typically be recognised by their white domes and ornate walls, are most common in Punjab.
You can also sometimes recognise them by the Sikh Khanda symbol, which represents the religion.

Telangana.text:
The only type of tile in Telangana is the W tile type.

As you can see, it doesn’t go in the south of the state.

Slate roofs can be found in a very specific area between Kalaburagi and Hyderabad in Telangana.

Note by MB: This is the same area where they use the thin grey stones (see thin grey stones meta), and thus you can often see them in combination
If you have a Telangana/Andra pole or Telugu with a dry landscape, you are likely in the area between Anantapur, AP and Shadnagar, TG (see image)

This pole has an asymmetric crossbar, with one side double the length of the other, and two insulators on the longer side, and one on the shorter side.

Research is not conclusive due to its rarity, but it's estimated to be 95% Telangana. Note by MB: It's important that the bar is asymmetric, if it's symmetric, and the insulators are asymmetric, it's a different pole.

The area on the border of Telangana and Karnataka often have houses with roofs made out of distinctly thin grey bricks. These grey bricks and similar coloured rocks are sometimes also seen in walls and scattered on the ground in stockyards.

Ladakh.text: All roads in Ladakh have this white car with visible front.

Delhi.text: Orange and bright green buses are typically found in Delhi.

Pole paint consisting of five or more thin black and yellow stripes can be found in Delhi.

#1 clue for rural Delhi (98%) Has to be the exact order and color.
Pole paint consisting of five or more thin black and yellow stripes can be found in Delhi.

Arunachal Pradesh.text: This Orange Pole Paint is found on the NH15 in Arunachal Pradesh
This pole configuraiton is mainly found in Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh.
The only divided road in Arunachal Pradesh is the NH415 south of Itanagar
Found only in North-East India, but not in Nagaland or Arunachal Pradesh.

Trapezoid poletop, but the diagonal bars do not reach the end of the crossbar.

Most common in flat Arunachal Pradesh
Sometimes in Tripura
Within Arunachal Pradesh, a back antenna can be found around Chowkam and East of Namsai.
Within Arunachal Pradesh, a white car with mirrors can be found on the road west of Itanagar.
Metal poles with a mesh pattern are commonly found in Sikkim (93%) and rarely in Arunachal Pradesh (5%)
It is quite rare to see red and white bollards, but they are mostly found in far west Arunachal Pradesh
In Assam, you can find houses with woven walls along the border to Arunachal Pradesh, north of Tinsukia.
If you see this white, boxy-looking car in Arunachal Pradesh, you're on the road between Tezu and Lohitpur.
This flag that resembles the Japanese flag stands for Donyi Polo, a religion found in Arunachal Pradesh between Ziro and Anini.
Green pole stripes are commonly found in the far western roads of Arunachal Pradesh. They are often combined with yellow or white stripes.
Poles with two diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape are common in Meghalaya (75%) and Arunachal Pradesh (20%) and occasionally found in Assam (2%).
These bollards are rarer and not unique to Arunachal Pradesh, but if you think you are here, these are the areas these bollards are most commonly found
If you see Mountains to the North in Assam, you're on the border to Arunachal Pradesh. In my experience, this is a particularly common sight on the border east of Itanagar.

Within Arunachal Pradesh, both this black and this red car are exclusively found in Roing.
The black car appears mainly on the NH313 and east.
The red car appears mainly west of the main road.
Poles with two diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape are common in Meghalaya and Arunachal Pradesh and occasionally found in Assam.

Meghalaya.text: Black Taxis with yellow roofs are found in Meghalaya and Mumbai.

The NH6 north of Shillong is the only divided highway in Meghalaya.

Note by MB: A good way to tell you're in Meghalaya is the lack of non-latin scripts.

The western part of Meghalaya basically looks like bangladesh with hills. There are a lot of areca palms, banana trees and palms.

“Hilly forests with areca palms surrounding flat agricultural fields” is how I would best describe this part of Meghalaya.
The state of Meghalaya uses English primarily and no other scripts. Thus if you see a lot of signs and no non-english language, you are most likely in Meghalaya.

Parts of roads NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong can be recognised by the presence of khasi pines with distinct yellow outer road lines and fresh dark pavement.

NOTE: This is the only road in Meghalaya that uses yellow outer road lines, but these lines exist in other states as well.
The endangered Indian pitcher plant is exclusive to the Khasi Hills, which are mainly in Meghalaya. They can occasionally be spotted on road sides, especially on the NH206 north of Umlārem.

In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see poles with two crossbars, each with two insulators. If there are more than two bars, you should be in Meghalaya or Mizoram. NOTE: They can rarely be seen in other states.
Khasi pines are mainly found in Meghalaya and Manipur. While the needles appear similar to those of chir pines, the overall crown formed by its branches will appear more jagged and disorganised.

The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded hillsides having many small peaks scattered around. NOTE: A somewhat similar landscape can be found in Meghalaya, however rather than distinct peaks, the hillsides will have a mostly smooth and flat top.

Rajasthan.text: In Rajasthan, rolling hills are common for the area south of Udaipur
In Rajasthan, there is a North-east angled ridge going from Mount Abu area to New Delhi
The western parts of Rajasthan can commonly be recognised by the dry landscape with sandy soil.
The biggest mountainous areas in Rajasthan are around Alwar max northeast and Udaipur - Mount Abu area

This tree, often called Jand by Indians, can be recognized by the clusters of leaves at the end of thick branches.

It is found in Northern Rajasthan and Southern Haryana/Punjab.
These 'dead'-looking trees are a very strong point to go to Rajasthan. They are concentrated mostly southwest of Sikar.
Calotropis Procera is found all over Rajasthan and less in surrounding states so it is a good clue for Rajasthan if you have a lot of it.

Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab and Haryana.
93% Punjab
4% Haryana
1% Delhi & Jammu (on Punjabi border)
0.5% Rajasthan
0.2% Ladakh
West of Mount Abu, you can find a lot of Euphorbia cacti with flat landscape. Note that this meta is only specific for Rajasthan, Euphorbia appears in other states, like Gujarat, too.

Salt flats and coastal marshes with nearly no vegetation, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. Shallow bodies of water can often be seen around these areas.

NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and you’ll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.

Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you know or have a feeling you’re in Rajasthan, it is most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and southeast of Kota (flat). This can be used combined with the elevation to get the precise area.

Rajasthan is a state that is drier than its surrounding states. It's difficult to explain, but many locs in Rajasthan just have a certain 'drier' vibe. If you saw this loc and thought 'This looks like Rajasthan', pat yourself on the back :)
Canola is mostly found in and around Rajasthan.
The western parts of Rajasthan can commonly be recognised by the dry landscape with sandy soil.

Chhattisgarh.text:
Extra vertical bar at the top of the pole, extends significantly over the pole.

85% West Bengal
12% Chhattisgarh
Clay houses exist a lot in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and some spill can be seen in southwestern Bihar.

Trapezoid poletops with poles completely made out of dark metal, are found in Chhattisgarh 95% of the time.

If it's not made out of dark metal, it's less certain.
Houses made out of clay are most common in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. There's some spill in far southwestern Bihar.
Typically not south of Maharashtra-Chhattisgarh-Odisha except in Kerala. Generic pole does NOT include any bars on the top of pole
Houses with colorful, particularly blue painted walls, can be found in the areas around Eastern Madhya, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.
Red soil can be found in several regions, but mainly near the southern west coast and in and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.
Thin rusted Poles that are hollow, i.e. have an indent going from the bottom to the top, are found in Maharashtra, and sometimes in Chhattisgarh.
Date palms can be found in Central India. They appear North of the Latitude of Chhattisgarh, except for Himalayan states, the Northeast and Western Gujarat/RJ.

Communist symbolism is mostly found in Kerala. Second mostly, but significantly less, it's found in Tamil Nadu. Sometimes, it's also found in Tripura, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. You can rarely spot it in Maharashtra, West Bengal, Assam and Manipur.

The communist party has a youth organisation, the DYFI, with the same distribution.
Red soil can be found in several regions, but mainly near the southern west coast and in and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.

Himachal Pradesh.text:
This coverage can be found on the 3 in Himachal Pradesh near the Ladakh border.

The coverange extends from Zing Zing Bar to Killingsarai
The NH5 near Sarahan ist the only road in Himachal Pradesh with a double guardrail.
Found Northwest of Madhya Pradesh, however not in Himachal Pradesh or further North.

This means, it has an indent that runs through the whole pole. If you look at it from the top, it looks like a C.

Most common in Mizoram, seen in Himachal Pradesh as well. Note by MB: Seen this in central states too, but still useful together with landscape ig.

Insulators at the top, directly attached to the concrete, pointing in one direction. Below, there is a metal crossbar with no insulators.

70% Maharashtra
10% Chhattisgarh
5% Himachal Pradesh
Punjab is generally a very flat state. If you know you're in Punjab, but it's hilly or mountains, you're on the border to Himachal Pradesh
In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh you can find an extremely dry landscape with little to no vegetation within the Himalayan mountains.
Shimla is  the only city in Himachal Pradesh to have a boxy car, which is this car with the top right corner visible with a thread (sometimes not visible).
Thin grey metal poles are seen all over northeastern India and in the Himalayan region of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. You will commonly see two of these poles in close proximity.

The western half of Uttarakhand is typically far more barren than the other Himalayan regions, due to logging and erosion. The coverage northwest of Dehradun on the Himachal Pradesh Border has some especially barren hills full of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.
Thin grey metal poles are seen all over northeastern India and in the Himalayan region of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. You will commonly see two of these poles in close proximity.
In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh you can find an extremely dry landscape with little to no vegetation within the Himalayan mountains.

Sikkim.text: Taxis in Sikkim often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle on it.
Roofs in Sikkim often have this short "curtain" hanging down on the side of the roof.
This party has an orange-red-green flag and a table lamp as a symbol. It operates exclusively in Sikkim.

While the car is blurred most of the time, Sikkim features a noticeable car that gives the western part of Sikkim, starting at Rangpo.

It can have an antenna, be blurred, almost invisible, but as long as you see a yellow car, you know it’s here.
Metal poles with a mesh pattern are commonly found in Sikkim.

Uttarakhand.text: These orange stickers on metal poles can be found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the East.
Metal poles in Uttarakhand sometimes have those red or yellow stripes painted on them.
In Uttarakhand, you can find these red-white stripes on poles on random roads around Dwarahat.
Besides Kerala and Uttarakhand, Delhi can also rarely have yellow stickers. All of these regions look very different.
This black bollard with stripes (usually at least one of the colors: red, white, orange) can be found in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.
In the Himalayas, pure metal poles are usually more common in the North-East. If you see them in the Northwest, it's most likely Uttarakhand.
In Uttarakhand, the Bihar pole (yellow and black stripes) can be found on the NH109 North and a small road South of Dwarahat. Since Uttarakhand is mountainous, you shouldn't mistake it for Bihar.

Goa.text: This car (note the antenna!) can be found in Goa, and in the Union Territory of Daman.
This black car, uniquely characterized through the black bars on each the side, is only found in Goa.
This white car, uniquely characterized through the bar on the side, which is black and grey, is only found in Goa.
Poletops with a short crossbar above a longer crossbar can be found in Goa.

Tripura.text: Within Tripura, Tea is found along the Bangladeshi border, and along the Assamese border.
Tripura Poles often tend to have an extra bar underneath as well as the small crossbar on top.
Many locations in Tripura have a pretty low brightness, despite the sun being out and not setting.

Mizoram.text: In Mizoram, a grey car with double mirrors appears in the southernmost coverage, near the NH502.
A car with a black front and a stubby antenna within Mizoram can be found on the roads west of Aizawi.

If you see a long antenna, combined with a black car front in Mizoram, you're on the NH6 north of Serkhan.

Keep in mind this car is not unique to Mizoram.
Mizo, found in Mizoram, is the language most commonly found on the Indian coverage other than English, which uses the Latin script.
The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded, smooth hillsides with a flat top.

Jammu and Kashmir.text:
Triangle poletops with three insulators on top can be found in Jammu and Kashmir, sometimes in Himachal Pradesh.

Note: Do not confuse this with the regular triangle poletops which can be found elsewhere. Also even these poletops are not 100% unique to J&K

Chir pines are more or less exclusive to Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir as well as in westernmost Arunachal Pradesh. These pines can be identified from their generally smooth-looking conical or spherical crowns with very long needles.

spotlight.text: Orange and bright green buses are typically found in Delhi.
Black Taxis with yellow roofs are found in Meghalaya and Mumbai.
Taxis in Sikkim often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle on it.
Elevated railways can be found in the following cities: Bengaluru Bengaluru Chennai Chennai Delhi Delhi Hyderabad Hyderabad Jaipur Jaipur Kochi Kochi Kolkata Kolkata Mumbai Mumbai

The area on the border of Telangana and Karnataka often have houses with roofs made out of distinctly thin grey bricks. These grey bricks and similar coloured rocks are sometimes also seen in walls and scattered on the ground in stockyards.
White painted clay huts are found in northwestern Bihar and northeastern Uttar Pradesh.
Wooden huts with a cross pattern can be found in central Bihar.

Japanese cedar trees can typically be recognised by their significant height combined with their narrow, fluffy-looking crowns. They are most commonly found near the border of Sikkim and West Bengal, as well as in Meghalaya.
The Bhutan white pine can be recognised by its hanging needles all pointing downwards. They are mainly found in the Mechuka Valley as well as near the Bhutan border in Arunachal Pradesh.
The endangered Indian pitcher plant is exclusive to the Khasi Hills, which are mainly in Meghalaya. They can occasionally be spotted on road sides, especially on the NH206 north of Umlārem.

The western half of Uttarakhand is typically far more barren than the other Himalayan regions, due to logging and erosion. The coverage northwest of Dehradun on the Himachal Pradesh Border has some especially barren hills full of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.

The landscape south of Shillong in Meghalaya, is characterised by V-shaped, green eroded valleys with somewhat flat and smooth ridgetops. NOTE: Mizoram hills are less smooth with more rises and falls instead of long smooth ridges.

Salt flats and coastal marshes with nearly no vegetation, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. Shallow bodies of water can often be seen around these areas. NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and you’ll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.
Near the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, you can find these large monolithic mountains, with huge exposed rocks. Several of these mountains can be seen from afar, especially the Magenthiragiri hills.
A flat, bushy landscape with very red soil can be found in southern Tamil Nadu.
Lakshadweep, located off the coast of Kerala, can be easily recognised by the abundance of coconut trees. They are often painted red-and-white, resembling the Polish flag.

The coverage on road NH326 (labelled 326) west of Brahmapur in Odisha has a thin grey antenna. The images are generally very high-quality for shitcam, with an especially high quality near the Harabhangi Reservoir.

Parts of roads NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong can be recognised by the presence of khasi pines with distinct yellow outer road lines and fresh dark pavement. NOTE: This is the only road in Meghalaya that uses yellow outer road lines, but these lines exist in other states as well.
