metas.description: If in the Nusas, and are in the hills (not mountains/taller hills like Flores) you are probably in Sumbra, mostly west/south

metas.title: South Sumatra Architecture
metas.description: often tiled roofs, with wooden front of the house. House is kinda elevated off the ground. once you see it you wont unsee it.

metas.title: Mamasa Roof
metas.description: very similar to some of the other roofs, but this one the bottom of the roof that is going up is completely straight and not curved.

metas.title: Timor white brick
metas.description: If you think u might be on Timor, (very dry, has a distinct vibe cause its the most east), white brick buildings are a good clue for Timor.

metas.title: Muna Island blue houses
metas.description: for some reason Muna Island just has a lot of blue, espcially houses. so if you think u may be in Muna island, and u see blue, its a good clue.

metas.title: North Kali blur
metas.description: most of it is overrun. will be front of the car, in northern north kali. also for more car meta: if its gen 3, you probably shoulndt click kali

metas.title: Bangka Belitung roof
metas.description: tiles only on like the creases in the roofs. can be found eslewhere (like nusas i think) but if its on like all the roofs its prolly Bangka Belitung

metas.type: Flat W/ Lone Mt. W Kali
metas.title: Flat w/ lone mt. w kali
metas.description: west kali is mostly flat, except for the occasional hill or mountain. so you will often see a flat landscape with one or two hills/mountains near you.

metas.title: Nusa Huts
metas.description: little huts in front of houses that offer shade. Found in the Nusas, where it is dry, and often in Lombok. can be much smaller than the one in the picture

metas.title: Central Java Pole
metas.description: can be a trident pole but doenst have to be. the way the central insulator is attached to the pole on the side with that extra peice is what makes it unique.

metas.title: Nusa Pole
metas.description:
On the Lesser Sunda Islands (“Nusas”), you can find poles with an extra support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.
The Nusas are very dry.

metas.title: West Sumatra Pole
metas.description: symmetrical pole, often metal, has connecting bars that go in at like a 35-40 degree angle from the middle of crossbar to NOT the pole itself, but to little connecting bits. NOT 45 degrees.

metas.title: Gorontalo Hills
metas.description: Gorontalo has these unique green hills almost roundish rolling hills. sort of a lack of trees, but there are often some oil palms, often corn growing. click around gorontalo and get a vibe for it.

metas.title: Sumbawa inbetween hills
metas.description: most of the coverage in Sumbawa is in between the hills/mountains in the flat areas. So if you are in the Nusas, but in flat area between mountains/hills (you can see them in the distance) you are prolly in Sumbawa.

metas.title: NS lake landscape
metas.description: Hills are cleared of trees, very green (if there are trees they are replanted, standing on their own, not natural looking). mostly a vibe but nothing else in indo looks like this. Hills with nothing on it exept grass = lake

metas.title: NS mount sinabung
metas.description: Very distinct Volcano visible from a decently far away around Berastagi. Also in the plateau the crops are different, farming equipment is differnt, often greenhouses, very small fields. overall very different culture from rest of NS.

metas.title: Bintan constructing
metas.description: bintan is a Batam wannabe. they are basically prepping it to be built up like Batam. So lots of like big buildings with no others around it that seem out of place. Lots of emptiness. click around a little bit and you will get a vibe for it.

metas.title: South Sula Roof
metas.description: this shape of roof with the trinagle and then the flaps coming off the sides at a different angle is extremely common in South Sula. They also often have gable horns. The more unique ones have peices of wood horizontal supporting the top triangle

metas.title: Central Kali Camera Glitch
metas.description: I found this camera glitch while searching. If you look 90 degrees to the left of the front of the car, there is a glitch that is easier seen when you zoom in fully with a bunch of little lines. in some panos it is more purple aswell. Found within Central Kali on these roads. some parts may have ben ovverrun with newer coverage. It will have 2024 copyright

metas.title: Nusa pole
metas.description: On the Lesser Sunda Islands (“Nusas”), you can find poles with an extra long support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.

metas.title: Landscape - Savannah
metas.description: This savannah landscape is occasionally seen on North Sumba.
metas.comparison: NOTE: In Generation 3, you will always see a white car.

metas.title: Churches
metas.description: Indonesia is religiously a Muslim majority country, so seeing churches, and other Christian signs, is a good clue for these regions.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Nusa Pole
metas.description: On the Lesser Sunda Islands ('Nusas'), you can find poles with an extra long support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.

metas.title: Landscape - Palu Bay
metas.description: Palu Bay is a unique slightly north-west facing bay just north of Palu city, which features mountains to the west of the bay, and a flat, more urbanised landscape to the east.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Even Pole
metas.description: Indonesia uses two types of pole tops: even and uneven. This refers to the bar that holds the insulators and whether it is symmetrical to the pole itself. Knowing where even and uneven poles are most commonly found is useful for region guessing.

metas.title: Vegetation - White Leadtree
metas.description: White leadtree (Leucaena leucocephala) can be recognised by its delicate featherlike (bipinnate) leaves. Fruits are often also visible in the form of legume pods. It can be found mainly in the Nusas as well as a few other dry areas of the country.

Bali.text: idk what these are, but they are most common on bali.
square bali pavement. not exclusive, but most common.
the rectangle below the crossbar on an even pole is unique to bali.
These two types, the one with this grey bricks, and the orange brick. again not exclusive but quite common on bali.
Like Bali, has basically everything bali has, but a bit more dry, has a vibe to the landscape. click around to get a feel for it.
bali has these weird thatched lookin roofs, very common in Bali, sometimes in like rice fields, or on side of road etc. does not have to be a full roof for a house

this is what the typical bridge in bali looks like w/ the gold and black. but what makes it unique is the little statue patron things on the ends of the bridge. the actualy stutue thing doesnt have to be there just the pedestal.

Generation 3 antenna coverage is most commonly found on Java, but can very rarely be seen on Bali in and around Denpasar. It is most commonly seen in East Java, as most of the antenna coverage in the west has been overwritten by Generation 4.

dark blue sticker on the pole is only found in Bali and Nusa Pineda i think, and i think a lighter version can be found in west nusas maybe lombok aswell, but both can get faded. If you see a blue sticker your prolly somewhere there. most likely bali i think.

Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too. Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.
A black cab with men sitting in the truck bed can be seen near Jagasatru on Bali.
A white SUV with black bars and a wooden plank on the roof can rarely be seen in eastern Bali.
Bali features both even and uneven poles, as well as the Lesser Sunda island variants. You can also find this unique rectangle attachment on the pole tops in Bali.
Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.
Bali features both even and uneven poles, as well as the Lesser Sunda island variants. You can also find this unique rectangle attachment on the pole tops in Bali.

Sumatra.text: like West sumatra, North sula has these nice small roads
within Sumatra, basically the only place you will see rice is in West Sumatra.
Looks like North Sumatra, (roofs, oil palms, vibe, etc) but has uneven poles. Very limited coverage
jambi has mostly tin roofs w/ the occasional tiled roof. remember gradient from most to least w/in sumatra goes from south to north.
West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs. the ends go up into a spike unlike the ones in North Sumatra (and south sula)
Like the richest part of sumatra, the roads are all paved really well, often road lines on smaller roads that usually wouldnt be there.
Lots of rubber trees in South sumatra. Ive also seen them in north sumatra though, but should be able to tell the difference w/ other clues w/in Sumatra
These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.

This plant is basically everywhere on the island, and is pretty much unique to Nias island within Indonesia. Recognizable red tinted leaves mixed in with the green leaves.

Being part of North Sumatra, they Nias has the NS poles, often made of metal. Nias also often just has random piles of rock on the side of the road.

Around the Lake in North Sumatra you get this roof (central NS). Very boat shaped. can often be found as miniature roofs like on side of the road or on shacks or on top of stuff, etc.

DO NOT confuse it with the West Sumatra roof, that one the ends are steeper and go higher and are "spiky".

One way to differentiate Kali from something like Sumatra is that in Kali, most of the roads are like cut through the forest. Everything is bassically on the side of the road again kinda carved into the forest. def more of a vibe

Areca palms, often called Sumatra palms w/in indo, basically mostly found within Sumatra. probably most often found in western North Sumatra (and the rest of the west coast). west coast of all of sumatra often hilly, North (eastish) coast often flat.

(i have seen them in the nusas, but you probably shouldnt confuse sumatra w/ the nusas)

South Sumatra has terrible land management. so if you feel like the land is being poorly managed, its prolly south sumatra. one effect of this is that there are often mixed types of plantations on each side of the road, or a plantation on one side, and then its wild on the other, etc.

block building with no nice things on the side (just concrete). Often above a garage (even if a building is one story, it can often still have a blocky or square feel which is a good clue for NS). Often found in rows, all next to each other This is a good clue for North Sumatra and Sometimes Riau.
West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs.
Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.
Steeply pitched roofs made of palm tree leaves can sometimes be seen on Nias Island, south west of North Sumatra.

North Sumatra features similarly distinct boat-shaped roofs, however the roofs are less angled upward and they do not feature spires.

NOTE: These roofs are most commonly found near Lake Toba, due to its sacred history.
The region around Lake Toba, in North Sumatra, can be recognized by mountains surrounding the lake and Samosir Island in the middle. Overcast coverage is also common for the region.
Areca palms (Areca catechu) are most prominent in western Sumatra; however they can also be seen elsewhere less commonly. They can be recognised by their relatively short and thick leaves.

Sumatran pines (Pinus merkusii) in Indonesia can be found in a few pockets across the country, notable areas include North Sumatra and Java. They can be recognised by having long needles for leaves, but be careful not to confuse them with she-oak, which has even longer leaves.

In some of the Generation 4 coverage in the city of Batam, a purple tint and a black blurred object can be seen. Although this camera glitch is most commonly found in Batam, you may spot it in nearby regions such as North Sumatra, around Medan. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.
Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.

Java.text: central java pavement. like 80% accurate w/in Java probably.
uneven pole, which within Java is most likely east java. The unique poles are the ones that are uneven and the pole continues much higher than the crossbar.
if within Java, and there are these rock walls, (volcanic most likely), and everything feels volcanic, like for ex. dark fields, rocks on the side of the road, etc., you are prolly here.

The Nusas typically look drier than other regions in Indonesia. The islands get especially dry towards the east, especially in Generation 3. Vegetation tends to look less tropical, but instead more brown with a lack of leaves. Sumba Island is also the driest of the Nusas.

NOTE: While less common, other regions such as Java can look similarly dry. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

The Nusas typically look drier than other regions in Indonesia. The islands get especially dry towards the east, especially in Generation 3. Vegetation tends to look less tropical, but instead more brown with a lack of leaves. Sumba Island is also the driest of the Nusas. NOTE: While less common, other regions such as Java can look similarly dry. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

Riau.text: Oil Palms = click Riau basically. Riau has a lot of oil palms.
within Riau, an oval that says "KJ" in it, w/ blue writing around the oval.
This specific Gable Horn (i think thats what its called) is unique to Riau.
lots of oil palms in riau. Dumai is the main port so the palm oil is exported through pipes to Dumai. If you see pipes, you think you might be in Riau, your probably around Dumai.

Kalimantan.text: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.
Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

malaysia has this curve on the edges of the roof sometimes. this is not at all of indo origin, so it is only found in places that border malaysia. So mostly on the east coast of Sumatra, all those islands, and West Kalimantan.

These horizontal slots inside the triangles of the roofs are almost unique to Southern Sulawesi.

NOTE: They can rarely be found in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.

Roofs with gable horns can be found most commonly in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan.

NOTE: Horned roofs are often found with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi. Use this tip along with other clues to determine which region you are in.
The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different. The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.
Within Indonesia, oil palm plantations are mostly concentrated in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Palm plantations can rarely be seen in Sulawesi.
In the regions of Sumatra and Kalimantan that lie opposite Malaysia, many buildings have metal canopies with curved ends. These canopies are often blue or red.

Tiled roofs are most commonly found on the island of Java, and sometimes nearby regions such as southern Sumatra, the Lesser Sunda Islands, and South Kalimantan.

NOTE: The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different. The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.

Plain sheet metal roofs are more commonly found toward the north, where tiled roofs are not found.
They are most commonly found on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.

Indonesia commonly uses these black-and-white square or circular bollards, as well as these yellow-and-black ones, which can also have a red reflector. Other designs can also be found.

NOTE: UK-style bollards are mostly found in Kalimantan.

Coastal she-oak (Casuarina equisetifolia) can be found along the coast throughout much of the country, but particularly in Sumatra, Kalimantan and Java. Their leaves resemble the needles of pine trees, but are noticeably longer. Another species of she-oak can be found in mountainous regions throughout the country.
Coverage in Indonesia is fairly limited. Notably, there is no coverage on Papua or adjacent islands, and coverage is sparse in areas such as Kalimantan, Aceh, Central Sulawesi and North Maluku.
Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.
Within Indonesia, oil palm plantations are mostly concentrated in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Palm plantations can rarely be seen in Sulawesi.

Maluku.text: like extrusions of roof at a slight down angle are common in North maluku.
houses on North maluku are often on this rock looking foundation that is a bit off the ground.
Even Pole, with the supports coming down directly to the pole at a 45 degree angle. found in North Maluku and West Kali
North Maluku often has these piles of rock scattered around and then these gutters and other stuff are sometimes made of rock

Lampung.text: southeast sula is often in a grid like lampung, can look like lampung at times
Most of Lampung is in a grid, lots of straight rods, not always North-south tho.
very bright tiles tiles mixed in with the "normal" colored tiles. you wont really see this in java. remember theres a gradient of how many roofs are tiled from Lampung to Jambi.

houses are kinda just all on their own. very spread out. the landscape is flat (in the east, west too difficult).  lampung architecture is extremely unique. click around and get a feel for it. the houses almost feel more modern to me, often have collums holding up like a small porch in front. often tiled roofs.

Cassava (Manihot esculenta) can be recognised by its small, hand-shaped leaves. It can be found both in plantations as well as semi-wild in residential areas. It is most commonly seen in Lampung and Java with Lampung being the main hot spot.

Sulawesi.text: Within the Nusas, the Sulawesi style fence is common on the Island of Sumbawa.
These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.
Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.
Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.
These sticks on the side of the road are like 100% Lampung 80% of the time. look for other clues cause it could just randomly be like Sulawesi and ur cooked.

A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs. The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.
Black Generation 3 coverage can be found almost everywhere in Indonesia, but is most common in Sulawesi.
Giant milkweed (Calotropis gigantea) is a small shrub with thick round leaves and pale flowers. It can be found in dry regions of Indonesia, namely the Nusas and parts of Java and Sulawesi.
The majority of rice production is concentrated in Java, but can sometimes be found in other provinces, namely South Sulawesi and South Sumatra. They can rarely be found in other provinces as well.

Coconut palms (Cocos nucifera) can be found in many regions throughout Indonesia, but are most abundant along the coast, especially in western Sumatra, southern Java, northern Sulawesi and North Maluku.

You can often see thin, black poles next to regular poles near the East Peninsula of Central Sulawesi. Two pieces of tape can be seen near the top of the poles, usually light blue and green. These can rarely be seen in northern South East Sulawesi.

Footstool palm (Saribus rotundifolius) has fan-shaped leaves similar to those of Palmyra palm; however the crown is more open, the leaves are thinner and the palm itself is usually taller. It can be found most notably in Sulawesi and more rarely in other parts of the country.

Palmyra palms (Borassus flabellifer) can be recognised by their fan-shaped leaves and dense round crowns. Compared to footstool palm, the crown is more dense, the leaves are heavier and the palm itself is usually shorter. It is found in dry parts of the country, namely the Nusas and South Sulawesi.

Gebang palm (Corypha utan) can at first glance look similar to both Palmyra and footstool palm due to its fan-shaped leaves, however the leaves are noticeably larger, stiffer and more upright in contrast to the round crown shape of both Palmyra and footstool palm. Unlike most palms, the gebang palm will only flower once at the end of its life in a dramatic gesture where the leaves wither away and it shoots one large inflorescence into the heavens before it dies. It is found mainly in the east of the country, namely Sulawesi and the Nusas.
Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

You can often see thin, black poles next to regular poles near the East Peninsula of Central Sulawesi. Two pieces of tape can be seen near the top of the poles, usually light blue and green. These can rarely be seen in northern South East Sulawesi.
Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.
These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.

The majority of rice production is concentrated in Java, but can sometimes be found in other provinces, namely South Sulawesi and South Sumatra. They can rarely be found in other provinces as well. For a full overview, see this page.

Surabaya.text: East java pavement. mostly around Surabaya. sometimes called surabaya pavement.
Pavement made out of bricks like this is found in East Java, particularly around Surabaya

Medan.text: within NS around Medan, you often get other crops in addition to Oil palms, like Corn, Sugarcane, etc. (not often rice). Also most of Medan and surrounding local area is in a North-South Grid

Jakarta.text: Poles with an indent on both sides are found in West Java, Jakarta, and Banten.
Poles with an indent on both sides are found in West Java, Jakarta, and Banten.

Yogyakarta.text: Trident style pole tops are most commonly found in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rarely in South and West Kalimantan, and North Sumatra and Riau.
Trident style pole tops are most commonly found in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rarely in South and West Kalimantan, and North Sumatra and Riau.

spotlight.text: The region around Lake Toba, in North Sumatra, can be recognized by mountains surrounding the lake and Samosir Island in the middle. Overcast coverage is also common for the region.

In some of the Generation 4 coverage in the city of Batam, a purple tint and a black blurred object can be seen. Although this camera glitch is most commonly found in Batam, you may spot it in nearby regions such as North Sumatra, around Medan. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
Steeply pitched roofs made of palm tree leaves can sometimes be seen on Nias Island, south west of North Sumatra.
A white SUV with black bars and a wooden plank on the roof can rarely be seen in eastern Bali.
A black cab with men sitting in the truck bed can be seen near Jagasatru on Bali.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.key_meta: Yellow dashed lines like this are super common in Ireland.

metas.title: Dashed yellow lines
metas.description: Yellow dashed lines like this are super common in Ireland. You can find sometimes similar lines in New Zealand so if you are not sure use other clues like landscape/vegetation etc.

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description:
These green and white bollards can be a good clue for Ireland.
They are not entirely unique to the country, but they are especially helpful in 50-50s with the UK.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Strip Of Grass
metas.description:
You will often see a strip of grass in the middle of tiny rural roads.
Such roads are called “boreens”.
While not unique, these boreens can often be a strong clue in a tough 50-50 between Ireland and the UK.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

general_rules.text: Irish phone numbers start with a two digit area code. The area codes are grouped geographically by first digit, and are therefore very learnable.

Western.text: Ireland’s west coast is defined by a rugged, hilly landscape. Steep hills and low mountains dominate. The neat fields of the east make way for wild grass- and moorlands. The grass often has more brownish and yellow tones to it. Sometimes you will be able to see exposed rocks.

Donegal.text: If a very small rural road has Generation 4 coverage and is located in an unusually hilly landscape, you are likely to be in Donegal. Note that this meta only applies to the smallest roads: thin, without road lines, and sometimes with grass in the middle. This type of coverage is also not exclusive to Donegal, it is just likely to be there.

Wicklow.text: One noteworthy area in the east is the Wicklow Mountains, just south of Dublin. They can look deceptively similar to the western coastal mountains. It can be very hard, if not downright impossible to distinguish these two areas. Two things to look out for: You will never see the coast from the Wicklow mountains. You will never see the coast from the Wicklow mountains. Like Donegal, its small roads are mostly covered with Generation 4 instead of the Generation 2 that is more typically associated with small roads in the west. Like Donegal, its small roads are mostly covered with Generation 4 instead of the Generation 2 that is more typically associated with small roads in the west.

spotlight.text: In the north of counties Sligo and Leitrim you can find distinctive tabletop mountains. Note that the mountains in the image are just an example, many of the mountains in this area have the same sort of shape.
The area in and around Burren National Park is characterised by a unique karst landscape consisting of exposed grey limestone rocks.
Cork is relatively unique in that it is significantly more hilly than the other big Irish cities.

IM.name: Isle of Man
IM.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (1 regions covered).

metas.title: Landscape
metas.description: The general landscape on the Isle of Man consists of hilly farmland, and narrow roads passing through them.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Red Strip Yellow Plates
metas.description: Similar to the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man uses white front licence plates with yellow rears, but with a red strip on the left.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Gen 2
metas.description:
Coverage on the Isle of Man is limited to Generation 2.
This camera can be recognized by the lower camera quality and circular blur above and below.
Colours will also seem slightly off.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

Douglas.text: Douglas, the capital and largest town on the Isle of Man, can be recognized by the rows of terraced houses, with a higher population density.

This generic lamp design with a blue base and a small blue sticker can be found on most of the island, except for around Douglas, and some parts northeast and south. In addition, the top 2 letters can be used to narrow your location down to 1 of the 21 parishes.
A small white sticker with 2 green numbers will be present on lamps in Douglas.

spotlight.text: The Ronaldsway Airport can be recognized by the large, flat and open field with a boundary fence.

IL.name: Israel & the West Bank
IL.key_meta: If you see cars with yellow front and back license plates in the Middle East, you are in Israel.

metas.title: Yellow plates
metas.description: If you see cars with yellow front and back license plates in the Middle East, you are in Israel.

metas.title: Roadlines
metas.description: Most roads feature yellow outer lines with white centre lines.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Painted Poles
metas.description: Utility poles commonly feature these painted black and white striped bottoms.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Kilometre Markers
metas.description: Kilometre markers are white with a thick border, which can either be red, green or blue.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Stop Sign
metas.description: Rather than having a word meaning ‘stop’ written on them, stop signs have a hand painted on them.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.description: Israel is the only country that uses a symbol on their stop sign making it unique and easily recognizable.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Stop Signs

metas.title: Curbs
metas.description:
You will very often see striped kerbs.
Red and white and fairly commonly black and white.
Red and yellow and blue and white are also rarely found.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Gen 3 Black Car
metas.description:
Most Generation 3 coverage was taken by a black Street View car with a long antenna.
You may also see the black car without an antenna and a silver car with a short antenna.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Blocky Buildings
metas.description:
Architecture tends to consist of bright and warm-coloured stone buildings, often with a blocky appearance.
While Mediterranean-style houses with orange tiled roofs are more common than in other Middle Eastern countries, flat roofs are still just as common.

general_rules.text: Here is a map of area codes in Israel and the West Bank. Note that only the phone codes featured on the map are regional.

Licence plates in the West Bank are often white with green text, often giving blurred plates a slight green tint. On public transport vehicles, such as taxis and buses, the colours will be inverted; green with white text, making blurred plates almost completely green. Beware that Israeli licence plates are also very common in most of the West Bank.

This larger white Citroën follow car with a West Bank licence plate can be found in a region surrounding Jerusalem. It is noticeably found in the cities of Bethlehem and Ramallah. NOTE: The side of this car features the text “SECURITY” in a bold font. Furthermore, this coverage will always feature a black Street View car with no antenna.

Ilps.text: This is a coverage map over Israel and the West Bank. Notably, southern Israel and most of the West Bank has very sparse coverage. You can click on the image to enlarge it.
Southern Israel and eastern West Bank are extremely dry and sandy.

In Jerusalem and surrounding cities in the West Bank, nearly every building is built with the same type of material, called Jerusalem stone. Beware that the stone will look much smoother on newer buildings. NOTE: Single houses with the same material can be found in other towns and cities.
Date palm plantations can often be seen close to the Jordanian border.
The Dead Sea can easily be recognised by the dryness surrounding it. NOTE: It is also visible from Jordan and the West Bank.

Mount Gilboa is a very dry looking mountain, which can be seen from far away and from many angles. There is some coverage on top of the mountain, which is very green and often with a very good view over the surrounding valleys.

Gen4Smudge.text: Most of the Generation 4 coverage features a dirty front camera.

Gen4Nosmudge.text: Generation 4 coverage with a clean front camera is mostly found in and around Tel Aviv.

Northlandscape.text: Northern Israel is usually far more mountainous and green than the rest of Israel. Throughout the region you will almost always see forested hills and mountains.

Centrallandscape.text: Central Israel is usually flat and has several cities. Highways are usually in better condition than roads in the south and north.

Jerusalemlandscape.text: The area west of Jerusalem can often look deceptively similar to northern Israel, with green forested hills and some agriculture sprinkled across the landscape. Two things can occasionally be used to tell the two apart. Firstly, in northern Israel you may occasionally see wide, flat valleys, while the Jerusalem area is always going to be hilly. Secondly, if you see houses made of Jerusalem stone, you are likely to be near Jerusalem.

Landscape.text: Most of the West Bank has a semi-arid Mediterranean landscape. It is generally greener than southern Israel, drier than northern Israel and west of Jerusalem, and hillier and less agricultural than central Israel.

Rockwalls.text: Rock walls put together with cement are found in the north of Israel.

Seaofgalilee.text: Other than the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean Sea, the only major body of water is the Sea of Galilee. It is noticeably more vegetated than the Dead Sea, making it easily recognisable.

Mountcarmel.text: Mount Carmel is a long mountain ridge, going northwest to southeast, near the city of Haifa. From the northeast, it can easily be recognised by its direction and size. There is also a lot of coverage on top of the mountain range, which is generally fairly green and looks noticeably high altitude.

Irrigationchannel.text: You can find these small irrigation canals on the side of the road, in the area around the city of Beit She’an.

Followcarwhite.text: A significant portion of the coverage in the West Bank has a visible security follow car. The most extensive of these is a small white Suzuki, which is found in the central and southern regions.

Followcardarkblue.text: Another follow car is a small dark blue Ford, which is found in the northwest.

spotlight.text: The southern stretch of road 90 will have a dry mountain range to the east. It is also common to see palm trees.
Road 2 can usually be recognised by the Mediterranean sea being visible on the west side of the road. NOTE: If you see mountains to the east, you will be somewhere between Haifa and Zikhron Yaakov.
Mount Tavor is located in the Northern District and can be recognised by its soft, round shape.
Timna National park can be recognised by the complete dryness combined with the mountain ridges in all directions.
These tall, rocky mountains can be found east of Eilat, making the city very easy to recognize.

This mountain range, in the far north of Israel, can be recognised by its shape, somewhat resembling a camel's back. As a bonus, if you are in a city and see these mountains to the west, you will be in Kiryat Shmona.
North of the Hasolelim forest reserve you can see this large reservoir.

Finding parking in Tel Aviv is notoriously difficult, meaning the side of almost every road will be full of parked cars. NOTE: If you are confident that you are in Tel Aviv and see available parking spots, you are more likely to be in the north of the city.
These white rectangular signs with a thin blue border are typically found in Jerusalem.
Jericho can commonly be recognised by the date palms in a somewhat sparsely built and poor-looking urban setting.

In the city of Ramallah you will generally see several black water tanks on most houses. NOTE: Several other cities in both the West Bank and Israel can have black water tanks. What makes Ramallah stand out is the sheer number of them on most buildings.
This grey mosaic brick work shaped like towers is unique to the city of Harish.
This white lamp is unique to Nahariya. It has three arms, with round light bulbs on top.

These lamps, shaped similarly to Barad Dûr, are unique to Acre. It can be found in several different colours. NOTE: Similar looking lamps can be found around central Israel, however the gap between the two horns on top of the lamp should confirm Acre.
These metal lamps, characterised by one high and one low lamp put together with a very angular look, are unique to Netivot.
Poles with blue and white paint on the bottom are unique to Eilat.
These yellow fences and signposts are unique to Kiryat Motzkin.
This style of blue and white fence is very common to see in Ashdod.

Blue house numbers with the number written with Arabic numerals in the top left and with Eastern Arabic numerals in the bottom right, with a thin diagonal line between them, can be found in Bethlehem. Street signs will generally have the same format.
House numbers in Rosh Haayin are blue, with a G-clef in the bottom left corner.
In Ness Ziona, There is an Israeli flag on house numbers.
Blue, shield-shaped house numbers are unique to the city of Herzliya.
Bnei Brak is an ultra-Orthodox Jewish stronghold, which can be seen only by looking at the people around. There will usually be people wearing Jewish religious clothes.
Roundabout signs which are either very thick or attached to a large cube, can be found in the city of Raanana.
These tall industrial chimneys, by the coast north of Netanya, are visible from far away.
This grey Hyundai follow car is unique to Rahat.

The Israel National Trail goes through the entire country and has one of the longest trekkers in the world. The trail goes through more or less every landscape present in the country, from the rocky desert in the south to lush forests in the north. Along the trail you may find these markings, which will typically be orange, blue and white, but can also feature other colour schemes.

IT.name: Italy
IT.key_meta: A short license plate with a double blue strip on the front and a long plate with a double blue strip on the back is unique to Italy.

metas.title: License plates
metas.description: A short license plate with a double blue strip on the front and a long plate with a double blue strip on the back is unique to Italy. Similar long plates with a double blue strip can be found in Albania and France, but the front plates won’t be short.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: Italian bollards are triangular in shape, white with a black top, and feature a red front and a white rear reflector. Albania and San Marino use the same bollards.

metas.title: Guardrail endings
metas.description: Italian guardrails commonly end in this distinct shape. The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.(San Marino can have same guardrail ending)

metas.title: Double Guardrails
metas.description: It is very common to find double guardrails in Italy.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: White Pole Sticker
metas.description: Wooden poles in Italy will commonly feature a small white pole sticker.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: Italian bollards are triangular in shape, and white with a black top. They have a red front and a white rear reflector.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Albania uses the same bollards.

metas.title: Via & Street Signs
metas.description:
Street signs are typically white with a thin blue border and black text.
The name for “Road” or “Way” in Italian is Via.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Guardrail Endings
metas.description:
Italian guardrails commonly end in this distinct shape.
The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Alps - Alpine Architecture
metas.description: Alpine architecture, which typically features large buildings with white stone walls and wooden details, are found in the Alpine region.

metas.title: Roadlines
metas.description:
One of the most common types of Italian road lines are white solid outer lines with no middle line.
This is generally less common in other Mediterranean countries.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Southeast - Trullo Roofs
metas.description:
This particular style of roof, called a trullo, is unique to the Itria valley in southeastern Italy.
It is particularly common in and around the town of Alberobello.

metas.title: Trident Pole Tops
metas.description:
The most common pole tops in Italy are concrete trident pole tops.
There are several possible configurations of insulators.
The two shown in the image are the most common ones.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Blue-Corners Italy
metas.description: Italy, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia all look about the same. Thankfully Romania will not have a white/silver border. Italy will have blue corners visible outside the white edge.

metas.title: Apulian - Flat Roofs
metas.description:
Houses in the Apulian region are generally very light coloured, and have flat roofs, typically with two to three floors.
The architecture is sometimes reminiscent of the Middle East.

metas.title: Architecture
metas.description:
Italian architecture mainly consists of pastel coloured stone houses, generally with terracotta roofs.
Houses will very commonly have wooden shutters, which will typically be divided in two and open sideways.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

general_rules.text: Italian area codes follow a pattern where the first digit generally increases to the east, then south.

Veneto.text: Solid wooden shutters with black metal hinges is a common feature in the northeast of Italy, particularly in Veneto.

Sicily.text: The landscape on the southeastern peninsula surrounding Bari has many olive plantations, which are often seen together with bright rock walls. The dirt in the region typically has a noticeably red colour. Beware that a similar landscape can also be found in southeastern Sicily.

Sardinia.text: Grey rocks sticking up from the ground are commonly found on Sardinia, particularly in the northeast. NOTE: A similar phenomenon can be seen on Sicily, however the landscape will typically be much drier than Sardinia.
Cacti in Italy are most common in the south, particularly in Sicily, southern Sardinia and the south of Apulia.
Rice is mainly produced in the western and central parts of Po valley, and less commonly in Sardinia.

Calabria.text: Citrus plantations are primarily found on eastern Sicily and the southern tip of Calabria.

spotlight.text: Etna, the tallest volcano in Europe, can be seen rising above the landscape from far away in eastern Sicily.

The island of Pantelleria is a volcanic island southwest of Sicily. Dark volcanic rocks can be seen in the many rock walls of the island, as well as on some houses. It is fairly common to see yellow lichen covering the rocks. The island also has a very large amount of cacti.

The Aeolian islands are a volcanic archipelago north of Sicily. Here you will find a mix of volcanic soil and rocks with mediterranean vegetation, like stone pines or olive trees. Like in Sicily, cacti are fairly common. In the mountains of the islands it is very common to see touristic white villas.

The island of Favignana has a distinct topography, with mountains running north to south splitting the island in two. On both sides of the island you will find flat areas, with many rock walls similar to those found in Bari. Unlike the other islands near Sicily, Favignana is not volcanic.

JP.name: Japan
JP.key_meta: Tall reflector with washed colors is exclusive to Kansai region.

metas.title: Low cam
metas.description:
All the coverage taken in Japan is low-cam, the only two other countries with low-cam is Sri Lanka and Switzerland but they look different.
You can recognize lowcam because of wide blur of the street view car and lower vantage point compared to normal camera.

metas.title: Kansai reflector
metas.description: Tall reflector with washed colors is exclusive to Kansai region.

metas.title: Shikoku reflector
metas.description: 6 small reflectors with a little strip "connecting" them in the middle.

metas.title: Shikoku orange band
metas.description: These orange and black bands wrapped around poles can often be found in Shikoku.

metas.title: Chubu triangle mount
metas.description: Transformers in Chubu are often attached with large triangle and horizontal bars.

metas.title: Chubu Plate
metas.description: Chubu plate is super unique because of the rounded shape, you can spot it from far away.

metas.title: Chugoku arrow
metas.description: You may sometimes find an orange arrow located above the top most pole plate in Chugoku.

metas.title: Okinawa plates
metas.description: Plate with multiple numbers and lines in between them. Often will have more than 2 plates.

metas.title: Kanto plate
metas.description:
Often silver and handwritten characters.
Horizontal characters above three vertical digits.

metas.title: Shikoku plate
metas.description: Distinct logo that you can remember since it has 4 dots representing 4 prefectures of Shikoku.

metas.title: Chugoku plate
metas.description: Chugoku plates will have usually written Energia in latin and sometimes they will include logo.

metas.title: Kansai 120 stepdown
metas.description: These attachments with an approximately 120-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Kansai.

metas.title: Kanto tall hat insulators
metas.description: Those insulators are unique to Kanto region and are easy to spot. They have black "hat" on top of white insulator.

metas.title: Tohoku plate
metas.description: Silver horizontal plates with logo in top left. NTT plate will be vertical.(In Hokuriku all the plates will be horizontal)

metas.title: Chugoku pole top
metas.description: This pole top is unique to Chugoku, there is similar version that are more thicc so make sure the pole top is thin like the one on the image.

metas.title: Kyushu Plates
metas.description: Distinc logo(sometimes might be missing). Three numbers horizontally near the top, with 4 vertical characters below them on the right(1 kana and 3 numbers).

metas.title: Kyushu bulky insulator
metas.description: Black meteor like looking insulator, from far might be confused with Kanto tall-black hat insulator but Kyushu one appears little more bulkier even from far.

metas.title: Hokuriku plates
metas.description: Silver horizontal plates with logo on the top right. NTT plates will be also horizontal(in Tohoku NTT plates are vertical, and only Tohoku plate is horizontal).

metas.title: Okinawa Transformers
metas.description: Transformers mounted opposite side of the pole with a T shaped bar mounted on the side of the pole.(Kyushu has straight bar). Sometimes only 1 transformer is present.

metas.title: Shikoku cross bar
metas.description: The transformers in Shikoku, which also have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a half triangle, will have “hat shaped” short horizontal insulators at the end.

metas.title: Chugoku cross-shaped bar
metas.description: The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.

metas.title: Kansai pole top
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region. Make sure it looks exactly the same with that little thing on the wires in the middle(idk how to call it lol)

metas.title: Kansai transformers
metas.description: The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square. (Tohoku transformers are mounted in similar way but the bar will be connected to top of the square)

metas.title: Infrastructure - Arrow - Yellow/Green
metas.description: This yellow and green arrow is found southwest of Sapporo.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Poleplate - Chubu
metas.description: Every region in Japan features a distinct plate on their utility poles.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Poletop - Chugoku
metas.description: This pole top, with four thin, skinny bars, is common in the Chugoku region.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Signpost Sticker - Aomori
metas.description: Most Japanese prefectures have unique stickers you can find on their signposts.
metas.comparison: The color of the top sticker varies.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Road Diamond - Aomori
metas.description: You can narrow down the prefecture you are in based on the style of road diamond.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - White Sticker
metas.description: A white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with black numbers.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Poletop Extension - 90° Angle
metas.description: These smaller attachments with a 90-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Shikoku.

metas.title: Landscape - Mount Fuji
metas.description: Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan, with a gradual incline and often snowy summit.
metas.comparison: Depending on the elevation, it can be seen from far away. This can create some excellent region guesses, especially if you account for direction and distance.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Poletop - Hokuriku
metas.description: This pole top, with two sides filled in and shaped like a tent, is common in the Hokuriku region.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Poletop - Chubu
metas.description: This pole top, with four thicker bars and a circle piece at the top, is common in the Chubu region.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Chubu
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a short top bar and horizontal bar below, is found the majority of the time in the Chubu region.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Red Number
metas.description: In Chugoku, a white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with red numbers. They may also be painted on the side.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Bollard - Black Stripe
metas.description: Some bollards on the island of Shikoku can have a black stripe just under the reflector. They can be found normally, attached to guardrails or walls.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Kanto
metas.description: This tuning fork pole top, with a long top bar that sticks out each end and horizontal bar(s) below, is found the majority of the time in the Kanto region.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Gas Tank
metas.description: Hot water, gas and propane tanks can be found more frequently in northern prefectures or high elevation mountainous areas. Here are a few common variations you can find:
metas.comparison: The standard hot water tank. Covered propane tanks. Exposed propane tanks. These cylindrical tanks. And finally, these circular tripod tanks. Moreover, these are even more common in rural towns or villages, where major water or gas lines are unavailable.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - One on Square
metas.description: In Tohoku, you may also find transformers mounted on the side of a square, with a straight bar mounted on the top of the square. Rarely, you may find a square without a bar.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While Kansai may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the bottom rather than the top.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Kyushu
metas.description: The transformers in Kyushu, which have a straight bar attached on the side of the pole with three insulators at the end, will have transformers mounted 180-degrees from one another.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / Zigzag Bar
metas.description: The transformers in Tohoku, which often have additional square holding brackets and the logo of the Tohoku Electrical Company, are sometimes mounted on a round plate with a zigzag bar.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Transformer - Black Tap Connector
metas.description: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Shosetsu
metas.description: Snow prevention roads, known as ‘Shosetsu’, are found mainly in northwest coastal prefectures. They appear as tiny circles in the pavement, and spray warm underground water to clear snow.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku
metas.description: This thick, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an octagonal reflector, and yellow stripe just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

metas.title: Vegetation - Bamboo
metas.description: In general, bamboo grows more often in the south, and slowly decreases further north. Population size and areas where it grows can vary, so use this information primarily in helping assist your region guess.

metas.title: Architecture - Northern Roofs
metas.description: The further you are north, roofs generally transition from tiled to level or flat sloped in order to compensate for heavy snowfall. Northern houses often have ladders attached to the side, giving roof access to clear snow.
metas.comparison: NOTE: In addition to north to south, high-elevation mountainous regions or high snowfall areas often use such roofs, even in more central or southern prefectures.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku (Black Variant)
metas.description: Additionally to regular Tohoku bollards, there are two other variations. You can find a black octagonal, and rectangular version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.

metas.title: General Architecture
metas.description:
Japanese architecture has many distinct and expressive styles, with many unique buildings.
These can range from traditional country houses, regional designs, modern large cities, coastal reinforced buildings, and anything in between.

metas.title: Landscape - Plains
metas.description: Japan is notably a very mountainous country. However, there are some regions that are quite flat, being the Nobi and Kanto plains. While at times they can look very similar, determining that it is one or the other can be very helpful.
metas.comparison: NOTE: While there are, of course, other flat areas in Japan, these two are the most recognizable.

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description: In Japan, simple white bollards with circular or rectangular reflectors at the top are commonly used. However, sometimes these bollards are black, or have other extensions. They can also have the city or prefecture written on it in kanji.

general_rules.text: Area codes are commonly found throughout the country and increase to the south. NOTE: Area codes ending with a 0 are often not regional, most notably 0120.

Hokkaido.text: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido(You can find similar rarely in northern prefectures of Japan)
Hokkaido plate can be recognized by having a lot of numbers in rows of 2.
This yellow and black arrow can be found on Hokkaido.
Cyrillic can be found on signs in the cities of Wakkanai and Nemuro, in northern Hokkaido.

You can find these chevron-like stickers, or more rarely orange ones, on guardrails in Hokkaido.

On the end or side of a guardrail. Stuck to metal posts between wire fences, which are often found in Hokkaido. On railings, which are often found on bridges, underneath the inside of the railing.
In Hokkaido, if there is more than one transformer, they will often be mounted on the sides of a square.
These artistically painted poles, made to resemble birch trees, are unique to the city of Date in Hokkaido.
This arrow, found in the Aomori prefecture (or more rarely Hokkaido), has distinct silver bolts around the border.
This alternate yellow and black design can often be found on the northern part of National Highway 275 in Hokkaido.
The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars.
Vertical traffic lights can be found in Hokkaido, and along the northwestern coast. The usual horizontal traffic lights can be found everywhere else.

The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.
These grey “insulator-esque” blocks, which wires are fed through, can be found in the regions of Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, Shikoku, and very rarely in Hokkaido.

Rice is mainly produced north of Tokyo. During growth, it resembles straws of grass. And when ready for harvest, brown husks are visible. They are also commonly planted in beds of water.

The regions of Chubu (21%), Kanto (15%), Tohoku (27%), and Hokkaido (7%) make up the majority of production.

Giant butterbur (commonly referred to as cabbage) is abundant in Hokkaido and some northern prefectures. Plants found south of Hokkaido often have smaller leaves. It is often found growing along the roadside.

Kerosine tanks, otherwise known as “Claymores”, can be found more commonly the further north you go. They are abundant in Hokkaido, but can be found in prefectures south of it, or in high elevation mountainous areas.

Japanese White Birch grows dominantly in the Chubu and Hokkaido regions, and to a lesser extent in Tohoku. Small areas of white birch can be found throughout Japan, so use this information primarily to help assist your region guess.

NOTE: Japanese Beech is another species of tree found in Japan. They, however, have more grey and spotted bark, as opposed to the mostly white Japanese White Birch.

Hokkaido has very limited winter and snow coverage. Unless you are certain, it is often better not to guess this prefecture. Though, if you do find yourself in Hokkaido, these regions are most likely. Other low amounts of miscellaneous coverage is primarily in the southern half of the island.

NOTE: While the Kanto transformer may also be mounted on two bars, Hokkaido will never have a wooden plate.

Yamaguchi.text: Yellow guardrails are exclusive to Yamaguchi prefecture.
These distinctive yellow guardrails can be found in the Yamaguchi Prefecture.
Guardrail endings with these red and yellow striped stickers can commonly be found across Chugoku, except in Yamaguchi. They can also rarely be found in Niigata.

This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.

NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.

This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite. NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.
These distinctive yellow guardrails can be found in the Yamaguchi Prefecture.
Guardrail endings with these red and yellow striped stickers can commonly be found across Chugoku, except in Yamaguchi. They can also rarely be found in Niigata.

Okinawa.text: Guy wires that look like paddle are unique to Kyushu and Okinawa.
Protruding bumps, sometimes darker reflector in the middle. Can also be found in Okinawa.
Transformers mounted opposite side of the pole with a straight bar mounted on the side of the pole with 3 insulators on one side at the end.(Okinawa has T shaped bar)
Okinawa can often be recognised by the white concrete buildings with flat roofs.
Sugarcane is almost exclusively found on the islands in southern Kyushu and Okinawa.
You can find these ‘Shisa’ guardian lions and house plaques with these specific characters in Okinawa. The colour and shapes of both can vary.
Transformers in Okinawa, which have a T-shaped bar attached on the side of the pole, will have transformers mounted on opposite sides of the pole.
Agricultural fields with red soil are commonly found on several southern islands, most notably on the islands of Miyakojima and Ishigaki in southern Okinawa.
Transformers in Okinawa, which have a T-shaped bar attached on the side of the pole, will have transformers mounted on opposite sides of the pole.
Sugarcane is almost exclusively found on the islands in southern Kyushu and Okinawa.

Gifu.text: This variation, found in the Gifu prefecture, is long and thin.

Tokyo.text: Tokyo City features a nice manhole design, with a 5 petal flower and many small circles on the outside.

Miyazaki.text: Green bands on guardrails are most commonly found in Oita and Miyazaki, but can be found on all of Kyushu.
Green bands on guardrails are most commonly found in Oita and Miyazaki, but can be found on all of Kyushu.

Toyama.text:
The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector.

NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.

The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector. NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.

Hiroshima.text: These unique red-tiled roofs are most commonly found in Chugoku, especially in the prefectures of Hiroshima and Shimane.

Ehime.text:
Cycling routes in Ehime use an outside white, with an inside blue line. They are more commonly found along the coast but may be found further inland too.

While exceptions do exist, and can be found in other prefectures, they are the extreme minority.

Green tea plants are often grown in hedged rows. You will often see these fans mounted on poles, which serve the purpose of preventing frost from falling on the plants.

The prefectures of Shizuoka (36%) and Kagoshima (34%) make up the majority of the production, with Mie (7%), Miyazaki (4%), and other prefectures (17%) making up the minority.

Chinese Silver Grass, referred to as Kyushu grass, is indeed very abundant on the island of Kyushu. However, use this tip with caution, as they can be seen outside of this area.

NOTE: Another notable region they can be found in is the prefectures of Niigata, Yamagata and Akita. Though, combining the rather large quantity found on Kyushu, its normally distinct vegetation, along with other information, there often will be a clear distinction.

The transformers in Hokuriku, which are attached with thin metal bars, often have these small “lamp” shaped insulators. There will never be a bar present except for the attachment mentioned above.

NOTE: The prefecture of Niigata will have the Tohoku transformer design, as opposed to Hokuriku one.

spotlight.text: You can find these ‘Shisa’ guardian lions and house plaques with these specific characters in Okinawa. The colour and shapes of both can vary.
Agricultural fields with red soil are commonly found on several southern islands, most notably on the islands of Miyakojima and Ishigaki in southern Okinawa.
Tokyo City features a nice manhole design, with a 5 petal flower and many small circles on the outside.
Cyrillic can be found on signs in the cities of Wakkanai and Nemuro, in northern Hokkaido.
These artistically painted poles, made to resemble birch trees, are unique to the city of Date in Hokkaido.

JE.name: Jersey
JE.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (4 regions covered).

metas.title: Red Granite
metas.description:
Jersey is home to large reserves of red granite.
As a result, it is a popular building material used for the construction of many walls and houses throughout the island.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Northern France Architecture
metas.description:
Similarly, the local architecture shares many characteristics with that of northern France.
This includes pastel-coloured walls and dark slate roofs.
However, British-style terraced houses are also common.

metas.title: Landscape
metas.description:
The island is shaped by a unique mix of British and Norman influences.
The many winding roads and hedgerows are reminiscent of English country lanes, with tree-covered roads being particularly common.
All images were taken by a Generation 2 camera.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

Parish.text: Most street name signs in Jersey are adorned with the coat of arms of the parish in which they are located. You can click on the graphic to enlarge it.

Helier.text: Contrasting with the island’s typically rural look, the area surrounding the capital city of St Helier is more urbanised, featuring taller buildings, narrower streets and a more lively atmosphere.

Les.text: The Les Mielles Nature Reserve is a vast, treeless expanse located on Jersey’s western coast. Combined with the gentle westward slope and partially overcast coverage, this makes for a very recognisable area.

October.text: Imagery containing a greenish-purple discolouration can be found in the southwest of the island. NOTE: This glitch typically makes parts of the screen appear darker than they actually are. In addition, it blends into the landscape more seamlessly than other glitches. Moreover, this glitch is not unique to Jersey. It can be found in other countries as well.

spotlight.text: The roads surrounding Jersey Airport can be recognized thanks to the visible boundary fence.
The La Collette Power Station is located on a peninsula south of the capital. Its chimney can be seen from various points along the south coast and serves as a useful reference point for pinpointing.

Victoria Ave runs along the island’s southern coast, immediately west of St Helier. It is the only divided road on Jersey and features a distinct maroon median. JO.name: Jordan
JO.key_meta: While driving on the right side, yellow outer lines with white middle lines are commonly found in Jordan, Israel, and the UAE.

metas.title: Black car meta
metas.description: While driving on the right side, yellow outer lines with white middle lines are commonly found in Jordan, Israel, and the UAE. The black back of the Google car without an antenna can help confirm you’re in Jordan 100%.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner
A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Basics

Coverage.text: Jordan only has Street View coverage in the far western part of the country. Coverage is limited to bigger towns and main roads in this area. NOTE: Coverage ends just north of Jerash. Even though Irbid is the second largest city of Jordan, it has zero official coverage. In the south, coverage extends all the way to the coastal town of Aqaba, but not south of it.

Highway 65 is a single lane, north to south highway. It features long, sandy stretches of road south of Feifa valley. Now and then, you may encounter overcast coverage on some sections. NOTE: When on the portion of road near the airport by Aqaba, you can find sunset coverage.

Amman.text: Amman is by far the largest city in Jordan with extensive coverage. It is a bustling, developed metropolis with a distinct “big city” feel to it. It is slightly hilly and most of the city consists of medium-sized apartment blocks.

Highway 40 is a recognisable divided road surrounded by low, green shrubbery that makes its way west of Amman through the hilly terrain into the sandy area close to the Dead Sea. NOTE: Y-shaped lamp posts as shown in the image can be found along the length of highway 40, making it distinguishable from highway 35 north of Amman.

Landscape.text: Highway 15 is the longest divided highway with coverage in Jordan. Most of the road is surrounded by desert landscape. It is also surrounded by rocky hills in the south closer to Aqaba. NOTE: Highway 35 north of Madaba and highway 40 west of Amman are also divided but do not feature a desert landscape, while the divided highway 80 in the south runs mainly from east to west, making it distinguishable.

Highway 35 connecting Amman and Jerash is a divided road surrounded by hills speckled with green vegetation. NOTE: Highway 40 west of Amman is also divided and features a similar landscape. However, the T-shaped lamppost shown in the image is only found on highway 35 which helps distinguish the two.

Near and in the city of Madaba, you will find flat fields which are sometimes tilled. They uniquely have the characteristic of rich, red soil. NOTE: The fields continue both north and south of Madaba, along Highway 35.

Wadi.text: This arid rolling hill valley is located near the almost dried out river of Wadi al Hasa on Highway 35. The rock is rounded and smooth, with a single lane highway running through the center.

Mountains.text: For a large majority of Highway 80 and its turns, this divided valley road is surrounded by large, rigid mountains. When turning onto the stretch of road leading to Aqaba, the mountains level off. NOTE: The road direction of Highway 80 is east to west, as opposed to Highway 15, which runs north to south.

Aqaba.text: This long stretch of jagged mountains can be found on the eastern to southern side of Aqaba.

spotlight.text: In Amman, taxis are yellow and green. NOTE: The colours of taxis can be useful to distinguish between Jordanian cities.
In Aqaba, taxis are olive green on the top and black at the bottom.
In Madaba, taxis are yellow with white bumpers.
In some parts of the town of Wadi Musa, unique mountains with distinctive, bulbous rock formations can be seen in the background.

West of the town of Wadi Musa, a collection of trekkers can be found in and around Petra, a rock-cut city from antiquity. This trekker coverage features highly eroded reddish rocks, narrow gorges, and occasionally groups of tourists crowding around the archaeological sites. NOTE: While not likely to appear in competitive or pinpointable maps, these trekkers are a mainstay in many maps, including the default World map. metas.title: Car
metas.description: All of the coverage in Kazakhstan was taken with a white pickup truck, which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Russian Infrastructure
metas.description: A lot of Kazakh infrastructure, from pedestrian signs, poles, houses, to bollards, is very similar to what you see in Russia.
