metas.title: Pedestrian Crossing
metas.description:
Like Russia, Kazakhstan uses yellow and white stripes on their pedestrian crossings.
However, unlike Russia the stripes often have white dashes on either side.
Sometimes, you can find the dashes without the stripes.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description: Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards. Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Landscape
metas.description:
Kazakhstan is a big and diverse country, which features a plethora of distinct landscapes like deserts, grassy steppes, mountain passes, and birch forests.
Most strikingly, most of the rural coverage in Kazakhstan is in a very empty, open and mostly flat landscape.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

general_rules.text: Kazakh area codes are useful to learn, and they generally follow an east to west pattern along three horizontal lines.

You can occasionally spot licence plate codes on the back of trucks and buses. The codes themselves follow an alphabetical order, with smaller numbers corresponding to regions that start with earlier letters. Note that cars do travel, and as such not all codes are reliable. Buses and smaller utility vehicles are the most reliable.

Driving.text: Driving directions can help you narrow down your options when you are on a rural road.

Terrain.text: Kazakhstan is a generally flat country, so getting locations that are hilly or mountainous are useful for narrowing the options. For example, the region around Karaganda is often either quite hilly, or you can see hills in the distance. Another notable set of hills would be the ones around Aktobe. And of course getting bigger mountains will mean you are in the south, or east.

Mountains.text: Tall mountains, which are often snow-capped, can be seen in southeastern Kazakhstan.
The East Kazakhstan Region is hilly and forested. It was covered in october, so you will see fall colours on the vegetation. The town of Ridder itself is flat, but surrounded by hazy mountains.

Max.text: The landscape in southern Kazakhstan near Uzbekistan is hilly and quite dry and shrubby, with a lot of orange looking grass. The landscape consists of dry but grassy rolling hills or dead flat agricultural land near Zhetisay. NOTE: These red and white KM markers that look like Kyrgyz ones, are only found near Zhetisay.

Pipes.text: Yellow boxes connected to the gas pipes are common outside houses in Shymkent, Turkistan, and Taldykorgan.

spotlight.text: In southern Almaty City, there is snow coverage in the mountains.
The Altyn Emel National Park is a barren grassland with snowy mountains in all directions. Some parts are very snowy. And in the eastern section, there is a small curvy mountain pass.
The only May coverage in Kazakhstan is found in the Almaty exclave of Alataou, which is east of Almaty proper. All of the coverage is sunny and the mountains are visible to the south.

KE.name: Kenya
KE.key_meta: If you see a snorkel on the Google car, you’re in Kenya.

metas.title: Unique car
metas.description: If you see a snorkel on the Google car, you’re in Kenya.
metas.comparison: However, the car is sometimes seen without it, so don’t rule out Kenya if the snorkel isn’t visible.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner
A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Basics

metas.title: Follow car
metas.description: In some of the Kenya coverage, you will be followed by a grey Toyota SUV.

metas.title: Pickup car
metas.description:
Sometimes you won't see Kenya snorkle and instead you will see gray/white pickup car with/without antenna and sometimes it might be even fully blurred.
But if you have a vibe that you are in Africa and you see pickup truck and you are driving on the left side you should be in Kenya(Or Namibia).
metas.comparison: Note:Other countries in Africa with pickup truck coverage drive on the right.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner

Coverage.text: Most of the coverage in Kenya outside of the southwest is limited to main roads. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Topo.text: The natural formation of land has great diversity between regions. The east and large portions of the north are extremely flat. In contrast, the further southwest you travel, the higher the elevation becomes on average. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Regional.text: Kenya has distinct regional climates. Some of these include: Humid Humid Semi-Arid Semi-Arid Arid Arid Very-Arid Very-Arid As regions vary, this means that there will be many transitional climates. Use this as a guide to quickly determine the general area to assist with region guessing. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Big.text: This Generation 3 grey car with a large snorkel is mostly found in the west, but can also be found in the Mombasa and Nairobi areas, and regions east of Nairobi near Kitui. NOTE: Most Generation 3 coverage has been overridden by Generation 4.

Small.text: This Generation 3 black car with a small snorkel is mostly found in the east of the country. You can also see it north and south of Nairobi. NOTE: Most Generation 3 coverage has been overridden by Generation 4.

Generation.text: Kenya has mostly Generation 4 coverage covered by a large grey Google car, with or without a snorkel. There are many metas regarding Generation 4, too many in fact to break down here. RESOURCE: Therefore, please use this document. It covers this area in depth, and was created by snowf_lake#9088. Key meta information can be found in the tips below. Other less extensive, but still noteworthy car meta, can be found in the spotlight section.

Tape.text: You can see pieces of white tape on the roof of the Google car in a lot of the coverage north and south of Nairobi.

A109.text: The A109 between Mombasa and Nairobi has light orange dirt and many hills around the road and in the distance. You will additionally see many transportation trucks delivering various goods. Most of the coverage between Mombasa and Emali also has a unique car, which has a cord on the left.

Mombasa.text: Mombasa and the other coastal towns are easily identified from the white sandy soil, palm trees and coastal feel.

Landscape.text: The far west areas of the country that are northwest and southwest of Kisumu are the most agricultural parts of the country. You will often see farms, grassy hills, and tall eucalyptus trees in this region of the country.

The northwest part of the country has very limited coverage, most of which is on the A1 or in Sibiloi National Park. It has faintly tan soil and sparse low trees. A lot of the coverage in this area is very flat, but you can also see hills or mountains.

Kitui.text: The area around Kitui is semi-arid, usually mountainous, and has light orange, sandy dirt.

Plonkit.text: White flowers, especially when they are in large numbers, are commonly found east of Chyulu Hills National Park, as well as in Tsavo National Park and near the A109 south of Nairobi.

National.text: Kenya has many unique Google cars in and around its National Parks and Reserves. These are still identifiable by the snorkel which is present in almost all of them. Many of the National Park and Reserve cars must be used in conjunction with landscape, as they can be found in multiple areas. You can learn more about these National Parks and Reserves in the spotlight section.

spotlight.text: The B9 in the Northeast is entirely unpaved and has bright reddish orange dirt with many trees surrounding the road. Most of it is very flat, but the coverage at the western end of the road can have hills and mountains. The soil also transitions into a more sandy colour.

The A2 between Isiolo and Marsabit has many plants alongside the road and you will often see large mountains in the distance. The stretch going through Namunyak Wildlife Conservation Trust will have a very large mountain range to the west.

North of Marsabit will be much flatter, with some mountains in the distance. The stretch just north or Marsabit will have mountains visible to the south, while further north, a different range can be seen. It will also have much less vegetation.
The A3 north of Garissa is very unique, with light coloured soil and many green trees on either side of the road.

The western part of the C34 is a flat, east to west road. There are two long, straight sections with an abundance of sugar cane. Furthermore, you will see a large mountain range north along the entire mentioned stretches of road.
This car that is covered in specks of dirt is unique to these stretches of the A3, B9, and the Habaswein-Dadaab Road connecting the two.

Nairobi is the largest city in the country, and capital of Kenya. It is the only city to have a considerable amount of skyscrapers, and is highly developed. It is densely populated, and is surrounded by small, poor settlements.

In a lot of the coverage north of Mt Kilimanjaro, the mountain is visible to the south, usually obscured by clouds. In the city of Oloitoktok, the mountain will often be visible directly to the south. NOTE: The map shows the location of Mt Kilimanjaro, but it can be seen from very far away.
Homa Bay has this protruding hill to the east that is often visible.
Mara Triangle has no considerable mountains and most of it is either flat or hilly. It has a white car that can be found in other Kenyan National Parks. Generation 4 coverage exists there as well.

Amboseli National Park has a grey car with a small snorkel. It is very flat with tan grass, few trees, and dried up lake beds. You can always see the base of Kilimanjaro to the south, with most of it obscured by clouds.

Aberdare National Park has a grey and brown car that features a large snorkel. Almost all of the coverage is outside of the National Park, with only two roads within the park covered. The main road through the park has these rubber bands on the roof rack, which can only be found in one other National Park in Kenya.

Between Kitale and Mt Elgon, you can find the Aberdare car as well, but it will always have rubber bands, unlike in Aberdare where it will only have them on the main roads through the park. It can be differentiated from Aberdare by its redder dirt, and greener landscape.

The area surrounding and between Kerio and Lodwar uses the same car as the Aberdare National Park, but with a vastly different landscape. It is very sandy, dry, and has little vegetation. You may also find yourself in Generation 3 coverage without car meta.
This stretch of the B8 just north of Kibaoni has many succulents on the side of the road.

metas.description: All other Laos coverage was taken with unique google car but if you have a vibe you are in Thailand but you will see yellow plates, ppl are driving on the right etc you will be in capital of Laos - Vientiane.

metas.title: Historical Architecture
metas.description:
Luang Prabang is the former royal capital of Laos and a UNESCO heritage site.
The city has a lot of historical architecture, including several temples.
Many buildings make use of traditional dark wooden architectural elements.

LV.name: Latvia
LV.key_meta: The Latvian word for street is "iela." This word is unique to Latvian, so if you see a street sign with it, you can be sure you're in Latvia.

metas.title: Street name ending - iela
metas.description: The Latvian word for street is "iela." This word is unique to Latvian, so if you see a street sign with it, you can be sure you're in Latvia.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: Half-circle/flat curved shape bollards with a rectangular reflector on the front and two circular reflectors on the back are common. The reflectors can be white or orange, and sometimes these bollards have numbers on them.
metas.comparison: Estonian bollards might look similar, but they have a rounded shape and will never have numbers on them.

metas.title: Electricity marker
metas.description: You can find these electricity markers in Latvia — they have a distinct shape with a black tip and a different color underneath.

metas.title: Hook pole
metas.description: Wooden poles with alternating pattern of hook-shaped insulators are really common in Latvia. They might appear sometimes in other countries but if you see them with flat landscape you gonna be most likely in Latvia(If you vibe baltics). Always try using other clues to confirm it.

metas.title: Bus Stop Sign
metas.description:
The bus has five windows.
Within the Baltics, this is unique to Latvia.
The other two Baltic countries have four windows.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Iela
metas.description:
The Latvian word for street is iela.
This word is unique to Latvian.
Very rarely, you might see ‘gatve’ in Riga (abbreviated as gat.).
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Thick Red Border Signs
metas.description:
Each Baltic country has a slightly different border for its warning and speed signs.
Latvian signs have a thick red border, with a thin white outline around it.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Long Leg Latvia
metas.description: You can identify Latvia from their guy with weirdly long legs. Long as hell for what. It's arguable Russia/Ukraine/Lithuania has long legs but even so they have 3 zebra stripes, not 5.

metas.title: Kilometre Markers
metas.description:
All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker.
However, they can be distinguished from each other by their angle relative to the road.
In Latvia, the marker will be parallel to the road.
It only has a number on one side.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description:
Latvian bollards have a thin, slightly curved shape.
They have a rectangular reflector on the front, and two circular reflectors on the back.
The reflectors can be white or orange.
The black strip is slightly angled.
Bollards often have numbers below the front reflector.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: White Bricks & Corrugated Roofs
metas.description:
Latvian architecture generally consists of a combination of wood and white brick, typically with somewhat steep corrugated metal roofs.
Slightly modern houses with pastel coloured stone walls and houses with a combination of wood with another material, particularly white brick, are also common.

Jelgava.text: The area south of Jelgava is characterised by a wide open landscape with considerably less forest and more fields than most of the rest of Latvia.

spotlight.text: The historic downtown area of Riga is characterised by majestic art nouveau architecture, that is in places reminiscent of the architecture in Vienna. This is unique within Latvia, and even within the entire Baltics.

LB.name: Lebanon
LB.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (5 regions covered).

Coverage.text: Most of the coverage is concentrated near the west coast, north of Beirut.

Flat.text: The region around Zahle has flat agricultural fields, with mountains visible to the northwest.

Snow.text: Coverage where snow is visible on mountain tops, or on the ground, is found in the northeastern mountains, east of Tripoli.

Very.text: Northern Lebanon is very flat and agricultural. You might see the mountains to the southeast.

Hint.text: A visible black car can be found in and around Zahle.

spotlight.text: The Generation 3 trekker coverage in Lebanon is extremely limited, mostly being found around tourist attractions, university campuses and trails. Note that due to the large number of distinct trekkers, this guide will only cover those that are considered pinpointable.

Beirut is the capital of Lebanon and the only covered city with many modern high-rise buildings. While the city might not be clearly visible from all parts of the coverage, you will almost always be able to see urban buildings or infrastructure in the background.
Coverage was taken along parts of the promenade in Beirut, with a grey brick pavement and a large number of fan palms.
Université Saint Joseph, southeast of central Beirut can be recognised by the old, grand-looking sandstone building.
Campus Debbieh of the Beirut Arab University consists of somewhat sparsely built large modern sandstone buildings on top of a forested hill. The ocean can typically be seen far away to the west.
The Lebanese International University (LIU) can be recognised by the many large stone buildings having unpainted bottom floors while the floors above are painted beige.
The University of Balamand has a lot of modern white painted buildings. The buildings often have a very cubic look.
The Lebanese American University, east of Byblos, has a very urban look, with a lot of construction work and large modern buildings.
The ancient city of Byblos is one of the oldest cities in the world and can be recognised by the many old historical buildings, almost all built out of the same type of unpainted stone bricks.
The trekker near Bsharri can be recognised by the large canyon to the south.
In Baalbek you can find a large complex of Roman ruins.
The Mseilha fortress can be found southwest of Tripoli and is built on a monolithic limestone rock.
The only rural coastal road with trekker coverage in Lebanon can be found southwest of Tripoli.

LS.name: Lesotho
LS.key_meta: One of the best ways to identify Lesotho is by its characteristic ‘Lesotho mountains.’ These mountains are bare and treeless, often with tabletop-like shapes and recognizable horizontal rocky ridgelines.

metas.title: Landscape
metas.description: One of the best ways to identify Lesotho is by its characteristic ‘Lesotho mountains.’ These mountains are bare and treeless, often with tabletop-like shapes and recognizable horizontal rocky ridgelines.
metas.comparison:
You can confirm it's Lesotho by the white back of the Google car, driving on the left, yellow outer lines, and the sun in the north. The only other countries in Africa with that combination are: Eswatini (the hills there have trees and usually tall golden grass around)
Botswana (which is super flat)
South Africa (though this is rare, as most of the coverage now uses the blue back of the Google car).

Coverage.text: Coverage in Lesotho is very sparse, particularly in the southeastern half, where it’s mostly limited to yellow roads. All urban coverage is found in the northwest.

Flat.text: Lesotho can be roughly divided into two regions, based on landscape: flat and mountainous. In the flat region, the road itself runs through a mostly flat or hilly landscape. “Flat” is a bit of a misnomer, as you will usually still see tabletop-like mountains around you. However they will usually be significantly further away from the road, giving you a more clear line of sight. This “flat” part is the region with the most coverage, settlements and agriculture.

Mountainous.text: Conversely, in the mountainous part, the road will usually be directly on the side of the mountain, instead of slightly away from it. The mountains are often large, closer to the road, and covered in green grass. Coverage in the mountainous part of Lesotho is very sparse: there are only 6 main roads (and a couple of very small off-roads) with coverage, meaning that you can learn each road by heart if you feel so inclined.

spotlight.text: There are two large man-made water reservoirs in the mountainous part of Lesotho, which can be seen from several road sections. The larger Katse reservoir is visible from parts of the A25. The smaller Mohale reservoir is visible from an off-road of the A3. NOTE: Do not confuse these with the small industrial lake found near the Letseng diamond mine.
The section of the A2 between Maseru and Mafeteng has by far the best road quality in all of Lesotho.
On a section of the A25, just east of the big reservoir, the camera is covered in raindrops in one direction.

Several sections of the A5 south of Nyakosoba are under construction. As a result, you will often see a sort of temporary “bollard” next to the road, consisting of a stick that is mostly painted white. Even on sections without the bollard, you can often recognize this road, as it is a wide dirt road with very dark brown soil.

The road going from Ramatsediso to Sehlabathebe NP, in the southeast on the border with South Africa, is very recognizable. Consider guessing there if the following three things are all true for your location: Unpaved road with light brown soil. Unpaved road with light brown soil. Good weather with little fluffy clouds. Good weather with little fluffy clouds. Grassy landscape high in the mountains. Grassy landscape high in the mountains. You will also often be able to see exposed, light-coloured rocks next to the road.

The only city with a significantly urbanised downtown area is Maseru, the capital. All other towns have a very provincial feel in comparison to Maseru. Note that the suburbs of Maseru can still have a very rural feel.

Qacha's Nek is a very recognizable town that is located far away from most other towns, on the southeastern border with South Africa. It is situated right in the middle of green mountains, and it had noticeably bad weather when the Google car drove there.

LI.name: Liechtenstein
LI.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (13 regions covered).

Triesenberg.text: Triesenberg and its surroundings are a fairly densely populated area on the slope of the mountains just east of the Rhine River Valley, which can often be seen below to the west.

Eastern.text: Mountains can be seen all around in the coverage east of the mountain ridge that cuts through Liechtenstein.

Ruggell.text: Around Ruggell, there is a small, forested ridgeline to the south. This is a big contrast to the towering mountains seen elsewhere.

Between.text: Around Mauren, you can see the aforementioned ridge to the north, but this side of the hills is much more developed and urban. And to the south and southeast, you will see the much bigger mountains usually seen to the east.

Rolling.text: There is a set of rolling hills that run from Bendern, northeast, to the Austrian border. The rest of Liechtenstein is either very flat or in the mountains.

Balzers.text: In the flat area west of Balzers, with the northeast-oriented gridded roads, to the North/Northwest, you can often see two rocky peaks on the Swiss side.
Unlike the rest of Liechtenstein, Balzers sometimes uses black bus stop signs. NOTE:  Regular bus stops are also present.

Vaduz.text: Unlike the rest of Liechtenstein, Vaduz sometimes uses red bus stop signs. NOTE:  Regular bus stops are also present.

Outline.text: Blue street signs with a thin white border will place you either in the south of Liechtenstein or in the north around Bandern.
Blue street signs that don’t have an outline are found in Eschen.

Boring.text: Flat black signs are found in eastern Liechtenstein.

Schaan.text: Black signs with a white border and embossed letters can be found in Schaan.

Brown.text: These brown street signs with a font reminiscent of traditional German typefaces, along with a white border, are found in Vaduz and the northern towns.

Arrow.text: Brown street signs that have an arrow design are unique to Ruggell. NOTE: The regular brown signs are also present in Ruggell.

Generic.text: Browns signs which have a more ‘generic’ font will place you in Planken.

spotlight.text: This steep rocky cliff with trees at its base and on the top can be seen in and around Mäls.
The only lakes in Liechtenstein are located just south of Steg, near the middle of the mountains.

LT.name: Lithuania
LT.key_meta: Lithuanian bollards are wedge-shaped with rectangular reflectors: an orange one on the front and a white one on the back.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: Lithuanian bollards are wedge-shaped with rectangular reflectors: an orange one on the front and a white one on the back.

metas.title: Street name ending - g.
metas.description: The Lithuanian word for street is "gatvė," often abbreviated as "g." on street signs. If you see a street sign ending in "g.," you're likely in Lithuania.
metas.comparison: This word is almost entirely unique to Lithuanian, though very rarely, you might see "gatve" (abbreviated as "gat.") in the Latvian capital, Riga.

metas.title: Thin Red Border Signs
metas.description:
Each Baltic country has a slightly different border for its warning and speed signs.
Lithuanian signs have a relatively thin red border, with a thin white outline around it.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description:
Lithuanian bollards are wedge-shaped.
They have an orange reflector on the front, and a white reflector on the back.
Both reflectors are rectangular.
You may find this thin version as well.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: G.
metas.description:
The Lithuanian word for street is gatve, often abbreviated as g. on signs and Google Maps.
This word is almost entirely unique to Lithuanian.
However, very rarely, you might see gat. in the Latvian capital of Riga.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Less Forest Cover
metas.description:
Lithuania has less forest cover than the other two Baltic countries.
As a result, the landscape appears more open and agricultural.
Your mileage may vary depending on the round however, so use this meta with some caution.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Kilometre Markers
metas.description:
All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker.
However, they can be distinguished from each other by their angle relative to the road.
In Lithuania, the marker will be at a 45° angle towards the road.
The sign itself has an L-shape.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Light Colored Bricks
metas.description:
Lithuanian architecture primarily consists of light coloured brick buildings, usually with somewhat steep corrugated metal roofs.
Wooden buildings are also fairly common, however less so than in Estonia.
Pastel painted stone buildings are somewhat common, especially in newer suburbs.

metas.title: Lithuania Fatty
metas.description: 3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. > Cross off Estonia and Russia (detailed guy in Estonia, Yellow borders in Russia) and you're left with Lithuania and Ukraine. Lithuania's guy is a liiittle bit more fat in the torso than Ukraine and the blue is generally more vibrant than Ukraine.

Elevation.text: Lithuania is overall a fairly flat country, with no hills over 300 metres. However, you can sometimes distinguish the hilly areas from the more flat areas. The biggest hills are in the southeast, with some hills in the central part of the west.

Eastern.text: Metal pole tags are predominantly found in the eastern part of the country. For more information on Lithuanian pole stickers and car metas, please see this document.

spotlight.text: The Curonian Spit is a long thin sand-dune spit south of Klaipeda, that separates the Curonian Lagoon from the Baltic Sea. The main road on this spit, road 167, has a recognizable combination of landscape and road direction: The road runs in an approximate north-south direction and has Generation 4 coverage. The road runs in an approximate north-south direction and has Generation 4 coverage. The road is surrounded on all sides by forest with many Baltic pines. In many places, you will see slightly windswept trees (visible in the example image).
On the Curonian Spit you can also find wooden, and often red, Scandinavian looking houses.

Rarely, you can see bilingual signs with Polish language in a small area southeast of Lithuania. Note that this is by no means very common, but it can help with getting very close guesses if you do see bilingual Polish-Lithuanian signs in an otherwise obvious Lithuanian setting.

LU.name: Luxembourg
LU.key_meta: Bollards in Luxembourg are black and white, wedge-shaped, and feature grey reflectors.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: Bollards in Luxembourg are black and white, wedge-shaped, and feature grey reflectors. Some have a distinctive indent in the lower half.
metas.comparison: They look very similar to German bollards, with the main difference being that the reflectors on German bollards are attached with two bolts, while those in Luxembourg have three.

metas.title: Yellow license plates
metas.description:
Luxembourg uses long yellow plates with a blue strip on the left.
Since Luxembourg is a small country, foreign cars with white plates are somewhat common.
metas.comparison: There are only a few other European countries that use yellow plates for private vehicles:

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: Bollards are black and white. They are wedge-shaped and have grey reflectors. Some have a distinctive indent in the lower half. The bollards of Belgium, the Netherlands and France look very different.
metas.comparison: NOTE: They look more or less identical to German bollards. The most notable difference is that the reflectors on German bollards have two bolts, while in Luxembourg they have three.

general_rules.text: Local road numbers have three digits. They are geographically clustered by first digit. The first digits range from 1-3. 1xx is found in the southern half. 1xx is found in the southern half. 2xx is found in and around the capital. 2xx is found in and around the capital. 3xx is found in the northern half. 3xx is found in the northern half.

Lux.text: The north of the country is hillier and has an overall higher elevation than the south.

Vineyards.text: Vineyards are primarily found in the southeast of the country.

spotlight.text: Some of Luxembourg City’s downtown area was covered by a Generation 3 urban trekker. Occasionally, the trekker’s sunglasses and greying hair can be seen. To report inaccuracies, suggest new clues or give general feedback about our content, please use this form: https://www.plonkit.net/feedback

MO.name: Macau
MO.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (2 regions covered).

Dense.text: Dense apartment buildings with gridded, narrow streets and cars parked on both sides can be found in this region in the northern half of Macau.

Rural.text: A hilly, rural region of Macau can be found in the south. Roads are narrow, winding up hills with trees on both sides. A helpful clue are the lamp posts, which are commonly seen. When this area appears in a world map, it can be confusing to newer players, as there are very few language or architecture clues available. The washed out early Generation 2 coverage can help with identifying it as being located in Macau.

spotlight.text: The Sai Van Bridge can be recognized by these unique cuboid towers with arches in them.
Red guardrails can be seen on the Amizade Bridge.

MG.name: Madagascar
MG.key_meta: A white boat, containing many people, can be found going around the island of Nosy Ambariovato.

general_rules.text: A white boat, containing many people, can be found going around the island of Nosy Ambariovato.

Coverage.text: Street View in Madagascar is very limited, with a mixture of land and boat coverage, most of which is on or near the west coast. It is worth noting that almost all the coverage was taken using trekkers, with only two exceptions, both of which have a visible, unique Street View car. Because of the limited coverage, this guide will be structured differently than most other guides. It will be divided into two main sections: one for land coverage and one for boat coverage, which in turn is divided into subsections based on region.

Ambanja.text: The coverage in Ambanja can be recognized by a person wearing a dark blue T-shirt and black sunglasses.

Nosyambariovato.text: The coverage on the island of Nosy Ambariovato can be recognized by the people, one wearing a blue T-shirt and sunglasses on their forehead, one with a light red T-shirt and one with a darker red tank top. There is also a fourth person in some of the coverage, wearing a light blue T-shirt. The coverage is very hilly and forested.

Nosyambariovatotown.text: There is a village by the northern shore of Nosy Ambariovato.

Ambikytown.text: Ambiky can be recognized by the large number of palms combined with the brown, sandy dirt road. In most of the coverage, there is a person walking in front of the trekker with a grey T-shirt and a brown backpack.

Ambikybeach.text: A beach west of Ambiky can be recognized by the low trees combined with low mountains to the northwest.

Ambikyforest.text: An area with coverage south of Ambiky can be recognized by the large, solitary green bushes combined with a very slight red tinge in the dirt. Certain parts of the coverage are quite wet.

Sambirano1.text: There are three major sections of coverage along the Sambirano river, most of which can be identified with the single person, wearing a dark blue T-shirt and sunglasses on their forehead. The same person is also present on Nosy Ambariovato.

Sambirano2.text: A small section of the coverage by the Sambirano river has two different people present on the coverage; one with a red T-shirt and white cap, and one with a spotted dress.

Atollnorth.text: A couple of atolls on the central west coast can be seen on Street View. The northernmost is the smallest, and is easily recognizable as it only consists of sand and you can always see from one shore to the other. NOTE: Among the five atolls with land coverage, only the two furthest south appear on the map.

Atollsouth.text: The other atolls can be recognized by their small size relative to other landmasses and the broad leaved palms which is rarely found anywhere else in the country.

Antananarivo.text: Most of the coverage in Antananarivo was taken on the side of a hill looking out over the city, which leads up to the Queen’s Palace, which can be seen near the top of the hill.

Andranomena.text: The coverage on the RN8 between Andriamena and Marofandilia can easily be recognized by the large silver roof rack on the Street View car. The coverage is very dry and sandy.

Andranomenatrekker.text: The trekker next to the RN8 can be recognized by its extreme dryness, combined with the four people wearing red, blue, grey and light blue respectively.

Baobabavenue.text: Baobab Avenue is easy to recognize by the extremely broad trunked baobab trees along the side of the road.

Morondavatown.text: Morondava is most easily recognized by the bald person wearing either a light green or a light red striped shirt. It is also one of few towns where the trekker walks on a paved road.

Morondavabeach.text: Morondava has a very smooth sand beach, with the ocean to the northwest. There are a large number of palms visible.

Belosurmertown.text: Belo Sur Mer can be recognized by the large number of palms combined with the blanket of white sand on the ground.

Belosurmerbeach.text: The beach outside Belo Sur Mer can be recognized by the somewhat dirty sand and the curved shoreline with the ocean to the northwest.

Kirindymitea.text: Kirindy Mitea National Park can be most easily recognized by having the reddest soil present on Street View in Madagascar.

Manahycar.text: A car with a barely visible grey metal roof rack can be seen by Manahy. There are some locations where the car is completely blurred out, where the shape of the blur is the best indication of the area.

Manahytrekker.text: A piece of coverage, partly taken on a large grassy field, and partly on the side of a sand dune, can be found south of Manahy.

Nosyratafanika.text: A village with the shore to the east can be found north of Andavadoaka.

Capitsere.text: A small, very sandy village with the shore to the north can be seen on a small cape north of Andavadoaka. Part of the coverage was taken just outside the shoreline.

Andavadoakatown.text: The town of Andavadoaka can be recognized by three different people appearing on the coverage; One wearing a greyish hat and a light blue shirt, and two with red and white T-shirts.

Andavadoakatrekker1.text: The main part of the trekker coverage surrounding Andavadoaka can be recognized by either the person wearing a greyish hat and light blue shirt or a person wearing a yellow T-shirt.

Andavadoakatrekker2.text: A second Trekker, going to the northeast of Andavadoaka can be recognized by a person with a light blue T-shirt.

Cow1.text: A blue cart dragged by a black cow on the left and a brown-white cow on the right can be found south of Andavadoaka.

Cow2.text: Another cart dragged by a white cow on the left and a black and white cow on the right can be found just south of Andavadoaka.

Velondriaketrekker1.text: A small seaside village, with little to no visible people can be found in the northern end of the bay, south of Andavadoaka.

Velondriaketrekker2.text: Coverage on a somewhat rocky ground with no people following the trekker can be found southwest of the bay.

Velondriaketrekker3.text: Coverage with multiple different people walking near and around the trekker, and with a small village to the west, can be found in the southeastern part of the bay. Part of the coverage goes through a very shallow body of water.

Velondriakenets.text: A cluster of fishing nets can be found in the bay.

Tsaranoro.text: The Tsaranoro Massif is a large monolithic mountain with trekker coverage. The steep mountainsides, combined with the mountainous area surrounding the coverage makes it very recognizable. The four people following the trekker can also occasionally be a useful clue.

Tsaranoroforest.text: A small part of the coverage in Tsaranoro was taken inside a forest, which occasionally hides the surrounding mountains. The best way to recognize this area is the relatively dark coverage, combined with the four people following the trekker.

Tsaranorocamp.text: A small settlement is found in the northeastern end of Tsaranoro. The mountains can typically be seen in the background.

Toliara.text: Toliara can be recognized as being a generally quite busy-looking town and the only large town on Madagascar with no person following the trekker.

Staugustintown.text: Two pieces of coverage can be recognized by two people following the trekker; one with a yellow tank top and one with a blue T-shirt. The first of these two parts is located in the town of St Augustin.

Staugustintrekker.text: The second part with the same two people is found to the east of St Augustin, going through a hilly landscape with a lot of shrubs.

spotlight.text: A mainly blue boat can be found along the coast south of Nosy Ambariovato.
A row boat containing five people with a wide wooden frame surrounding it can be found northwest of Ambohimena.

A boat going up the Sambirano River can be seen with two people; a tourist with a blue T-shirt and a gondolier with a brown shirt. The northernmost part of the coverage is very dark, as it was taken during sunset.
The boat covering some small atolls along the central parts of the west coast can be recognized by the driver, wearing a white cap and no shirt.

The boat north of Andavadoaka can mostly be recognized by the large sail almost filling up the entire screen and the bow which is painted yellow and blue. Note that the sail is not present in the northern parts of the coverage.

The boat in the bay south of Andavadoaka can be recognized by either the somewhat smaller sail than the one north of Andavadoaka, or the person sitting by the bow wearing a red T-shirt with the text “Diesel”. Beware that only one of the two will appear on most of the coverage.

Four people; one dressed in red, one in blue and one in yellow in the back, and one dressed in brown at the front, can be seen on a boat by the town of St Augustin. To report inaccuracies, suggest new clues or give general feedback about our content, please use this form: https://www.plonkit.net/feedback

MY.key_meta: Malaysian licence plates are black and generally have two white sections.

metas.title: License plate
metas.description: Malaysian licence plates are black and generally have two white sections. These are visible even when blurred.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Indonesian licence plates are also black, but they will have three white sections.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta South East Asia - Beginner

metas.description: This is a typical Malaysian directional sign. Green background and hexagonal yellow highway shields are unique to Malaysia.

metas.description:
These thick yellow bars are also almost exclusive to Malaysia.
NOTE: You can very rarely see similar patterns in Hong Kong.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta South East Asia - Beginner

metas.title: Double white middle line

from_maps: A Learnable Meta South East Asia - Beginner

metas.title: Black sticker
metas.description: Electricity poles in mainland Malaysia often have black stickers on them, which can have different designs but are always black with white text and sometimes other elements. These stickers are quite distinct, so if it looks like you're in Southeast Asia, it's worth checking the poles for them.

metas.description: Stop signs in Malaysia always have the word "Stop" written in Malay (Berhenti).

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description: Malaysian bollards will often have the colours black, white, grey and red. Here are three examples of typical Malaysian bollards.
metas.comparison: NOTE: There can be multiple varieties of these bollards, but the layout is mostly the same.

general_rules.text: Each Malaysian state, excluding the three federal territories, has its own road numbering system with a unique letter at the start of the road number. NOTE: Sabah also has A roads, but only the A2 and A7.
Malaysian postal codes are useful to know, since they can be found on most street signs in the country.

Johor.text: Yellow street name signs are specific to the state of Johor.
Black stickers with the text ‘TEL TNB’ at the bottom, are only found in Johor.

Yellow street name signs with a black outline are specific to the state of Johor. NOTE: This arrow-shaped street sign, regardless of its colour, is exclusive to Malaysia. NOTE: Yellow signs are also found in southern Negeri Sembilan, however only the tip of the arrow will be black.

Perlis.text: Trash bins with a logo resembling leaves are found in Perlis and Kedah.
These isolated rock formations, rising abruptly from an otherwise flat landscape, can be found near the Thai border in Perlis state.
Trash bins with a logo resembling leaves are found in Perlis and Kedah.
These isolated rock formations, rising abruptly from an otherwise flat landscape, can be found near the Thai border in Perlis state.

Sabah.text: Thin metal poles with two parallel pole tops are exclusive to the Sabah region of Borneo.
Thin metal poles with two parallel pole tops are exclusive to the Sabah region of Borneo.
Green street signs that form an arrow shape and have a yellow hexagonal symbol with the letters JKR on the left side are found in Sabah.

Assuming you are on Borneo: the state of Sabah is very mountainous, and much of the coverage is on mountain roads like this one. NOTE: Sarawak generally has flatter roads. Even if you see mountains, they will usually be at a distance.

Sarawak.text: This lamp post with a supporting piece of sheet metal resembling a boomerang is found in Sarawak.
Electricity poles on the Borneo side typically have a 2-1 insulator configuration, and a long diagonal wooden support. They are exclusive to the Sarawak region of the island.
White pole stickers are only found on electricity poles on the island of Borneo, in Sarawak.

Electricity poles on the Borneo side typically have a 2-1 insulator configuration, and a long diagonal wooden support. They are exclusive to the Sarawak region of the island. NOTE: Indonesian poles can look similar, but they are usually not made of wood, and use smaller or no diagonal supports.
This lamp post with a supporting piece of sheet metal resembling a boomerang is found in Sarawak. NOTE: It is more common in cities other than Kuching.

Negeri Sembilan.text: Trash bins with a logo resembling an ‘S’ are found in the states of Negeri Sembilan, Malacca and Johor.
Trash bins with a logo resembling an ‘S’ are found in the states of Negeri Sembilan, Malacca and Johor.

Kuala Lumpur.text: Trash bins with this logo featuring a sunny landscape, saying ‘Alam Flora’ are found in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The logo will occasionally be absent, and it will just say ‘Alam Flora’.
Trash bins with this logo featuring a sunny landscape, saying ‘Alam Flora’ are found in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The logo will occasionally be absent, and it will just say ‘Alam Flora’.

spotlight.text: Urban areas in Labuan are dotted with blue cylindrical containers.
This unique grey car with a long front antenna can be found in Gunung Mulu National Park, Sarawak.

MT.name: Malta
MT.key_meta: If you see a license plate with a blue strip while driving left with this climate/landscape, you know you're in Malta.

metas.title: Vibes
metas.description: If you see a license plate with a blue strip while driving left with this climate/landscape, you know you're in Malta. If you can't see the driving direction, use other clues like limestone rock walls to recognize Malta.

metas.title: Triq
metas.description: The Maltese word for street is “triq”, which can be seen on almost every street sign.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.description: Regular metal guardrails are rare on Gozo Island. Low stone barriers are more common instead.

metas.description:
Limestone rock walls are extremely common in Malta.
This alone is usually enough to determine that you are in Malta.

metas.title: Covered Balconies
metas.description:
This style of traditional covered balconies is very common on Maltese buildings.
They are often painted in bright colours.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Bus Route with 3
metas.description: Bus routes starting with 3 are only found on Gozo Island. These can be quite hard to see, meaning they are most useful in moving games.

metas.title: Architecture
metas.description:
The vast majority of buildings in Malta consist of low storey buildings, with white to beige coloured walls.
Buildings made of limestone are also fairly common.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Landscape
metas.description:
The general landscape of Malta consists of slightly hilly dry agricultural fields.
Many roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide, due to the island’s size.
Having a mediterranean climate, cacti and various dry shrubs can be seen.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

Gozo.text: Regular metal guardrails are rare on Gozo Island. Low stone barriers are more common instead.
Uniquely, all bus routes on Gozo Island are in the 300s. These can be quite hard to see, meaning they are most useful in moving games.

spotlight.text: These blue signs are unique to Valletta.

metas.title: Landscape - Mexicali Landscape
metas.description: The area around Mexicali features flat farmland with a ridge to the west. Washingtonia palms are very common and these poles made out of brown wood can be found.

metas.title: Vegetation - Sabal Yapa
metas.description: This palm grows pretty much exclusively in the Yucatán peninsula. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.
metas.comparison: Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

metas.title: Landscape - Guaymas Cliffs
metas.description: The town of Guaymas has a lot of jagged cliffs and mountains that make the area very distinct. The soil is also distinctly pinkish and organ-pipe cacti can be seen scattered on the hills and next to the road.

metas.title: Vegetation - Sabal Mexicana
metas.description: This palm seems to be prominent in coastal Texas, the east and the south coast of Mexico, Yucatán peninsula, and Guatemala. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.
metas.comparison: Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

metas.title: North - American Style Bungalows
metas.description:
Architecture in northern Mexico often features design elements from American style bungalows.
Many houses are coloured with light or pastel colours, gated and commonly have front yards.
Orange tiles inspired by Spanish colonial architecture are also typical.

general_rules.text: The first digit of Mexican area codes are regional and can be seen on this map.
Similarly, Mexican postal codes can be seen on this map. They will commonly appear at the bottom of street signs, and are ordered alphabetically based on state names.
Every state in Mexico has one or several unique licence plate designs. In this infographic you can find the most common and helpful ones.

Chihuahua.text: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.
Poles in Chihuahua city occasionally have a strip of white pole paint with the street name written in black or blue text.

The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.

The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.
A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.

Tlaxcala.text: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.
These clumps of grass in almost a teardrop shape are common in the region around Tlaxcala.
This Street View car with a yellow hood can be found by the La Malinche volcano in Tlaxcala.
This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

Baja California.text: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.
Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.
These reddish brown-tinged hills, often accompanied by large boulders, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.
This species is found mostly in Mexico, mainly in Sonora and southern Baja California and Northern Sinaloa. If the cactus is significantly larger than 3m, it's probably in Southern Baja.
These reddish brown-tinged hills, often accompanied by large boulders, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.
The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.

Quintana Roo.text:
Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.
These thin, white-barked trees can be found in the Yucatan peninsula, but are most prevalent in Quintana Roo.
Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo. NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.

Zacatecas.text: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.
It is native to central mexico, most commonly found in Zacatecas and San Luis Potosí although it can be seen anywhere from Nuevo León down to Puebla, in dry regions.

The 54 is a divided highway that runs through northeastern Zacatecas which features yucca trees spammed on both sides of the road. Additionally, the streetview car is often exposed and appears almost white due to the sunlight.
Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

Oaxaca.text: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.

blue, but less blue than tequilana, smaller grouping

If you see a cactus in a coastal area, you're probably in Oaxaca.
Oaxaca is very diverse in Cacti, so if you see a strange cactus, or one that isn't explained in this map, you can consider going Oaxaca.
The Eurus Wind Farm is located in southeast Oaxaca and is the largest wind farm in Mexico. Rows of wind turbines can be found along the 190 around Juchitán de Zaragoza.

The area around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south of it in Oaxaca often feature rolling hills with really distinct orange and beige-tinged soil, passing from one colour to the other with each hill. The beige-tinged soil can be seen more prominent in some locations.
This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is mainly found in Oaxaca.

Yucatan.text: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

Comment from Vincent: When not in the sun, the rock walls appear darker, but it's likely the same type of rock.

This palm is recognizable through its round fan leaves.

Within Mexico, it's usually found in Yucatan.
These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

Jalisco.text: Vast fields of blue agave (Agave tequilana), used to produce tequila, are mostly found in Jalisco and Nayarit.
Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

Commonly known as the blue agave, A. tequilana is immediately recognisable by its blue, sharply protruding leaves. This is the agave from which tequila is extracted, and it mainly inhabits Jalisco, where it is almost always observed in magnificent fields which can even coalesce into vast shades of blue from a distance.

Similar, but different: A. anguistifolia. While it is difficult to distinguish them, A. tequilana is noticeably bluer. One other difference is that A. angustifolia is more commonly spotted in isolated groupings than A. tequilana, but expansive fields still exist.
Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

Sonora.text: The Saguaro Cacti can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.
Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.
The golden glow of the fruit cholla is also unmistakable, and present mostly in the Western Half of Sonora.

The Saguaro is endemic to the Sonoran Desert and is found primarily in western Sonora in Mexico, and in western Arizona in the US. Elevation is a limiting factor to its environment, as the saguaro is sensitive to extended frost or cold temperatures.

Campeche.text: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.
These red agricultural fields surrounded by dense forests of tropical trees are most common in northern Campeche.
These red agricultural fields surrounded by dense forests of tropical trees are most common in northern Campeche.

Nayarit.text: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.
Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

San Luis Potosi.text: The Blue Myrtle Cacti have short arms that uniformly curve and point upwards. It is abundantly found in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo.

Agave salmiana, also known as pulque agaves, have wide, smooth, curling leaves, and a crown-like appearance. They are common in the central Mexican valley and further north around the city of San Luis Potosi.
If it is present in groups, Tree Cholla is usually a good indication of San Luis Potosi.
Poles with a mesh body are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.

The tree cholla is a cactus, and its skeletal, discoloured arms spurting in every direction make it recognisable.

Mostly found in San Luis Potosi, Queretaro and Hidalgo, often in Coahuila and Durango and rarely in Zacatecas.
This extremely long and flat ridge is found in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosi.

Thatched roofs are most common in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi.
They can also be found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.

Myrtillocactus Geometrizans is a species of cactus in the genus Myrtillocactus, native to central and northern Mexico. It is especially abundant in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo, and much more rarely Guanajuato.

Agave lechuguilla is a very frequent sighting in the hills of Durango and Coahuila, particularly around the cities of Saltillo and west of Torreon. More rarely it can be found in San Luis Potosi and Hidalgo. It is distinguished by its slick, lime-green leaves that almost look as if they are combed to one side.

Agave salmiana, colloquially the pulque agave, is native to central Mexico. Agaves in general are distinguishable by their crown-like appearance, with stiff leaves which fan outwards symmetrically. The pulque agave is no different, but has green leaves, relatively smooth edges, and flat leaves that curl slightly away from the central axis.

Note its distribution, in an arc around Mexico City and a second pocket of endemism which straddles San Luis Potosi city and Aguascalientes.
Poles with a mesh body are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.

Queretaro.text: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.
This lamp with black front and back edges and a white middle section is found in Santiago de Queretaro.

Most lamp posts and lamp arms in Aguascalientes city are yellow.

NOTE: They are not exclusive and are only very common.
Red brick buildings are mostly concentrated in the states west of Mexico City, specifically Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.

Sinaloa.text: Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.
This red Street View car with a black roof can be found in the town of La Seca in Sinaloa.

The 40D that crosses the Sinaloa-Durango state line is recognizable by the stunning lush cliffs and mountains along the road. The highway commonly passes through tunnels and the road itself features double yellow middle roadlines.

Sabal Rosei is native to the Pacific coast of Mexico, from Sinaloa to Jalisco but mostly concentrated in the state of Nayarit. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color. Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.

The Indian Comb (Pachycereus pecten-aboriginum), is a common cactus that always implies Sinaloa, or south Sonora near Sinaloa, although technically its habitat extends elsewhere. Its densely packed branches emerge from a single stem, but most recognisable is its inflorescence - the brightly coloured flowers which usually adorn the tip of its arms.
Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.

Mexico City.text: Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half with a pink upper half.
This road divider with a yellow top and bottom edge is found all along the 95D from Mexico City to Acapulco.
Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.

White concrete block buildings are highly concentrated in the states surrounding Mexico city, and are generally more common to the east.
They can however still be found all over the country.
Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.
Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half with a pink upper half.

Veracruz.text: Sugarcane can be found all over the country, but by far most common in Veracruz.

These fences made out of trees with red-coloured bark are commonly found in Veracruz.

NOTE: These tree fences can still be found in other coastal states and are best utilised when combined with other clues.
The area around Poza Rica in Veracruz features a lot of citrus tree plantations. It is common to see large amounts of these trees grown right on top of the hills.
The Attalea rostrata is a huge palm recognizable from its upright leaves, almost resembling an umbrella. It is mostly exclusive to Veracruz and Tabasco, and can be rarely found in Chiapas.

These fences made out of trees with red-coloured bark are commonly found in Veracruz. NOTE: These tree fences can still be found in other coastal states and are best utilised when combined with other clues.

This tall, flat ridge, with very prominent ridgelines, belongs to the Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve in Northern Coahuila near the US border.

NOTE: The only road the mountain range can be observed from is the Federal Highway 53 that leads to Boquillas del Carmen.

The rough century plant looks similar to the pulque agave but its leaves are blueish and it is much smaller. It is distributed nearly identically to A. lechuguilla (Durango and Coahuila, especially around Saltillo and West of Torreon,
rarely SLP and Hidalgo), and is often difficult to spot from the road, only barely visible in the distance in batches.

Guerrero.text:
Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.

NOTE: This is most reliable when the tar is not faded.
Coconut palms can be found all across the coast, but are often found in large groups in Guerrero and Colima.
Pachycereus weberi is widespread in the Mexican states of Puebla, Guerrero, Morelos, Hidalgo and Oaxaca at altitudes of 600 to 1,500 m.
The species originates from Mexico (Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca, southern Puebla). It will almost always place you somewhere in Oaxaca, usually central in the state.

This tall, columnar cactus, with no branches, is native to northern Oaxaca and southern Puebla, and another of the many species present there. Much less commonly but still possibly it can be seen in central Guerrero.

Agave cupreata is a very rarely observed agave that is localised to central Guerrero. Its name is apt - it has a much more pronounced, cup-like appearance than other agaves, with the leaves lurching inwards. It is often found growing on walls in groups as depicted.
Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero. NOTE: This is most reliable when the tar is not faded.

Grainy pavement with a blue-ish grey tinge is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.

Poles with a lowered crossbar and a single support beam that extend from one end of the crossbar to the pole itself can be found in Durango.

In Pitaya the branches less organically sprout from the ground in the weed-like manner of the Organ Pipe, and instead curl smoothly outwards from a central stem.

It is mostly found in Jalisco, south of Guadalajara. Less commonly, it's seen in Guanajuato. It can be seen in Queretaro too, but surprisingly rarely.

Prickly pear cacti with a total absence of other cacti, yucca, agaves or in general succulent plants except for the prickly pear is generally a good signal for the centre-west (Jalisco, Guanajuato, Michoacan).

In the northeast most area of State of Mexico, around the town Nopaltepec, they often farm Opuntia in vast plains.
Farms of prickly pear are otherwise most commonly found in north east Morelos, where they foreground striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. These farms can be found randomly elsewhere in the country, but much less commonly; if there is a third most common location for them it would be Guanajuato.
Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

Its spiky thin leaves, protruding from the centre in a cylindrical formation, make it quite distinct from other common agaves.

metas.title: Vibe
metas.description:
Monaco is a rich and densely populated city state, with a Mediterranean feel to it.
The architecture is similar to cities in southern France and northern Italy, but more luxurious.
You will see a lot of apartment buildings, neoclassical details, and pastel colours.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

Harbour.text: In the harbour, there is an extensive Generation 3 trekker on a boat. The Google employee’s brown hair and sunglasses are visible. You can see Monaco’s skyline and the hills beyond it. There are a lot of expensive yachts around. This trekker shows up a lot in the official competitive game modes, so it is worth remembering. Mongolia very often has a visible Street View car as all of Mongolian coverage was driven with a large pickup truck.
The truck can have several features such as a tent on top, red side-view mirrors, a snorkel, and roof-racks.
All of these can be of help in identifying Mongolia.
