Forests.text: You can find forests, typically surrounded by grassy fields, all around northern Mongolia. Generally these will be Siberian Larches, with pines and birches being common as well.

Unpavedgrassyfields.text: Small dirt tracks within flat, vast grassy fields are mainly found in far eastern Mongolia.

Unpaveddesert.text: There are several areas with off-road desert coverage in southern Mongolia. Most of this coverage is directly south or east of the town of Mandalgovi.

Pot2Rdx.text: There are a couple of paved desert roads in southern Mongolia. You can learn more about these roads later in the guide.

Mqlkn4H.text: You can find arid steppe rangeland, characterised by the coarse soil, patchy grass, and small shrubs, throughout southwestern Mongolia.

B4Whmyy.text: These dry, rugged hills and mountains are common to see in far western Mongolia.

Rxhdqce.text: Lakes and rivers are much more common in western Mongolia.

Snow.text: Snow coverage is mostly found around Ulaanbaatar.

Friendshippeak.text: In the westmost part of Mongolia, there is some very remote coverage showcasing the tallest mountains in Mongolia where you can see glaciers and snow-capped peaks. This area also has a unique Street View car with a green or black bag above the right side roof racks.

Altanels.text: East of Uvs lake, you can find a lot of these small shrubs and patchy grass in a somewhat flat landscape. NOTE: Similar shrubs can be found around Shaazgai Lake, but that area is considerably more hilly.

Khankhokhiinationalpark.text: Khan Khokhii is a national park in northwestern Mongolia with some of the most dense forests in the country. It has partially cloudy skies, dark soil, and the western grey tent. Keep in mind that the trails in this park do not appear on the map. NOTE: There are other forests in Mongolia, but Khan Khokhii is one of the biggest and one of the only areas where you can be completely surrounded by trees.

Gobigurvansaikhan.text: The Gobi Gurvan Saikhan National Park, in the far south of Mongolia, features bright orange sand and sand dunes. There are two separate spots covered in the park: one in the middle just north of Sevrei, which has distant southern mountains, and the other in the far southwest corner of the park, which has a Jeep follow car.

Yolynamvalley.text: Yolyn Am Valley is located just west of Dalanzadgad and can be identified by the extremely foggy coverage, and having dark coloured soil and hills.

Khoridolsaridag.text: This beautiful river valley, just west of Lake Hatgal in the Khoridol Saridag mountains, is very recognizable from the surrounding rocky cliffs and forests, and the ground that is completely covered in pebbles.

Night.text: Mongolia has four main areas of nighttime coverage. Those areas are: Northwest of Murun Northwest of Murun West of Dashbalbar West of Dashbalbar South of Baruun-Urt South of Baruun-Urt East of Dariganga East of Dariganga All of these locations are driving towards town. Driving direction and car meta can help identify which area of nighttime coverage you are in.

Rainstormcov.text: East of the town of Khorgo there is a large stretch of road which was driven during a rainstorm. It features much darker skies, rain drops on the camera, and occasionally a rainbow can be seen.

ME.name: Montenegro
ME.key_meta: If you look up and see a "rift" in the sky, this glitch is most commonly found in Albania or Montenegro within Europe.

metas.title: Rifts
metas.description: If you look up and see a "rift" in the sky, this glitch is most commonly found in Albania or Montenegro within Europe. Most of the time, you will see it, but if you don’t, don’t rule out these countries.

metas.title: Mountainous Landscape
metas.description:
Montenegro is a small, mountainous country.
Inland mountains are lush and green, while most coastal mountains have distinct exposed, light coloured rock.
Most roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

Coverage.text: Coverage in Montenegro is limited to main roads, with very few minor roads covered. The only main road not covered is the A1, south of Kolasin.

Riftmap.text: This map shows the distribution of where rifts are found. Although rifts are common in Montenegro, coastal rounds will almost never have them. By the coast, there will be a short antenna with no rifts. There will be a long antenna with rifts inland. NOTE: An exception to this is the area around the coastal villages of Utjeha and Dobra Voda. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Northern.text: Green, agricultural valleys with deforested hills to make way for farmland are most commonly seen in the north.

Bay.text: The Bay of Kotor has a touristy and populated feel to it, with many people dressed in swimwear. A distinct steep, rocky ridge can also be seen.

Podgotuzi.text: Dry mountains with a lack of trees are seen around Podgorica, and to the south of it. Vineyards are also commonly seen in this region.

Pine.text: Pine forests can be found in the north and a small area north of Nikšić, but most commonly in the east.

Durmitor.text: Durmitor National Park can be recognized by a distinct landscape consisting of grassy, treeless mountains with a high-altitude feel. The town of Žabljak is situated in this national park, and can be recognized by the landscape but also by the unique architecture.

spotlight.text: Podgorica is the capital and largest city in Montenegro, and can be recognized by the modern buildings, wide roads and modern infrastructure.
These distinct staircase-like mountainsides can be seen in the Cemi River Valley.
Many small islands can be seen within Slansko Lake.
The Pljevlja Coal Mine can be recognized by the wide, artificial wall of gravel. The mine can often be seen from afar.
The Google Car can be seen chasing this police car on the P15, between Lovcen National Park and Čevo.
The southern part of the E80, between Orahovo and Đurmani, can be recognized by the yellow outer lines.
The Skadar Lake Bridge can be recognized by the railway and stone bollards next to the road.

NA.name: Namibia
NA.key_meta: Namibia is the newest African country with coverage featuring the white pickup truck.

metas.title: Pickup truck
metas.description: Namibia is the newest African country with coverage featuring the white pickup truck.
metas.comparison: The landscape is similar to Botswana—flat and dry. Roads typically have yellow outer lines, and driving is on the left side. Note: You may not always be on main roads with outer yellow lines. In such cases, it can resemble some parts of Kenya, which also drives on the left and sometimes features the white pickup truck.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: These stone bollards are found in Namibia. They have a small reflector on top and are usually located behind these red and white reflectors.

general_rules.text: Namibian area codes are a simple way to get the right region or city on urban rounds.

D-roads are grouped into four regions based on their first digit. Three-digit road numbers (e.g. D203) are found in the far south. As you move further north, you will encounter four-digit numbers beginning with 1, 2 and finally 3.

NP.name: Nepal
NP.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (1 regions covered).

Chir.text: Chir Pines, which can be identified from their generally smooth-looking conical or spherical crowns with very long needles, are found everywhere in the mountains, but are much more common in the west, and near Kathmandu. NOTE: The eastern region is generally greener than the west.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.key_meta: If you see yellow license plates on both the front and back in Europe with a super flat landscape, it’s likely the Netherlands.

metas.title: Yellow plates
metas.description: If you see yellow license plates on both the front and back in Europe with a super flat landscape, it’s likely the Netherlands. Luxembourg also uses all-yellow plates but is much hillier. Denmark may have yellow plates for commercial vehicles, so use other clues like architecture, bike lanes, and surroundings to confirm it’s the Netherlands.

metas.title: North - Very Large Roofs
metas.description: Farms in the north of the Netherlands often have very large roofs.

metas.title: Bulky Yellow Signposts
metas.description: Road signs on traffic islands often have these bulky yellow signposts.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Zeester
metas.description: Netherlands' guy has funny limbs, they shrink towards the end sorta like a starfish.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: The Netherlands has a simple, white or black bollard with a red and white reflector.

metas.title: Gen 4 Black Back
metas.description: Some Generation 4 coverage has a car blur glitch where the black back of the Google car is visible.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Yellow Plates
metas.description:
The Netherlands has long, yellow licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left.
Dutch taxis have blue plates.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Brick Roads
metas.description:
Brick roads are common in the Netherlands, both in rural and urban areas.
The brick pattern shown in the image is especially common.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Rumble Strips
metas.description:
Many rural roads feature a sort of brick rumble strip on the sides.
This is fairly unique to the Netherlands and a good way to identify the country in very rural rounds.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Row Houses
metas.description:
As mentioned before, row houses are very common in the Netherlands.
Almost half of the Dutch housing stock are row houses, significantly more than almost all other European countries.

metas.title: Flat Landscape
metas.description:
The Netherlands is extraordinarily flat.
In most of the country, you will get no more than a few metres of elevation.
Large swathes of the country are reclaimed land that is at or even below sea level.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Bicycle Paths
metas.description:
Many Dutch roads are flanked by bicycle paths.
Different designs exist, but a very common one is a reddish-pink lane.
Cycling is one of the most common modes of transportation in the Netherlands.
You will see cyclists and bicycles everywhere.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

general_rules.text: Dutch landline phone numbers start with a three- or four-digit area code. These are geographically grouped, except for the ones that start with 07, and two of the 02 codes. NOTE: Dutch mobile phone numbers start with 06, which is a code that is not used for any of the landline area codes. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Some road markers (“hectometre markers”) have province-specific designs. This only applies to markers for regional N-roads, which have road numbers in yellow boxes. Not all N-road markers have province-specific designs: some just have a generic design that can be found nationwide. The A-roads all have the same signs and are recognizable because the road number is in a red box. Bollards sometimes feature kilometre stickers, which are also limited to specific regions. You can click on the image to enlarge it. Image provided by Timzkii.

Noord-Brabant.text: All Dutch provinces have their own flag. However, most of these are very rarely seen in the wild. The major exceptions to this are the flags of Friesland and Noord-Brabant. In addition, you can sometimes see the unofficial but very popular flag of the Achterhoek cultural region in the east of Gelderland. For a full list of all provincial flags, you can view this Wikipedia page.

Friesland.text: In the province of Friesland, the Frisian language is commonly spoken. While Dutch language is still most prevalent on signs, a lot of town entry signs will feature bilingual town names. Some street names in Friesland uniquely end in -wei or -strjitte. NOTE: Frisian has vowels with circumflex diacritics (“little hats”): Â, Ê, Ô and Û. Dutch does not have these letters, except in loanwords. In addition, the Y is significantly more common compared to Dutch.

Limburg.text: This long, vertically arranged white sticker with three to four digits is found on street lights in Limburg.
While most of the Netherlands is very flat, Southern Limburg has some low hills.

North Brabant.text: Similarly to Limburg, North Brabant also has white stickers on their street lights, however it is horizontally arranged and only has one or two digits.

Flevoland.text: Almost all of the land belonging to the province of Flevoland was reclaimed from the sea in the mid-20th century. As a result, the province has a distinct, man-made look: extremely straight roads and large crop fields dominate the landscape. Wind turbines are common. In urban areas, there are no historical buildings. NOTE: The only exception to this description is the town of Urk, which is situated on a former island now surrounded by the rest of the province’s man-made polder landscape.

spotlight.text: Amsterdam street signs feature the city district in a smaller font size below the actual street name. NOTE: This design is very uncommon in the rest of the Netherlands.

Buildings in the Zaanstreek region just north of Amsterdam often feature wooden architectural elements, usually painted green or black; with white trims. They sometimes have tall roof spires, usually painted white.

The Afsluitdijk is a very recognizable man-made causeway between Noord-Holland and Friesland. It is a divided highway that runs in a very straight southwest to northeast direction. You can see water to your southeast, and a dike to your northwest. NOTE: There are other large causeways and dams in the Netherlands, but the Afsluitdijk is the biggest and has a very recognizable road direction.
In the Westland municipality, just southwest of The Hague, greenhouses are extremely common. They cover most of the municipality’s land surface.

The harbour of Rotterdam is one of the largest in the world. It extends all the way from downtown Rotterdam to the North Sea coast. If you see a lot of industrial activity, often in combination with large, round fuel storage tanks, there is a good chance that you are in this harbour area. NOTE: Amsterdam and Delfzijl also have large harbours. Both also feature a lot of fuel storage tanks.

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.key_meta: New Zealand has a unique white bollard with a red strip that wraps around the entire back and part of the front.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: New Zealand has a unique white bollard with a red strip that wraps around the entire back and part of the front.

metas.title: Give way sign
metas.description: Give-way signs in New Zealand have a white border and red text, while in Australia, give-way signs use black text.

metas.title: Timaru orange sticker
metas.description: Poles near Timaru often have a tall rectangle of orange paint on them with the text “DANGER LIVE WIRES”.

general_rules.text: New Zealand phone numbers are seven digits with a two-digit area code in front of it. Numbers starting with 02 are mobile numbers.
The first digit of Fonterra farm signs follows the regional pattern seen on the map. This image was provided by snowf_lake and brainy. You can click on the image to enlarge it.
While New Zealand flax can be found across the country, if you see them in long neat rows, you should consider Southland.

Poles with the middle insulator being installed on top of a tall metal bar are often found along the Auckland Waikato border, as well as in other parts of Waikato. NOTE: Insulators installed on significantly shorter vertical bars are rarer and can be found all across the country.

A long black vertical sticker with 6 digits with a small black square beneath it, is found on most of the North Island, in Southland and in Otago. On the North Island the first digit will be a 3 or a 4, while on the South Island it starts with an 8. NOTE: There is a similar regional black sticker with 6 digits but without a small square below it. Additionally, the sticker can rarely be white.

Similarly, a small white horizontal pole sticker with several numbers is found in several parts of the North Island. NOTE: The edges of the plate must be straight, meaning they cannot be rounded. Rounded plates are seen all across the country.

Marlborough.text: Most utility poles in the Marlborough region have a long square shaped olive-brown possum guard. These can appear alongside the usual shorter silver possum guards.
Vineyards are particularly common in the Marlborough and Hawke’s Bay regions. NOTE: Vineyards can be found throughout New Zealand, so be sure to check other clues as well.
Most utility poles in the Marlborough region have a long square shaped olive-brown possum guard. These can appear alongside the usual shorter silver possum guards.
Uneven crossbars, meaning they are off-centre, are found in Otago, Marlborough, Wellington and Taranaki.

Christchurch.text: The cities of Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch all have unique bus stop signs. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Several New Zealand cities have distinctive rubbish bins. The distinguishing feature of the bins are the council logos on the front. The colour of the bin lid varies within cities. NOTE: It is rare to find bins with green lids outside of Christchurch. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

North Island.text: The Waikato and Northland regions are characterised by their drier climate and rolling hills. In particular, the Northland region is quite hilly. NOTE: This type of landscape can be found in other parts of the North Island, but is more common in the mentioned regions.
Corn is almost exclusively found on the North Island.
Wooden fences with tightly packed fence posts are most common on the North Island and the north of the South Island, as well as on the Banks peninsula.

South Island.text: The West Coast and part of the Tasman region on the South Island can be recognized by its temperate rainforests and rugged landscape. This can be seen through the hundreds of tall hills and mountains, as well as the dark, compact greenery which is due to the area’s high level of rainfall.
The Southern Alps, a large, snowy mountain range, stretches throughout the majority of the South Island. Vegetation on the mountains becomes rarer the further south it is.
A yellow tag, similar in appearance to a cow-tag, is found on most poles in Gisborne. It is also found in a few spots on the South Island, as well as over the border in northern Hawke’s Bay.
Wooden fences with a big gap in-between them are most common on the South island as well as in Taranaki.
Fences with thin metal fence posts are almost exclusive to the South island.

Southland.text: The flatter parts of the Southland and Otago regions can be recognised by their cold climate and sloping, alpine hills. The vegetation in this area is often quite stunted due to the climate.
Many of the utility poles in Southland feature a long cylindrical silver possum guard. These are also more rarely found in western Otago.
Holey poles are found most commonly in Southland and around Auckland.
Square concrete poles without the usual indent are most common in Southland, but can also be found in Otago, Taranaki and Manawatū-Whanganui.
Similar wooden extensions, which are significantly longer, are mainly found in Southland and Hawke’s Bay, but can also be seen in Otago.

Taranaki.text: Bright sandy cliffs are a common sight in the central region of Manawatū-Whanganui. They may also be found in parts of Taranaki, Waikato and a road going into Hawke’s Bay. NOTE: Sometimes the cliffs may appear like sandy rocks.

Mount Taranaki, often referred to as Mount Egmont, is easily distinguished due to its relatively smooth slopes and its pointed, often snowy peak. It can frequently be identified from afar, as the surrounding area is flat.

Northland.text: Generation 2 coverage and gravel roads are particularly common in the Northland region. NOTE: These tips do not exclusively indicate Northland. Be sure to use other clues when making guesses.

Canterbury.text: Tall hedge and tree rows are particularly common in the Canterbury region. They are mostly found in the Canterbury plains, which comprises very flat, large fields. Due to Canterbury’s flat landscape, mountains can often be seen in the distance to the west. NOTE: Hedges that are even taller are common near Tauranga.
A typical bollard, but with a green stripe, is common in southern Canterbury, as well as in some pockets in eastern Southland.

Bay of Plenty.text: Very tall hedges are found in the Bay of Plenty, mainly around Tauranga. NOTE: Noticeably lower, but still tall, hedges are commonly found in Canterbury.

Some concrete poles in eastern Waikato and Whanganui city have white paint on the middle part of their wooden crossbars. This white painted crossbar can also be found in parts of western Bay of Plenty, Taranaki, Manawatū-Whanganui and eastern Wellington.

Auckland.text: A warning sticker attached to poles, which has a yellow danger triangle between two white rectangles, is found in Hawke’s Bay, from lake Taupo to lake Rotorua, in northern Waikato and south of Auckland city.

West Coast.text: A medium sized black vertical sticker with 5 digits is found in West Coast, Tasman, southern Canterbury and southern Northland.

Hawke's Bay.text: A small black horizontal pole sticker, with several numbers, is often found in Taranaki and Wellington. The sticker may rarely be found in parts of Manawatū-Whanganui, Waikato, and southern Hawke's Bay.

Gisborne.text: Solid outer white lines without middle lines are most common in Gisborne, but can also be found in northern Hawke's Bay and Wellington. NOTE: The roads in Wellington are typically narrower.
Short pieces of wood attached to a fence post, slightly extending it, can often be found on fences in Hawke’s Bay and occasionally in Manawatū-Whanganui and Gisborne.

Wellington.text: A typical bollard but with a black stripe instead of a red one is commonly found in Wellington, especially in older Generation 3 coverage.

spotlight.text: An easy way to recognize the city of Wellington is by how hilly it is.

In 2011, Christchurch was hit by an earthquake. As a result, roads on coverage from 2012 often appear in quite bad shape. Water damage caused many driveways to be cut off from streets due to large puddles of water, dirt or mud. Due to this reason, many residential houses in the city had to be removed, leading to several districts on newer coverage appearing like normal suburbs, but with almost no houses. This is noticeable when looking at where former driveways used to be.
Part of State Highway 85 in Otago has light snow coverage, specifically between the towns of Becks and Morisson.

Fruit farms covered in green netting are particularly common near Tauranga, but can also be seen near Gisborne. NOTE: Fruit farms are not fully exclusive to these regions, so make sure to consider other clues as well.

Banks peninsula, also sometimes called Akaroa, due to the town, is rocky with grassy hills, and small patches of trees. NOTE: This region can sometimes have gorse, which are also commonly found on the Otago peninsula.
The region of northern Marlborough, known as Marlborough Sounds, has densely forested mountains protruding from water. NOTE: Northern Marlborough is almost exclusively in Generation 4.

The Otago peninsula east of Dunedin is recognizable from its combination of plants such as cabbage trees, yellow flowered bushes, small groves of cone-shaped pine trees, and New Zealand flax. Additionally, the peninsula’s poles often have off-centre crossbars.

State Highway 80 in the Southern Alps is recognizable by its north-south orientation up a glacial valley. The west side of the road is lined with snow-capped mountains, while the east side of the road runs alongside the Tasman River and Lake Pukaki.
The volcano of Putauaki in eastern Bay of Plenty has a seemingly cut-off top which vaguely resembles the shape of a frog, with two big “eyes” protruding on either side of the top.

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.key_meta: In Nigeria, Street View coverage often includes a police escort car visible "behind" the Street View car.

metas.title: Police follow car
metas.description: In Nigeria, Street View coverage often includes a police escort car visible "behind" the Street View car. However, it may sometimes be missing, so don’t rule out Nigeria if you don’t see it.

metas.title: Steeply Pitched Roofs
metas.description:
Most Nigerian houses are single-storey, with steeply pitched roofs commonly made of metal sheets.
Cinder block walls surrounding the houses are also common.

Cvd28Vo.text: Nigeria is generally a fairly flat country with subtle elevation changes throughout. The south is relatively flat apart from some noticeable hills in the southeast, in Enugu state and in the southwest, between Ife and Lokoja. In the north, more prominent hills and mountains are found from Abuja and Jimeta. The largest mountains are found in the east, making up the Mandara mountain range and the Nigeria-Cameroon border. However, due to little coverage, the mountains are rarely visible.

Le4Uiwu.text: Shown is a Köppen climate map of Nigeria. The climate ranges from tropical rainforest in the far south, where you can find an abundance of palms with lush, green vegetation, to a more arid, savannah landscape in the centre, with more scattered trees. In the far north, it transitions to an arid steppe where the vegetation becomes even more sparse. NOTE: Due to dry/wet seasons, the coverage may look drastically greener/drier than expected for certain latitudes.

Coveragemap.text: Nigeria is a sparsely covered country, with very few roads in the northwest and east. Most of the coverage is centred around big cities and the highways that connect them. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Nigeria%20Gen%203.text: Knowing where you can find each generation is very useful. Notably, Generation 3 is not found north of Abuja. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Kqmqk8D.text: Generation 4 is not found in the northwest or far south. Shitcam is now found in most of Nigeria. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Wb24Taw.text: This map shows states with unique vehicle and tuk tuk colours. If a vehicle is shown, the state will have yellow tuk tuks. NOTE: There may be some rare exceptions to what is shown in the image. Paint jobs in-game may also differ slightly to those shown in the image. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

V97Cxfq.text: Nigeria is mainly Christian in the south, and Islamic in the north. As such, seeing women in hijabs and men in muslim attire is more common in the north.

Wx3Wlqr.text: These haystacks are extremely common and are almost exclusively found in Kaduna state.

Wnclirz.text: If you find yourself in an arid, but green, agricultural landscape with an abundance of corn around, you are likely to be in Kano state. It is only covered by shitcam, without any Generation 3 or 4.

Dqj6Bjw.text: Benue state can be recognized by the lush, green grass covered ground, with reddish soil. The vegetation is somewhat scattered, with the grass making way for taller trees. Shorter trees and shrubs between the grass and taller trees are somewhat uncommon. Thatched huts are also common in comparison to other southern states. NOTE: An abundance of palms should make you lean toward the bordering southern states that can look similar.

Qcnk9Jk.text: Niger state is the shitcam equivalent to Benue state. It is almost entirely covered by shitcam, and can be recognized by the scattered trees, reddish soil, and dry grass.

Fv0Bosj.text: The highways that run through the northwestern states of Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara, and Katsina can be recognized by an even more open and arid landscape compared to Niger state. The tree coverage becomes even more sparse, or there may not be trees at all. These states are entirely covered by shitcam.

Gmsg3W0.text: A savannah landscape combined with rocky hills can most commonly be seen in the northeast in the states of Plateau, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, and the north of Taraba. The hills in the far east and west of this region are typically greener and covered in more vegetation compared to the hills toward the middle of the range. NOTE: Around the city of Gombe, hills composed of softer, clay-like soil can be seen instead.

Undefined.text: These monolithic mountains with exposed, weathered rock are common in and around Abuja.

spotlight.text: A flat landscape with coastal vegetation and many palms can be seen east of Lekki. The ground is very sandy. Almost all of the coverage is old Generation 3, with a silver follow car.

The A121 can be recognized by the lush, tropical vegetation surrounding the divided highway, with a short, concrete median. Being a major highway, many vehicles, especially trucks, can be seen along it. NOTE: The A232 heading east of Benin City is also divided, however the median is noticeably wider than that of the A121.
The A3 going east of Potiskum to the Borno State border can be recognized by the Generation 4 coverage, mostly open arid landscape, and the highway being divided.
Dark red soil is most commonly found in and around Benin City and Enugu. NOTE: Red-tinged soil can be found in many places. This tip refers specifically to dark red soil.
The Obudu Plateau road can be recognized by having the tallest mountains in Nigeria with street view coverage. The road winds up lush, green mountains and the coverage is slightly foggy and wet.
This variant of shitcam with a distinct blue tint can be found in these areas.

This map shows where each old Generation 3 follow car can be found. They are uncommon, but can still be useful to know. NOTE: The A121 is not shown on the map as it is recognizable from other clues. This silver Lexus, not shown on the map, can rarely be seen on the highway between Onitsha and Enugu.

MK.name: North Macedonia
MK.key_meta: North Macedonia uses two types of bollards.

metas.title: Bollard
metas.description: North Macedonia uses two types of bollards. One is rounded and very thin, while the other one is wedge-shaped(looks like Croatia bollard). They both are white and have red or white reflectors, typically on a black surface.

metas.title: Dry Grasslands
metas.description: The general landscape of North Macedonia consists of relatively dry grasslands, and small hills and scattered trees.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

general_rules.text: You can sometimes see some smudges on the camera. If you see one black smudge on the camera, you will most likely be on the A3 between Bitola and Prilep, or the R1302 in the far east. Keep in mind smudges can be randomly seen throughout the country.

Coverage.text: Coverage is sparse, only including some highways and some cities in the country. The cities of Skopje, Bitola, Kumanovo, Prilep, Tetovo, Veles, Ohrid, and Strumica are the only ones with significant coverage inside the city. You can view the official coverage in more detail on this site.

Skopje.text: Skopje is the capital and by far the largest city. If you see any large apartments or buildings, you are almost guaranteed to be in Skopje.

Winter.text: Winter to late fall coverage is found in the cities of Skopje, Tetovo, Prilep, Bitola, and Ohrid.

Fyrom.text: A green truck is visible behind the Google Car for a portion of the E-65. The truck is visible from Kichevo to Arbinovo.

Veles.text: For some of the E-75 north of Veles, there are triple yellow lines with a dashed centre line. In the northern part of the road, there is a yellow-truck following the Google car. The rest of the road is either under construction or newly paved. This road is very similar to the A3 east of Veles, although that one is much flatter and has an arid landscape surrounding it.
A section of the A3 east of Veles also has triple yellow lines, which in Europe is extremely uncommon. The rest of the road has a very arid landscape and is noticeably under construction.

spotlight.text: If you see three smudges, you will always be on the R1304. The only large city on this road is Kočani, although it has extremely limited coverage.
If you see a brown smudge, you will be in the far southeast of the country.
A fly can be seen on the southern portion of the R1205. This is found nowhere else in the country.
If you see black and yellow striped kerbs, you are most likely to be in Strumica. They are rarely found in Skopje and if you see them around roundabouts, you will most likely be in Tetovo.
Ohrid is the only large city located next to a lake.
These long rectangular lamps are only found in the city of Prilep.
These two extremely rocky hills are visible in some parts of the city of Prilep.

MP.name: Northern Mariana Islands
MP.key_meta: The entire Google car is blurred, but an antenna at the front right can still be seen.

metas.title: Unique car
metas.description: The entire Google car is blurred, but an antenna at the front right can still be seen. It will feel noticeably closer to the car than in other countries with a similar car.
metas.comparison: You can confuse it with:
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner

Nmi.text: The only island with car coverage is the main island of Saipan. The islands north of that have no coverage. Tinian and Sinapalu south of Saipan only have tripod coverage.
Dense commercial areas can be found on the southern half of the west coast.

spotlight.text: The Suicide Cliff is a steep cliff with a lot of exposed rock near the northern tip of the island.

NO.name: Norway
NO.key_meta: In Norway, commercial plates are green.

metas.title: Green Plates
metas.description: In Norway, commercial plates are green. These can often be seen on vans or big trucks(not semi-trucks).
metas.comparison: NOTE: In Europe, green licence plates are almost unique to Norway, but can also be found on electric vehicles in Hungary and Romania.

metas.title: Long yellow-orange middle lines.
metas.description: Many larger roads in Norway have solid outer lines and yellow middle lines. The yellow lines have a distinct tinge of orange, making them easily recognizable.

metas.title: Long outer lines
metas.description: If you see long dashed outer lines, you'll know it's Norway. You can find similar dashed lines with the same climate in Sweden, but they will be half the length, and Finland uses full outer lines.
metas.comparison: (N)orway for normal, (S)weden for short, and (F)inland for full.

metas.title: Small Dot Roadlines
metas.description: Road lines will often be made up of small dots of paint.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Infrastructure - Bergen Hydrant
metas.description: You can find this specific design of green fire hydrants in Bergen.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Two Red Stripes
metas.description: Two red stripes going around lamp posts are commonly found in Stavanger.

metas.title: Vegetation - Bright Moss
metas.description: Brightly colored moss is common to find in the area between Lillehammer and Oppdal

metas.title: Norway
metas.description: 4 Zebra Stripes: Norway, Sweden, Bulgaria. > Bold, non-detailed person: only Norway.

metas.title: Landscape - Lofoten Mountains
metas.description: Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.

metas.title: Vegetation - Pine
metas.description: Pines are most common in coastal and far inland areas in the southern half of the country.

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description: Norway uses thin, curved rectangular bollards with the reflector inside of a black parallelogram.
from_maps: A Learnable Europe - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Architecture - Røros Architecture
metas.description: The old mining town of Røros can be recognised by the densely built traditional wooden architecture.

metas.title: Landscape - Exposed Rock
metas.description: Exposed rock, often spotted with small coastal pines and bushes, is mainly found on the south coast.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Wide Black ID
metas.description: Small, wide black pole plates, with a single line of letters and digits, can be found in southeastern Norway.

metas.title: Vegetation - Spruce
metas.description: Spruces are mainly found in the southern half of the country, particularly in the southeast and around Trondheim.

metas.title: Landscape - Atlanterhavsveien
metas.description: This road uses dark rocks as bridges. You will see water on both sides of the road. The coverage features dark clouds.
metas.comparison: The road includes the famous Storseisundet bridge.

metas.title: Landscape - Røst Island
metas.description: This island has only Gen 2 coverage. You will see lots of boats everywhere. The landscape is flat and islandish (duh).

metas.title: Infrastructure - Rusty Guardrail
metas.description: Rusty guardrails are almost exclusively found in coastal regions, and particularly on the southern half of the west coast.

metas.title: Landscape - Highlands
metas.description: Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.

metas.title: Landscape - E10, East of Narvik
metas.description: This road is very green and usually features big mountains with no trees. Right on the Swedish border you will find parts without trees.

metas.title: Language - Russian language
metas.description: Russian can sometimes be seen alongside Norwegian on signs near the Russian border. It is mostly found on roads E6 and E105 near Kirkenes.

metas.title: Landscape - Northern Coastal Grasslands
metas.description: Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.

metas.title: Landscape - Deep Fjords
metas.description: While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.

metas.title: Landscape - E10 on the border of Troms and Nordland
metas.description: This road runs through a valley. You can see a big mountain range along the road, with no trees on the mountain. Some sections are very green, and some section feature fireweed.

metas.title: South Coast - Full White Wooden Houses
metas.description: While completely white wooden houses can be found in the entire country, they’re especially common on the southern coast, where you’ll commonly see entire villages made up of them.

metas.title: Architecture - White House Village
metas.description: While completely white wooden houses can be found in the entire country, they're especially common on the southern coast, where you'll commonly see entire villages made up of them.

metas.title: Landscape - Lysevegen
metas.description: Lysevegen is a very windy and skinny road with 28 180° turns down the mountain. Notably, there are big power lines visible. You can see huge mountains in the distance. The coverage is very cloudy.

metas.title: Landscape - Northeastern Landscape
metas.description: The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.

metas.title: Landscape - End of the World Road
metas.description: This famous road can be identified by the lack of trees and the small white rocks. The visibility in the coverage is somewhat low. Some sections are very flat, while others can have small hills and lakes.

metas.title: Landscape - Russian Border Road
metas.description: Along the Russian border you can see this noticeably humid and green-looking road, with very overcast and occasionally foggy coverage. The trees are somewhat low and mainly consist of thin birches and pines.

metas.title: Landscape - Trollstigen
metas.description: Trollstigen leads down a huge mountain, and is surrounded by such. The road is very steep and windy. The rock is very dark and has green moss on it. Some sections are cut into the rock, with waterfalls appearing.

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description: Bollards in Norway are always completely black and white. They have a silver rectangular reflector on the front and two white dots on the back. The black stripe is slightly angled, and the bollards are narrow and flat.

metas.title: Landscape - Stavanger Farmlands
metas.description: The farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. The fields look vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.

metas.title: Landscape - E10 in Lofoten
metas.description: This road features huge mountains. It is a skinny road that has water to the east. Lots of sections have bridges or open tunnels. You will frequently find fireweed on the sides of the road. The vegetation on this road has a yellowish tone.

metas.title: Vegetation - Bracken
metas.description: This species of fern (Pteridium aquilinum, also known as bracken) which typically has a fairly tall stem and many wide leafs branching out, is mostly found in the south of Norway. Beware that other species of ferns can be found further north.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Big Wooden Snowpole
metas.description: Big wooden sticks are found on roads that are covered with snow almost the entire year. So far, they've been spotted on the road that runs north of Hardangervidda National Park, on the road west of Jotunheimen and southwest of Valdres Natur-og kulturpark.

metas.title: Landscape - 82 (Andoya)
metas.description: The 82 on the island of Andoya, which is part of the Lofoten archipelago, is flat apart from one tabletop looking hill. In generall, the hills on this road are quite unique and recognizable. You will find short scrubs along the road. Often, you will be able to see water.

metas.title: Language - Sámi Signs
metas.description: Bilingual signs with Sámi can be found in several northern areas in Norway. While the Sámi languages are very different from Norwegian, the best way to recognize them are the letters Á, Đ and the use of several vowels in a row, something which is uncommon in Norwegian. Note that not all signs in these areas will be bilingual.

general_rules.text: The first digit of Norwegian road numbers are region dependent. Note that there are some exceptions among single and two-digit roads. There are also a small number of roads beginning with a 9: Road 9, going north of Kristiansand, and a couple of two-digit roads in the far north. NOTE: Regional roads starting with “Fv” do not follow this pattern.

Innlandet.text: Bamboo snow poles are regional and can mostly be found in Innlandet, Akershus, Østfold, Buskerud and Vestfold but can also be found rarely in Trøndelag, Vestland, Agder, Telemark and Rogaland.
The road between Atna and Ringebu in Innlandet is completely covered in snow. You will find a winter wonderland with green rocks
Bamboo snowpoles are regional and can mostly be found in Innlandet, Akershus, Østfold, Buskerud and Vestfold but can also be found rarely in Trøndelag, Vestland, Agder, Telemark and Rogaland.

Black plastic snowpoles are more regional and will mostly be found in Trøndelag, Møre og Romsdal and Vestland, but can also be found in Nordland and more rarely in Innlandet, Buskerud, Rogaland and Telemark

Oslo.text: Fairly large black or red pole plates can be found in Oslo.
Maples are mainly found in the south, particularly by the farmlands around Oslo.

The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.
Maples are mainly found in the south, particularly by the farmlands around Oslo.

The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.

More.text: The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.
The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.

Similarly to the southeast, the farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. However, the fields look more vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.

Agder.text: This road between Aadneram and Nomeland in Agder features a thick 1m high snow along the skinny road. You will not find trees along this road.

Finnmark.text: Green plastic snowpoles are found mostly around the island of Senja in Troms since the company selling these is also located there. The company also sells other colors less frequently. These can also less commonly be found all over Troms and Finnmark.

Svalbard.text: Svalbard is an unincorporated archipelago within the Norwegian Kingdom. A separate Plonk It guide to Svalbard can be found here.

spotlight.text: Fairly large black or red pole plates can be found in Oslo.

OM.name: Oman
OM.key_meta: If you have a vibe that you are in Middle East and you see big white pickup truck with antenna in the middle you gonna be in Oman.

metas.title: Pickup car
metas.description: If you have a vibe that you are in Middle East and you see big white pickup truck with antenna in the middle you gonna be in Oman
metas.comparison: Note: Car might be sometimes fully blurred with visible antenna and sometimes  you can find similar pickup truck in UAE. Qatar pickup truck will have antenna in front left of the car.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Beginner
A Learnable Meta World - Google Cars - Basics

metas.title: Chevrons
metas.description: Oman uses black-and-yellow chevrons that have an unusually large number of arrows.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: License Plates
metas.description: Licence plates on private vehicles are generally yellow, while commercial vehicles have red plates.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Car
metas.description: All the coverage in Oman was taken with a white pickup truck, meaning you will either see most of the car or a large front blur.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

metas.title: Landscape
metas.description:
Most of Oman features a desert landscape with little vegetation.
While the middle and southern half is mostly flat, the north coast features dry mountains similar to those found in the UAE.
The southern coast also has mountains, though less dry.
from_maps: A Learnable North & West Asia - Identify Every Country

Landscape.text: Northern Oman features a dry mountainous landscape similar to eastern UAE. The south coast of Oman also rarely features some similar mountains.
Close to the southern coast, especially around Salalah, you will find a rolling hills landscape. The area commonly features rocky ground, bushes and small trees as well as some fairly green valleys.

South of Bidiyah you can find a couple of dirt roads going through a slightly rolling landscape consisting of orange-pink sand and small yellow-ish shrubs. The roads mainly go between long and low sand dunes with a general south-south-west direction.

Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. Road 51, which circulates the island, usually only has a white centre road line, which can help in recognising it. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

Mountains.text: The mountains north of Nizwa have an amount of green bushes that are unusually large for the north. The mountains are very rocky and jagged, which differentiates them from the more rolling mountains in the south.
Salalah is located on a flat coastal plain with rolling mountains surrounding it to the north.

Oman%20Red%20Dunes.text: Sandy dunes, that usually look quite red, are found near the border with Saudi Arabia and further inland in the middle of Oman.

Oman%20Pipes.text: Gas pipelines, often paralleling the road, are most common around Fahud, in Ad Dhahirah Governorate. But they can also be found in many pockets in central-southern Oman.

spotlight.text: The ridge east of Mirbat is similar to the Salalah ridge, but more pronounced, and the terrain just south of it is more rugged and hilly.
A prominent lone-standing mountain can be seen from afar just southeast of Nizwa. It is more wide than it is tall, and has a crown-like shape.

Just north of Adam, you’ll find a flat desert landscape with greyish soil and mountains in the distance, notably one long ridge to the south followed by two smaller and rounder hills to the east and southeast. Other mountains are also visible to the north and west.

In and close to Adam, the coverage is usually quite hazy, and the ridge and hills from the previous tip can be seen to the north. Though sometimes, only one or two are visible. Unlike north of Adam, you won’t see mountains in any other direction.
Oil drills are common around Amal and sometimes seen along Road 39. As well as northwest of Fahud, in Ad Dhahirah Governorate.
If you are surrounded by mountains on all sides, and you are in a somewhat urban area, you are likely just southeast of Muscat, in Al Amarat.
The bumpy and sloped ridge of hills combined with all the pipes and other oil related infrastructure makes the town of Fahud very distinct.

Musandam governorate has more in common with the UAE than most of Oman, due to the even drier mountainous landscape, and it often has an orange tone. Dipping beds, or mountains with diagonal layers, are common too. NOTE: Most of mainland Oman is dry but still has somewhat shrubby mountains.

PK.name: Pakistan
PK.key_meta: No country-wide identifier found — see Regional (20 regions covered).

Coverage.text: Coverage in Pakistan is extremely limited, only being found in Punjab around major temples and tourist attractions. Due to the number of distinct coverage spots, this section will only focus on the parts that are considered pinpointable.

Lahorecar.text: You may find this grey car, with a visible right side, driving around Lahore Fort in the north of Lahore. NOTE: This is considered hidden coverage, as it can not be accessed normally on Google Maps. It can however be accessed in the Map Making App and is still included in some community-made maps.

Lahoreurbantrekker.text: Just south of Lahore Fort you can find a trekker walking around some narrow urban streets that are typically very busy. NOTE: This is also hidden coverage.

Lahorefort.text: Lahore Fort is a large fortress in Lahore, with the Alamgiri Gate being one of the most iconic monuments in Pakistan.

Lahorefortroad.text: Inside Lahore Fort you may find this road completely surrounded by tall red brick walls on both sides.

Governmentcollege.text: The Government College University of Lahore can be recognised by its gothic architecture.

Patialablock.text: The Patiala Block of King Edward Medical University in Lahore is a large white colonial building with large white domes having black lines going around them.

Kinnairdcollege.text: Kinnaird College for Women University is mainly made up of traditional Pakistani red brick buildings, often combined with red brick paths.

Jallo.text: The coverage in Jallo, an eastern suburb of Lahore, can be recognised by the semi-urban coverage in a fairly poor-looking neighbourhood, with a very thick haze.

Bahriagrandhotel.text: Bahria Grand Hotel, in the southwestern suburbs of Lahore, can be recognised by the minigolf course in front of the hotel. There is also a statue of a cow by the entrance to the hotel grounds.

Harappa.text: West of Sahiwal, just northwest of Harappa, you can find a trekker starting in the south at Harappa Museum. This trekker can be recognised by most of the coverage being taken on a very narrow path made of concrete.

Hiranminar.text: Hiran Minar is a small temple, completely surrounded by a small lake with a single bridge connecting it to land, can be found just northwest of the city of Sheikhupura.

Hazrabababullehshah.text: The coverage around the shrine of Hazrat Baba Bulleh Shah, in western Kasur, can typically be recognised by the mosque with a large green dome, and two smaller green domes on top of the minarets. While the mosque itself isn’t visible from all of the coverage, the minarets can be seen from most spots.

Pakpattanmarket.text: In Pākpattan you can find a busy market street with a roof made of rugs. NOTE: Like the car coverage in Lahore, this, and the rest of the coverage in Pākpattan, is hidden coverage.

Pakpattanbusystreet.text: Just west of the market street in Pākpattan you can find a very busy-looking urban street.

Pakpattannarrowalley.text: You can also find this narrow alleyway in Pākpattan, just north of the market street.

Rohtasfort.text: Rohtas Fort, west of Jhelum, can typically be recognised by the almost black fortress walls. While the walls aren’t always nearby, they can usually be seen in the distance.

Katas.text: The coverage in Katas, north of Sargodha, can be recognised by the hazy sky combined with the hilliness.

Patriata.text: Patriata, northeast of Islamabad can be recognised by the hilly forests, mainly consisting of tall pine trees. Interestingly, parts of the coverage were taken from an aerial lift.

Changamanga.text: The coverage in Changa Manga Forest Park can be recognised by the path angle being northeastern, and the narrow channel closely following the path, either on the northern or southern side. To report inaccuracies, suggest new clues or give general feedback about our content, please use this form: https://www.plonkit.net/feedback

PA.name: Panama
PA.key_meta: The first digit of phone numbers can be used to regionguess Panama.

metas.title: Alto
metas.description: Panama, Guatemala, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta World - Stop Signs

metas.title: Spanish Influence
metas.description:
Panamanian architecture often reflects Spanish colonial influences, featuring vibrant colours, and some ornate detailing.
The most common type of building has painted concrete or sometimes brick walls with red metal sheets or tiles for a roof.
Many windows have bars on them for security.

general_rules.text: The first digit of phone numbers can be used to regionguess Panama. The numbers with a smaller font indicate potentially useful regional two-digit codes. NOTE: Only phone numbers with 7 digits are helpful, and any numbers starting with 5, 6, or 8 are useless as well.
The first digit of taxi and bus licence plates can be used to regionguess Panama. NOTE: Cars travel, so they are not always reliable, especially outside of cities.

PE.name: Peru
PE.key_meta: Signs with concrete blocks at the bottom are unique to Peru in South America.

metas.title: Concrete blocks
metas.description: Signs with concrete blocks at the bottom are unique to Peru in South America.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta Latin America - Beginner

metas.title: Electricity counter
metas.description: Peru's electricity meters are rectangular and have horizontal rectangular openings. They look kinda like post boxes.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta Latin America - Beginner

metas.title: Sign post
metas.description: Black-and-white signposts like this are only found in Peru in South America. (If the signpost is inside a city, take this rule with a grain of salt, as you can rarely find them in other countries.)
from_maps: A Learnable Meta Latin America - Beginner

metas.title: Black yellow stripes
metas.description: Black-and-yellow stripes on guardrails are common throughout Peru. Similar striped guardrails can also be found in Bolivia, but to differentiate them, check the outer stripe. Peru uses a black stripe, while Bolivia features a yellow one.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta Latin America - Beginner

metas.title: Infrastructure - Divided Highway
metas.description: Highway 1N/S is divided in the highlighted area on the map.
metas.comparison: NOTE: It is the only divided highway outside of cities.

metas.title: Diverse Architecture
metas.description: Here are a few examples of types of buildings commonly seen in Peru:

metas.title: Infrastructure - Pucallpa
metas.description: The east-central Amazonian city of Pucallpa, which lies close to the Brazil border, has a consistent street grid of WSW to ENE.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Some northern and eastern areas of the city feature grids of different orientation.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Cigarette Bollard
metas.description: This bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.

metas.title: Landscape - Lichen
metas.description: Patches of light green lichen can be seen covering rocks and growing on the ground in high elevation areas of central and southern Peru.

metas.title: Landscape - Titicaca Villages
metas.description: Low grass, a few hills, stone walls in villages and brown brick buildings are typical for the region south of Lake Titicaca in eastern Peru.

metas.title: Moquegua Bollard
metas.description: This cylindrical bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.

metas.title: Agriculture - Banana Plants
metas.description: Similarly to sugar cane plants, banana plants are generally found in agricultural regions adjacent to the coast in the northern half of the country.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Northern Tuk Tuks
metas.description: Tuk-Tuks with open front compartments are primarily found in the northern half of Peru, and are especially common in northern Amazonian adjacent regions.
metas.comparison: NOTE: This type of Tuk-Tuk can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.title: Landscape - North of Titicaca Wetness
metas.description: The coverage on the north side of Lake Titicaca was taken during a significantly wetter season than the coverage taken on the south side of Lake Titicaca.

metas.title: North - Overhanging Roofs
metas.description:
Buildings with overhanging roofs with wooden supports are mostly found in northern regions of Peru.
These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.

metas.title: Landscape - 5N (San Alejandro - Esperanza)
metas.description: Ruta 5N between the towns of San Alejandro and Esperanza is a relatively straight, flat road in good condition. This road primarily runs north-south through the rainforest.

metas.title: Landscape - Shrubby Mountains
metas.description: Far north Peru features mountains that are often covered in shrubby trees and bushes. Closer to the coast and the Ecuador border, these mountains are often quite dry in appearance.

metas.title: Landscape - Sandwiched Agriculture
metas.description: Coastal agricultural valleys in the middle and south are commonly sandwiched between dry mountains with no vegetation. The general orientation of these valleys are southwest-northeast.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Agricultural valleys in the north of Peru can look similar, but often feature more shrubs and trees on the mountains.

metas.title: Landscape - Northern Amazonian Landscape
metas.description: The areas adjacent to the northern Amazonian city of Tarapoto feature moderately tall foliage-covered mountains and can bear a similar resemblance to the hilly areas of Colombia or Brazil.

metas.title: Bollards
metas.description: Bollards in Peru are painted red or yellow, and the country mainly uses a variety of triangularshaped concrete bollards. Occasionally you will also spot other designs, such as these circular concrete variants.
metas.comparison: NOTE: These concrete variants can also be found in Bolivia and Brazil so do not rule out these countries if you find such bollards.

metas.title: Vegetation - Pine Plantations
metas.description: Pine plantations are typically found in higher elevation areas of the country, away from the coastal deserts and Amazonian Regions. The most common types of pine trees planted are Pinus radiata and Pinus patula.

metas.title: Landscape - 1S (Coastal)
metas.description: The 1S south of the city of Ica is not divided and mostly follows the coast. The soil is often red or orange in these areas, and there is little-to-no vegetation. This road is also entirely covered with the Generation 4 camera.

metas.title: Landscape - 28B
metas.description: Ruta 28B between the towns of Kimbiri and Echarate is a paved road with very faded or missing road lines. It is also characterised by being a relatively small road with Generation 4 coverage, which hugs the hillside and is located next to a river valley.

metas.title: Landscape - 30C
metas.description: Ruta 30C in eastern Peru uses a white Street View car in Generation 3 between the cities of Planchon and Iñapari. It features dense forest, few villages, and resembles interior areas of Brazil. Some of this area has been overwritten with Generation 4. Most of this segment runs north to south.

metas.title: Architecture - Titicaca Architecture
metas.description: As a general rule, the closer you are to Lake Titicaca in Peru, houses and buildings made out of red brick become more common. This type of architecture resembles the predominant type of building seen in parts of western Bolivia, which is helpful for remembering where it is seen most commonly. Additionally, buildings with blue tinted glass can be seen most commonly in the same areas.
metas.comparison: NOTE: Red brick buildings can be seen anywhere in the country, so use other clues before guessing.

Arequipa.text:
Volcanoes are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa.

NOTE: Within Peru, volcanoes are only found in the southeast in the highlighted area.

Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature barren and mostly flat desert landscapes that can resemble areas of northern Chile. You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.

Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature barren and mostly flat desert landscapes that can resemble areas of northern Chile. You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.

Tacna.text: Olive tree plantations can be found in the far southern region of Tacna.
The city of Tacna in the far south of Peru has this distinct dry ridge to the north.
This bollard is almost exclusive to Tacna region. It does spill into Moquegua but it is by far most common in Tacna.
Olive tree plantations can be found in the far southern region of Tacna.

Cusco.text: A train track covered by a trekker is located between Aguas Calientes and Cusco.
Within Peru, this white Street View car is found in central Cusco. It drives from the remote town of Aguas Calientes up to Machu Picchu.

Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature rocky and sharp mountain tops. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.

The southern city of Cusco is recognizable by its prevalence of both red brick and Spanish colonial style buildings. Cusco is surrounded by mountains on all sides and features an airport in the middle of the city. Due to its proximity and similar architecture, Cusco superficially resembles the Bolivian city of La Paz.

Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature rocky and sharp mountain tops. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.

Lima.text: These bollards are only found on the 1S highway between the towns of Ica and Lima.
This bollard is only found on the 1N highway north of Lima (still within Lima region).
Most of the boulevard-type streets in Peru are in the city of Lima. These boulevards are typically long, straight streets divided by concrete or a grassy berm.

Coconut palms (and other species of tall palms) can sometimes be seen in coastal areas of Peru, mainly north of Lima. They are mainly found in the agricultural areas which are typically found around the major coastal cities.

Coconut palms (and other species of tall palms) can sometimes be seen in coastal areas of Peru, mainly north of Lima. They are mainly found in the agricultural areas which are typically found around the major coastal cities.

Lamp posts in Lima and Lima Department often have a distinct, sweeping curve at the top, resembling an inverted "J" shape. NOTE: This design can occasionally be found in other parts of the country, such as Iquitos and Pucallpa. For other, more specific patterns, please see this document.

Puno.text:
A flat landscape in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

NOTE: This landscape might look similar to Bolivia. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

A flat landscape in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha. NOTE: This landscape might look similar to Bolivia. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

Iquitos.text: The road to Iquitos can be recognized by black car Gen 3, lack of center lines and rolling Amazonian landscape

Iquitos is a city in northeast Peru. It is an isolated city with only Generation 3 Street View coverage. Three-wheeled tuk-tuks, overcast skies, and rolling Amazonian landscapes are commonly seen in the area. This coverage is isolated from other areas of northern Peru.
Street View coverage in Peru is mostly located in the west and on main highways. There are some exceptions in the east near Iquitos and along the 30C. You can click on the image to enlarge it.

Tumbes.text:
These three landscapes are typically found along offroads in Tumbes. You will always see sandy soil with either green or withered bushes.

NOTE: In addition, Tumbes does not have black cars on off roads. Make sure to consider it whenever you see such landscapes with a white Street View car.

Piura.text: The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.

The landscape northwest of the city of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes.  The landscape is hilly, which distinguishes it from other Piura regions.
The country is generally flat in the east and mountainous in the west. However, an exception is the often flat desert near Piura in the northwest. You can click on the image to enlarge it.
The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.
Northwest of the city of Piura lies an area with similar vegetation to the area mentioned previously. However, this area is noticeably hillier.

Huancayo.text: The valley connecting the cities of Jauja and Huancayo features a flat plain with plentiful trees, agricultural areas, and small villages. North-south oriented mountains can be seen on both edges of the valley.

North of the city of Huancayo lies a shallow lake called Lake Chinchaycocha (also referred to as ‘the middle lake.’). This lake is generally marshy and a range of mountains can be seen to the east of the lake. This lake can look similar to Lake Titicaca, but is generally less densely populated and features fewer trees.

Lambayeque.text: The 1N near the Piura and Lambayeque border has a distinct looking landscape. It features a semidesert landscape and has overcast coverage in Generation 3. The new Generation 4 is drier but still looks somewhat similar.

Cajamarca.text: Dark red-tinted soil is found in several areas of Peru. Some notable areas include the areas near Cusco and Ayacucho in the south of the country, as well as areas near the northern cities of Cajamarca and Tarapoto. It can be found to a lesser extent in adjacent regions.

Dark red-tinted soil is found in several areas of Peru. Some notable areas include the areas near Cusco and Ayacucho in the south of the country, as well as areas near the northern cities of Cajamarca and Tarapoto. It can be found to a lesser extent in adjacent regions.

Ayacucho.text:
In higher elevation areas near the centre of the country, exposed rocky outcroppings are commonly seen in the sides of hills and mountains. Some areas with the highest concentrations are near Lago Chinchaycocha (Junin District) stretching south towards the city of Ayacucho.

NOTE: Exposed rocks can rarely be seen anywhere in the country, so use this meta with some caution.

Chiclayo.text: Most of the sugar cane production is found in the northern coastal regions of Peru near the cities of Chiclayo and Trujillo. Typically you see large fields of sugar cane in these areas. Smaller areas of sugar cane can be found further south in other valleys close to the Pacific coast.

Volcanoes are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa. NOTE: Within Peru, volcanoes are only found in the southeast in the highlighted area.
Most of the boulevard-type streets in Peru are in the city of Lima. These boulevards are typically long, straight streets divided by concrete or a grassy berm.

Iquitos is a city in northeast Peru. It is an isolated city with only Generation 3 Street View coverage. Three-wheeled tuk-tuks, overcast skies, and rolling Amazonian landscapes are commonly seen in the area. This coverage is isolated from other areas of northern Peru.

The southern city of Cusco is recognizable by its prevalence of both red brick and Spanish colonial style buildings. Cusco is surrounded by mountains on all sides and features an airport in the middle of the city. Due to its proximity and similar architecture, Cusco superficially resembles the Bolivian city of La Paz.
The city of Tacna in the far south of Peru has this distinct dry ridge to the north.
Within Peru, this white Street View car is found in central Cusco. It drives from the remote town of Aguas Calientes up to Machu Picchu.
A train track covered by a trekker is located between Aguas Calientes and Cusco.

metas.description: Tuktuks and Trikes are an extremely common sight in the Philippines. In many areas, they are more common than cars.

metas.title: Concrete roads
metas.description: If you're in Southeast Asia and see concrete roads, you're most likely in the Philippines, Thailand, or, much more rarely, Indonesia. If you're driving on the right side, it will be the Philippines, while driving on the left side indicates Thailand or Indonesia.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta South East Asia - Beginner

metas.title: Yellow and white lines
metas.description: Center lines in the Philippines can be white or a (usually slightly orange-tinted) yellow. The combination of the two colors, which you can also often get, is not really a thing anywhere else in Southeast Asia and as such is a good indicator for the Philippines.
from_maps: A Learnable Meta South East Asia - Beginner

metas.title: Vehicle - Low Roof Tuk-Tuk
metas.description: Low roof Tuk-Tuks are generally found in the North.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Trike - Square Roof
metas.description: These trikes with a square roof are also very common within Maguindanao.

metas.title: Car Meta - Taped Car back
metas.description: In northwestern Bohol you can find this Street View car with tape on the back.

metas.title: Vehicle - Palawan Tuk Tuk
metas.description: This Tuk-Tuk with a single front window and flat roof is exclusive to Palawan.

metas.title: Car Meta - Orange Car
metas.description: An orange Street View car with visible side mirrors can be found on Corregidor Island.

metas.title: Culture - Roman Soldiers
metas.description: Images and statues of ancient Roman soldiers can be found on the island of Marinduque.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Siquijor Lamp
metas.description: Lamp posts on Siquijor are typically painted yellow, with black stripes at the bottom.

metas.title: Car Meta - Mayon Vehicle
metas.description: This vehicle with several thick black bars can be found just south of the Mayon Volcano.

metas.title: Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.description: The majority of sugarcane in the Philippines can be found on the islands of Negros and Panay.

metas.title: Landscape - Arayat Volcano
metas.description: The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.

metas.title: Car Meta - General Santos Car
metas.description: You may find this black Street View car with a visible roof rack in and around the city of General Santos.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Northwest-Leyte & Biliran Insulator
metas.description: Three ridges plus a long extender at the top to carry the wire are most commonly found in Leyte and Biliran.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Trike - Sultan Kudarat
metas.description: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly.

metas.title: South - Diamond Pattern
metas.description: Houses built with amakan walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a diamond pattern are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.

metas.title: Landscape - Chocolate Hills
metas.description: On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have dark brown soil beneath the grass, earning them the name of Chocolate Hills.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Palawan Highway
metas.description: The highway going south from Puerto Princesa on Palawan can be characterised by being very wide, often featuring six lanes, while simultaneously having very little traffic.
metas.comparison: Along the road you will usually see this double electrical wire, which can help confirm your guess.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Bataan Death March
metas.description: These large decorated white waystones, commemorating the Bataan Death March, can be seen along roads going from Mariveles and Bagac in the south to San Fernando in the north.
metas.comparison: NOTE: The Bataan Death March continued from San Fernando to Capas by train, where a larger memorial has been built.

metas.title: Landscape - Mayon Volcano
metas.description: The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect smooth cone shape. Beware that it will very often be covered in clouds.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Double Pancake Insulator
metas.description: Double pancake insulators are very rare, but most likely to be found along the coast of East Samar, from about the height of the island of Hilabaan all the way down to the southern tip.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Yellow Backboards
metas.description: On the islands of Panay and Guimaras (the little island next to Iloilo), electricity counters are frequently mounted on yellow backboards. These can be horizontal or vertical, metal or wood.

metas.title: Palawan - Diagonal Woven Pattern
metas.description: Houses built with amakan walls (referred to as Sawali in the north) with a diagonally woven pattern are mostly found on the island of Palawan, but can also be found throughout the northern half of the country.

metas.title: Infrastructure - Acne Blocks
metas.description: The southern peninsula of Quezon has these sloped concrete blocks with round spots made from small rocks that kind of look like a skin issue. Blocks in this style with straight edges are common throughout the country, and you can get slanted concrete blocks without the acne in other places as well, but the combination is exclusive to this area.

general_rules.text: Landlines will start with a 0 followed by the area code. Mobile phone numbers start with 09.

Mindanao.text: Pineapple plantations are mostly found on Mindanao.
The vast majority of Oil palm plantations are found on Mindanao.

Banana plantations are almost exclusively found in central and southern Mindanao.

NOTE: Wild growing banana plants can be found all over the country, so make sure what you are seeing is an actual plantation before guessing.
While corn can be found in most of the country, it is most common on northern Luzon and on Mindanao.
While most of the Philippines is strongly christian, a region of western Mindanao is majority muslim.
In and around the city of Marawi, Mindanao you can find many destroyed houses and ruins from the Marawi siege in 2017.

These waystones with K and a number below show the distance related to Manila (or the max distances on specific islands)

This number can be used to narrow down guesses. For example, certain islands cannot exceed the orange numbers on the image.
As another example, Mindanao, and nowhere else, always has numbers above 1000.
Flat roofs are mostly found in the south. If it's a three-wheeler (as seen on the leftmost), you're probably on Mindanao.

The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat dry mountainsides and an abundance of pine trees. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.

Moluccan albizia are trees with light coloured trunks and pinnate leaves near the top of the tree. They are mainly found on Mindanao and are especially common in the eastern and central regions of the island.
